attributes.docstring_full: Add long-term validation material (a ``/DSS``) when the document is next saved. The certificates, CRLs and OCSP responses embedded in the document's signatures -- the ones already there and the ones :meth:`sign` makes before this call -- go into the document security store (ISO 32000-2 12.8.4.3), with whatever is given here: revocation data fetched separately is the usual case. It turns a PAdES-T signature into PAdES-LT. A store the document already has is extended. The store is written as an incremental revision, so every signature stays valid. Parameters ---------- certificates, crls, ocsp_responses : sequence DER bytes, or ``cryptography`` ``x509.Certificate``, ``x509.CertificateRevocationList`` and ``ocsp.OCSPResponse`` objects. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining.
attributes.signature: def add_ltv(self, *, certificates: Sequence[Any]=(), crls: Sequence[Any]=(), ocsp_responses: Sequence[Any]=()) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Add one or more pages from image files, bytes, or streams, one per image.
attributes.docstring_full: Add one or more pages from image files, bytes, or streams, one per image. Images are embedded as full-page images. Each source gets its own page, laid out according to the *layout* mode. Parameters ---------- image_sources : list of str, Path, bytes, bytearray, or BinaryIO Image file paths, raw image bytes, or file-like objects with a ``read()`` method (JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, WebP). layout : str, optional Layout strategy. Currently only ``"grid"`` is supported (default), which places one image per page filling the entire page. size : PageSize, (width, height), or str, optional Page size to use. If ``None`` (default), each page matches its image's natural size at *dpi*. dpi : float, optional Resolution to use when deriving page size from image pixels. Default is 72 DPI. fit : str, optional How to fit the image within each page. ``"cover"`` (default) scales the image to cover the entire page, cropping if necessary. ``"contain"`` scales the image to fit entirely within the page, preserving aspect ratio. ``"stretch"`` stretches the image to fill the page, potentially distorting it. Returns ------- list of int One-based page numbers of the newly added pages, in order. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If any image data is invalid or the size is malformed. Notes ----- JPEG and PNG work without optional dependencies. Static BMP, GIF, and WebP require the ``images`` extra. Animated GIFs are not supported. Examples -------- :: # Add several pages from image files page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_images( ["scan1.png", "scan2.png", "scan3.png"] ) # Add pages from image bytes with open("image.png", "rb") as f: page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_images([f.read()]) # Add pages from file-like objects (e.g., BytesIO) from io import BytesIO image_data = download_image_from_network() page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_images([BytesIO(image_data)]) # Add pages with explicit A4 size page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_images( ["img1.jpg", "img2.jpg"], size="A4" ) # Use fit mode to control image placement page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_images( ["img1.jpg", "img2.jpg"], fit="contain" )
attributes.signature: def add_pages_from_images(self, image_sources: list[str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO], layout: str='grid', *, size: PageSize | Sequence[float] | str | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, fit: str='cover') -> list[int]

attributes.docstring: Add one or more pages from PDF files, bytes, or streams, one per source.
attributes.docstring_full: Add one or more pages from PDF files, bytes, or streams, one per source. Each PDF source is opened and its first page is imported into the current document. The page's content, resources, annotations, and other properties are preserved during the import. Parameters ---------- pdf_sources : list of str, Path, bytes, bytearray, or BinaryIO PDF file paths, raw bytes, bytearrays, or file-like objects with a ``read()`` method. page_numbers : list of int, optional One-based page numbers to import from each source PDF. If ``None`` (default), page 1 is imported from each source. If a list, each element corresponds to the source at the same index. Returns ------- list of int One-based page numbers of the newly added pages, in order. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If any PDF data is invalid. FileNotFoundError If any PDF path does not exist. IndexError If any page number exceeds the number of pages in the corresponding source PDF, or if a negative page number is provided. TypeError If any source is not a supported type or a file-like object's ``read()`` method does not return bytes or bytearray. Notes ----- Each source PDF is loaded temporarily during the import and closed afterwards. The imported page retains its original properties: content, annotations, form fields, layers, and page boxes. Examples -------- :: # Add pages from multiple PDF files (page 1 from each) page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_pdf( ["document1.pdf", "document2.pdf", "document3.pdf"] ) # Add specific pages from each source page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_pdf( ["doc1.pdf", "doc2.pdf", "doc3.pdf"], page_numbers=[2, 1, 3] ) # Add pages from bytes with open("source.pdf", "rb") as f: page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_pdf([f.read()]) # Add pages from file-like objects (e.g., BytesIO) from io import BytesIO page_numbers = document.add_pages_from_pdf([BytesIO(pdf_bytes)])
attributes.signature: def add_pages_from_pdf(self, pdf_sources: list[str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO], page_numbers: list[int] | None=None) -> list[int]

attributes.docstring: Put *stamp* on *pages*, or on every page when none are named.
attributes.docstring_full: Put *stamp* on *pages*, or on every page when none are named. See :mod:`aspose_pdf.stamps`. A stamp whose drawing is the same on every page is written once and invoked from each of them, so stamping a long document does not repeat it; a :class:`~aspose_pdf.stamps.PageNumberStamp` says something different on each page and is written per page.
attributes.signature: def add_stamp(self, stamp: Stamp, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Put a contents page in front of the document, and return its pages.
attributes.docstring_full: Put a contents page in front of the document, and return its pages. Default entries use the same heading detection as :meth:`generate_outlines`, reading tagged structure or inferred size tiers. ``source="bookmarks"`` uses the existing bookmark tree. Each line shows a title, dot leaders, a page number and a clickable link. Heading links land at the heading's coordinates when available. Bookmark links fit the target page's width. Example:: with Document("report.pdf") as document: document.add_table_of_contents() document.save("report-with-contents.pdf") The **page numbers account for the contents itself**. Putting it at the front pushes every page it points at further back, so the numbers are worked out after the pages exist, not before; a heading on a page *before* *at* keeps the number it had. Where the document has page labels, the label is what is shown -- a contents that says ``12`` for a page the reader sees as ``xii`` is wrong in the only way that matters. Parameters ---------- source : str ``"headings"`` reads tagged or inferred headings by default. ``"bookmarks"`` lists existing local bookmark targets in tree order, indented by nesting level. It reads current named destinations and unsaved bookmark edits. Each entry links to its bookmark's page. External actions and unresolved targets are skipped, while their local children can still be listed within ``max_level``. title : str, optional The heading over the list. ``None`` writes none. max_level : int Ignore headings or bookmark levels deeper than this (1 to 6). prefer_structure : bool Read the structure tree when it has headings in it, as :meth:`generate_outlines` describes. Applies to ``source="headings"``. at : int Where the contents goes. ``1`` is in front of everything; ``2`` puts it after a cover page. size : PageSize, str or (width, height), optional The sheet to make it on. Defaults to the size of the page it goes in front of, so it matches the document it belongs to. margin : float Points of blank around the list. font_name : str One of the standard 14 fonts. title_size, entry_size, indent : float Point sizes for the title and the lines, and how far each level is indented past the one above. leader : str What fills the gap between a heading and its number. ``""`` leaves it blank. links : bool Make each line clickable. page_numbers : bool Show the page each heading is on. tag : bool Mark the lines as ``/TOCI`` in the structure tree (table 333). Off by default, since a document that is not otherwise tagged gains nothing from one tagged page. Returns ------- list[int] The one-based numbers of the inserted pages, in order. Empty when the selected source has no usable entries. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If a size or a measurement is one a page cannot have.
attributes.signature: def add_table_of_contents(self, *, title: str | None='Contents', max_level: int=3, prefer_structure: bool=True, source: str='headings', at: int=1, size: Any=None, margin: float=72.0, font_name: str='Helvetica', title_size: float=20.0, entry_size: float=11.0, indent: float=18.0, leader: str='.', links: bool=True, page_numbers: bool=True, tag: bool=False) -> list[int]

attributes.docstring: Append all pages from another document to this one.
attributes.docstring_full: Append all pages from another document to this one. This method provides a simple, intuitive way to concatenate PDF documents by appending all pages from the source document to the end of this document. The source document remains unchanged and can be used independently after the append operation. Parameters ---------- other : Document The document whose pages should be appended. Must be a valid Document instance that has not been disposed. Returns ------- Document This document (self), allowing for method chaining. Raises ------ TypeError If *other* is not a Document instance. PdfValidationException If *other* has been disposed or is otherwise invalid. Examples -------- Basic concatenation:: from aspose_pdf import Document with Document("first.pdf") as doc1: with Document("second.pdf") as doc2: doc1.append(doc2) doc1.save("combined.pdf") Method chaining:: with Document("main.pdf") as doc: for extra in ["append1.pdf", "append2.pdf", "append3.pdf"]: with Document(extra) as append_doc: doc.append(append_doc) doc.save("full_document.pdf") Notes ----- - All pages, resources, annotations, form fields, and bookmarks from the source document are imported. - The source document remains independent and can be disposed or reused. - Page numbers in the target document are updated to accommodate the newly appended pages.

attributes.docstring: Get the collection of attachments in the document.
The document's author, the ``/Info`` ``/Author`` entry, or ``None``.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's author, the ``/Info`` ``/Author`` entry, or ``None``. Assign text to set it, or ``None`` to remove the entry. The value lives in the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`).

attributes.docstring: Trim selected pages individually or apply one shared visible frame.
attributes.docstring_full: Trim selected pages individually or apply one shared visible frame. Return changed CropBoxes as detached ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` tuples keyed by original one-based page index, in first-selected order. ``None`` selects all pages; repeated indices count once. Empty documents, selections or plans return ``{}``. ``dry_run=True`` returns the same plan without writing any page boxes. By default each page follows :meth:`Page.auto_crop <aspose_pdf.pages.Page.auto_crop>`, with blank-looking and full-bleed pages left unchanged. ``uniform=True`` unions all detected ink bounds in displayed coordinates and applies that frame to every selected page, including blank ones. It requires exactly equal displayed CropBox dimensions in page user units, after rotation. Origins and rotations may differ. An entirely blank selection is left unchanged. All options, selections, page geometry and crop results are validated before any box is written. A failed render, parse or resource limit leaves all CropBoxes intact. Rendering follows get_content_bounds(): white paper, no antialiasing, optional visible annotations and the current rotation, layers and font substitution. Finite nonnegative ``margin`` adds padding, clamped to each page's current visible box. ``uniform`` and ``dry_run`` must be booleans. Pages render one at a time; streaming inputs read selected page content only. MediaBox, explicit production boxes, content, object coordinates, annotations and form values are preserved. Changes reach files only on explicit save. Cropping is a finite-resolution visual heuristic: tiny or faint marks can be missed, and scan borders count as content. Cropped-out data remains stored; this operation is not redaction.
attributes.signature: def auto_crop(self, margin: float=0.0, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, uniform: bool=False, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, include_annotations: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> dict[int, tuple[float, float, float, float]]

attributes.docstring: Make recognized web and email addresses in existing text clickable.
attributes.docstring_full: Make recognized web and email addresses in existing text clickable. Recognize HTTP(S), ``www.`` (using HTTPS), and common ASCII email addresses (using ``mailto:``). Surrounding prose punctuation is removed from targets. No network requests or text/content changes are made. ``pages`` selects one-based pages in order, including repeats. ``max_count=0`` considers all addresses; a positive cap includes unplaceable addresses and those overlapping existing links. The result reports new live ``annotations``, ``skipped_fragments`` without reliable geometry, and ``existing_fragments`` overlapping any existing Link rectangle. Repeated runs do not add overlapping links. Coordinates use axis-aligned text bounds; forms, unmeasurable fonts, ambiguous repetitions and wrapped addresses may remain unlinked. Selected streaming page content stays lazy. Validation precedes edits; errors on later pages can leave earlier pages' links in place.
attributes.signature: def auto_link(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, urls: bool=True, emails: bool=True, max_count: int=0) -> AutoLinkResult

attributes.docstring: Heuristically tag existing page content into the structure tree.
attributes.docstring_full: Heuristically tag existing page content into the structure tree. Each text object on every page becomes a ``/P`` (or ``/H1`` when its font size dominates) structure element, and each image XObject paint becomes a ``/Figure`` with ``/Alt``. Elements are wrapped in marked content and linked, in reading order, through ``/StructParents`` and the ``/StructTreeRoot`` ``/ParentTree``. Pages already carrying marked content are skipped. Parameters ---------- image_alt : str, callable, or None Alternate text for image figures: a fixed string, a callable mapping an image's resource name to its alt text, or ``None`` to leave images untagged (text only). Defaults to ``"Image"`` -- a placeholder that needs human review, since alt text cannot be inferred. Returns the number of structure elements created. This is a heuristic aid, not certified accessibility; review and refine its reading order, hierarchy, and alternate descriptions through :attr:`tagged_content`, and pair it with :meth:`convert_to_pdfua` for catalog prerequisites. Raises ------ AsposePdfException If the document is disposed, not loaded from a file/byte stream, or encrypted.
attributes.signature: def auto_tag(self, image_alt: str | Callable[[str], str] | None='Image') -> int

attributes.docstring: The catalog's ``/URI /Base`` for resolving relative URI actions.
attributes.docstring_full: The catalog's ``/URI /Base`` for resolving relative URI actions. Returns the declared ASCII string, or ``None`` when absent. Malformed dictionaries, references or non-ASCII strings raise ``PdfParseException``. Assign an absolute ASCII URI to set it, or ``None`` to remove it. Spaces and international characters must be percent-encoded. Stored spelling and trailing slashes are preserved; no address is fetched or checked online. Link inventories and reports apply the base to ``resolved_uri`` while retaining each action's raw ``uri``. Other URI dictionary entries and shared metadata are preserved. Page content is not decoded.

attributes.docstring: Return a new document imposed as a saddle-stitched booklet.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a new document imposed as a saddle-stitched booklet. Two pages to a sheet, in the order that reads correctly once the printed stack is folded down the middle: the last page beside the first, the second beside the second-last, and so on. The page count is padded to a multiple of four with blanks, because a folded sheet carries four pages whether they are all used or not. The sheet is twice the width of a page unless *page_size* says otherwise. Crop-mark options follow :meth:`n_up`: marks surround actual placed pages, while blank padding slots stay unmarked. They require enough margin and gutter space; no fold marks or bleed are generated.
attributes.signature: def booklet(self, *, page_size: Any=None, margin: float=0.0, gutter: float=0.0, crop_marks: bool=False, crop_mark_length: float=9.0, crop_mark_offset: float=3.0, crop_mark_width: float=0.5) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Change the document's passwords and keep everything else.
attributes.docstring_full: Change the document's passwords and keep everything else. *old_password* may be the user or the owner password. By default the new passwords guard the **same permissions with the same cipher** the document already had; only the passwords change. As with :meth:`encrypt`, an omitted *new_owner_password* makes the new user password the owner password too. A document with no protection gains one with :meth:`encrypt`'s defaults. Parameters ---------- permissions : int or Permissions, optional New access permissions -- ``Permissions.denying("print")`` and the rest. ``None``, the default, keeps the ones the document has, which is what makes this a password change rather than a re-protection. algorithm : str, optional A new cipher, as :meth:`encrypt` names them. ``None`` keeps the document's own. Raises ------ PdfSecurityException If *old_password* opens neither the user nor the owner side.
attributes.signature: def change_passwords(self, old_password: str, new_user_password: str, new_owner_password: str | None=None, *, permissions: int | Permissions | None=None, algorithm: str | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Check PDF integrity.
Alias of dispose (matches .NET ``Close``).
attributes.docstring_full: Alias of :meth:`dispose` (matches .NET ``Close``).

attributes.docstring: True if the document has been closed or disposed.
attributes.docstring_full: True if the document has been closed or disposed. A document that is closed cannot be used for further operations. This property follows the convention of built-in Python file objects. Examples -------- Using the property with a context manager:: with Document("file.pdf") as doc: print(doc.closed) # False # ... do work ... print(doc.closed) # True Checking before an operation:: doc = Document("file.pdf") if not doc.closed: print(doc.page_count)

attributes.docstring: Compare extracted page text and return detached per-pair reports.
attributes.docstring_full: Compare extracted page text and return detached per-pair reports. Select pages independently with one-based iterables; order and repeats are retained. ``None`` means all pages. Pages are paired by position, without automatic alignment. Unpaired pages have a missing index/text on the other side and never match, even against blank pages. Two empty selections return []. Selectors, flags and exclusions are validated first. Defaults compare exact extracted strings. ``ignore_whitespace=True`` collapses Unicode whitespace runs to a single space and strips leading and trailing whitespace; word boundaries remain significant. ``case_sensitive=False`` applies Unicode case folding. Extracted text remains unnormalized in each report; ``unified_diff`` describes the normalized text with three lines of context. Missing blank pages have headers alone. ``skip_artifacts=True`` omits explicitly marked Artifact text. ``exclude_regions`` removes glyphs overlapping any supplied rectangle from extracted report strings, matching and diffs, including untagged headers and footers. Rectangles are ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` in unrotated PDF points with a lower-left origin, independent of CropBox and page rotation, as in :meth:`Page.extract_text`. The same regions apply to every selected page on both sides. A bounded iterable is snapshotted before extraction; ``None`` and empty iterables preserve full-page extraction. Nonempty exclusions require reliable glyph geometry and omit an entire /ActualText replacement when any of its glyphs is excluded. Text without reliable geometry is omitted conservatively. Uses page text extraction, including hidden OCR text and its reading-order/font limitations. Images need an existing text layer; appearance, metadata, annotations and form values are not compared. CropBox and rotation do not clip or reorder extraction. This is not OCR or a semantic comparison and does not establish PDF equivalence. Extracts one pair at a time without filling full-document text/content caches. Reports retain original strings and diffs and survive document disposal. Shared work uses the stricter enabled source limits for pair count, string/diff UTF-8 sizes and cumulative retained report bytes; content decoding keeps each source's own limits. Line diff matching can be expensive for repetitive text; use page subsets for large inputs. Errors propagate without a partial list. Neither document is edited.
attributes.signature: def compare_text(self, other: Document, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, other_pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, ignore_whitespace: bool=False, skip_artifacts: bool=False, exclude_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None) -> list[PageTextComparison]

attributes.docstring: Compare rendered page pairs and optionally retain red difference images.
attributes.docstring_full: Compare rendered page pairs and optionally retain red difference images. ``other`` must be an open ``Document``. ``pages`` and ``other_pages`` independently select one-based page numbers in their respective documents; ``None`` means all pages on that side. Order and repetitions are kept. Selections are paired by position; a shorter side produces missing-page results with a ``None`` index and size. Two empty selections return []. Pages render on white paper at finite positive ``dpi``, without antialiasing, using each document's font substitution, CropBox, rotation and layer visibility. Visible annotations and form appearances count unless ``include_annotations=False``. Views align at the top-left without scaling, alignment correction, deskewing or page matching. A pixel changes when any RGB channel differs by more than ``tolerance`` (integer 0-255). Nonignored pixels covered by only one page always change. The difference ratio divides changed pixels by the union of page areas after removing ignored pixels. ``matches`` requires both pages, equal raster dimensions and a ratio at most ``max_diff_ratio`` (0-1). Default tolerances require exact rendered equality. Bounding boxes use top-left pixel coordinates with exclusive upper bounds; metadata and hidden content are not compared. ``ignore_regions`` is an iterable of ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` rectangles in PDF points (1/72 inch), measured right/down from the top-left of the displayed comparison canvas, after CropBox and rotation. The same rectangles apply to every pair and both sides; they are independent of DPI, not unrotated PDF user-space boxes. Finite real coordinates must enclose positive area. Negative/off-canvas bounds are clipped. Pixels touched by a region are ignored, rounding its bounds outward. Overlaps count once. Exclusions affect metrics, bounds and match status, and ``ignored_pixels`` reports their union within the page areas. An all- ignored pair has zero total/ratio and matches only if both pages exist with equal raster dimensions. Neither PDF's content is removed. ``include_diff_images=True`` attaches a ``RasterizedPage`` to every result: changes are red over pale grayscale context. Images enclose both views, with ignored areas in light blue and white padding outside both pages. Save them through ``result.diff_image.save(path)``. Without this flag, only metrics are retained. Reports and images outlive the source documents. Both selections, ignore regions, geometry and comparison canvas limits are checked before rendering. The stricter enabled resource limits apply to shared work and output images; retained images also share a cumulative ``max_raster_pixels`` allowance. Selected pages render one pair at a time; streaming content remains lazy. Errors propagate without partial results, and neither PDF is edited. Equality depends on the renderer's coverage and resolution; tiny differences or unsupported drawing may be missed, and different physical sizes can round to the same raster.
attributes.signature: def compare_visual(self, other: Document, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, other_pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, tolerance: int=0, max_diff_ratio: float=0.0, include_annotations: bool=True, include_diff_images: bool=False, ignore_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None) -> list[PageVisualComparison]

attributes.docstring: Compress uncompressed document streams.
attributes.docstring_full: Compress uncompressed document streams. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining.

attributes.docstring: Convert the document to PDF/A format in-place.
attributes.docstring_full: Convert the document to PDF/A format in-place. Removes prohibited content, injects an OutputIntents array with an sRGB ICC profile, adds an XMP metadata stream, and ensures the document title is set — bringing the document into conformance with the requested PDF/A level. A **Standard-14** font that the document does not embed is embedded from the bundled metric-compatible substitutes, since PDF/A requires every font embedded and those are the ones a converter can supply. Any *other* unembedded font is reported in the returned list instead: the program is not in the file and cannot be invented. Parameters ---------- level : str Target PDF/A conformance level (e.g. ``'1b'``, ``'2b'``, ``'3b'``, ``'4'``). Case-insensitive. PDF/A-4 is written against PDF 2.0, so the header version is raised to match. Returns ------- List[str] Remaining compliance issues that could not be fixed automatically (typically unembedded-font warnings). An empty list means the document is now fully compliant. Raises ------ AsposePdfException If the document is disposed, encrypted, or was not loaded from a file or byte stream.
attributes.signature: def convert_to_pdfa(self, level: str='1b', *, font_lookup_directory: str | Path | None=None) -> list[str]

attributes.docstring: Add the catalog-level PDF/UA prerequisites to the document in place.
attributes.docstring_full: Add the catalog-level PDF/UA prerequisites to the document in place. Creates the structural shell PDF/UA-1 requires at the catalog level — a ``/StructTreeRoot``, ``/MarkInfo /Marked true``, a document ``/Lang``, ``/ViewerPreferences /DisplayDocTitle true``, an ``/Info /Title``, and an XMP metadata stream declaring ``pdfuaid:part = 1`` — so that :meth:`validate_pdfua` passes. With ``auto_tag=True`` it also infers a real (if coarse) structure tree from the existing page text first (see :meth:`auto_tag`). This is still **not** certification-grade — images, alternate descriptions, and fine-grained reading order are not inferred — but it produces a tagged document rather than only a shell. Parameters ---------- language : str BCP 47 language tag for the catalog ``/Lang`` (default ``"en"``). title : str, optional Document title; falls back to an existing title or ``"Untitled"``. auto_tag : bool When ``True``, heuristically tag existing page text into the structure tree before building the shell (default ``False``). part : int ``1`` for ISO 14289-1 (the default) or ``2`` for ISO 14289-2, which also raises the header to PDF 2.0, adds an XMP ``pdfuaid:rev`` and declares the PDF 2.0 standard structure namespace. Returns ------- List[str] Remaining PDF/UA issues that could not be fixed automatically. An empty list means the catalog-level prerequisites are satisfied. Raises ------ AsposePdfException If the document is disposed, not loaded from a file/byte stream, or encrypted.
attributes.signature: def convert_to_pdfua(self, *, language: str='en', title: str | None=None, auto_tag: bool=False, part: int=1) -> list[str]

attributes.docstring: Convert the document toward a PDF/X standard in place.
attributes.docstring_full: Convert the document toward a PDF/X standard in place. Writes the identification the standard asks for in the place it asks for it, states the trapping status, gives every page a ``/TrimBox`` where it has neither trim nor art box, embeds the output intent, strips what the standard prohibits (additional actions, document JavaScript, XFA, and optional content for the parts built on PDF 1.4), and embeds the bundled substitutes for unembedded Standard-14 fonts. It will **not invent a printing condition**. The output intent is the promise a PDF/X file makes about the press it was made for, so where one is needed and neither *icc_profile* nor the document supplies it, the requirement stays in the returned list instead of a profile nobody chose being embedded. A standard that permits an RGB intent (PDF/X-3 and PDF/X-4) falls back to the bundled sRGB profile, which is a real registered characterization; PDF/X-1a admits no RGB intent, so converting to it needs a CMYK profile passed in. Colour is **not** converted either: a PDF/X-1a target with RGB content reports the RGB rather than guessing a separation for it, the way an unembeddable font is reported rather than substituted. Parameters ---------- standard : str Target conformance level; see :meth:`validate_pdfx`. icc_profile : bytes, bytearray, str or Path, optional The characterized printing condition, as ICC profile bytes or the path of an ``.icc``/``.icm`` file. output_condition_identifier : str, optional ``/OutputConditionIdentifier`` -- the registered name of that printing condition, such as ``"FOGRA39"``. Defaults to the profile's own ``desc`` tag, and failing that to ``"Custom"``. output_condition : str, optional ``/OutputCondition``, a human-readable note about the condition. registry_name : str ``/RegistryName``, where the identifier is registered. trapped : str or bool Written to ``/Trapped``. ``"Unknown"`` is refused: PDF/X exists so that the receiver does not have to guess. title : str, optional ``dc:title`` for the XMP packet. Defaults to the existing title. font_lookup_directory : str or Path, optional Searched for the programs of unembedded fonts before the bundled substitutes are tried. Returns ------- List[str] The conformance issues that remain. An empty list means the document now passes :meth:`validate_pdfx` for that standard. Raises ------ AsposePdfException If the document is disposed, was not loaded from a file or byte stream, or is encrypted (PDF/X prohibits encryption). PdfValidationException If *trapped* is not a yes-or-no answer. ValueError If *standard* is not a level this library knows.
attributes.signature: def convert_to_pdfx(self, standard: str='PDF/X-4', *, icc_profile: bytes | bytearray | str | Path | None=None, output_condition_identifier: str | None=None, output_condition: str | None=None, registry_name: str='http://www.color.org', trapped: str | bool='False', title: str | None=None, font_lookup_directory: str | Path | None=None) -> list[str]

attributes.docstring: The program that authored the document, the ``/Info`` ``/Creator``.
attributes.docstring_full: The program that authored the document, the ``/Info`` ``/Creator``. ``None`` when absent. Assign text to set it, or ``None`` to remove the entry. The value lives in the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`).

attributes.docstring: Remove the document's password protection.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove the document's password protection. This is the counterpart of :meth:`encrypt`: the next save writes a plain file. Opening an encrypted document already unlocks it for reading, and a re-save keeps the protection it came with -- taking the lock off is this explicit call. *password* must open the protection: the user or the owner password, whichever the document was opened with. Anything else raises :class:`~aspose_pdf.exceptions.PdfSecurityException` and leaves the protection in place. (A document certificate-protected in this session needs no password to take that protection off again.)

attributes.docstring: The document's named destinations, as a mapping of name to destination.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's named destinations, as a mapping of name to destination. ISO 32000-1 12.3.2.3: a place in the document under a name, which a link, a bookmark or another file can point at instead of naming a page and a view. Both places a PDF keeps them are read, and writing one name leaves every other entry in the file exactly as it was:: document.destinations["chapter-2"] = XYZDestination(page=7, top=760) page.add_link((72, 700, 200, 720), "chapter-2") See :class:`~aspose_pdf.destinations.NamedDestinationCollection`.

attributes.docstring: Release the document and underlying engine resources (primary lifecycle API).
attributes.docstring_full: Release the document and underlying engine resources (primary lifecycle API). ``subset_api.yaml`` maps .NET ``Dispose`` here; :meth:`close` is specified as an alias. Consistent with :class:`~aspose_pdf.engine.simple_pdf.SimplePdf` and facades, disposal is idempotent.

attributes.docstring: Embed a real font program for every font the document only names.
attributes.docstring_full: Embed a real font program for every font the document only names. A PDF may *refer* to a font without carrying it -- ``/BaseFont /Arial`` and nothing else -- and then it draws differently wherever Arial is different or absent. PDF/A, PDF/UA and PDF/X all forbid that, and no amount of rewriting fixes it, because the program simply is not in the file. This supplies it: each missing font is matched to a real face, and the face is written into the document, which carries it from then on:: report = document.embed_fonts() # bundled faces report = document.embed_fonts(directory="/fonts") # and a folder report = document.embed_fonts( sources=FontSubstitutionOptions.system() # and this machine ) With no arguments it supplies the **Standard-14** families, and Symbol and ZapfDingbats, from the bundled metric-compatible faces -- those need no font source and are the same on every machine. For anything else, name where the fonts are: a *directory*, a :class:`~aspose_pdf.font_substitution.FontSubstitutionOptions` with programs you hand over or the machine's own fonts, or neither, in which case the document's :attr:`font_substitution` is used. Faces are matched on what they *are* -- the family and style in their own ``name`` table, refined by the font's descriptor -- not on what their files are called. The document's own metrics stay: ``/Widths`` and ``/W`` are not replaced, so an embedded face changes which glyphs are drawn and never where they sit. That is deliberate -- it is the contract rendering substitution has always had, and what a viewer does with a font it does not have. It also means a face that is **not** metrically compatible with the one the document named shows as bad spacing, up to glyphs overlapping each other, rather than as reflowed text. Supply a face metrically close to the original, and check the result, before relying on this for a document whose look matters. Returns ------- List[str] One message per font it could **not** supply, saying why: no source answers to the name; the face's outlines are a kind that font cannot carry; the font is a ``CIDFontType0``, whose CIDs index its original program's own charset; or it is a composite font whose codes are not its CIDs -- anything but an Identity CMap -- so nothing says which character each CID stands for. An empty list means every font in the document now has a program. Call it before :meth:`convert_to_pdfa`, :meth:`convert_to_pdfua` or :meth:`convert_to_pdfx` to see what will be left over -- each of those does this pass itself. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If *sources* is not a ``FontSubstitutionOptions``, or both *sources* and *directory* are given.
attributes.signature: def embed_fonts(self, *, sources: FontSubstitutionOptions | None=None, directory: str | Path | None=None) -> list[str]

attributes.docstring: The document's embedded files as typed FileSpecification.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's embedded files as typed :class:`FileSpecification`. Each entry carries the decoded ``contents`` plus any MIME type, description and creation / modification dates stored with the attachment — read back from the ``/Filespec`` and ``/EmbeddedFile`` objects, or taken from metadata passed to :meth:`add_attachment` before the first save. Attachments added without metadata expose ``None`` for those fields. The list is ordered by name. This is the typed, read-only counterpart to :attr:`attachments` (a plain ``name -> bytes`` mapping, which stays writable).

attributes.docstring: Encrypt the PDF document with the standard security handler.
attributes.docstring_full: Encrypt the PDF document with the standard security handler. Parameters ---------- user_password : str Password required to open the document. owner_password : str, optional Password required to change security settings. Defaults to the user password if omitted. permissions : int or Permissions What a reader may then do, as a ``/P`` word (ISO 32000-1 Table 22). A raw signed integer still works; build one by name with :class:`~aspose_pdf.permissions.Permissions` -- ``Permissions.denying("copy")``, ``Permissions.allowing("print", "print_high_resolution")`` -- which keeps the reserved bits as the standard requires, where ORing the bit values together by hand clears them. Defaults to :meth:`Permissions.all` (``-4``), every permission granted. algorithm : str ``"AES-256"`` (the default, ``/V 5 /R 6``), ``"AES-128"`` (``/V 4 /R 4``, AESV2) or ``"RC4"`` (128-bit, ``/V 2 /R 3``). RC4 is offered for readers that predate AES and is weak; prefer a default AES-256 document. An unrecognised name raises :class:`~aspose_pdf.exceptions.PdfSecurityException` rather than quietly encrypting with a different cipher. Raises ------ PdfSecurityException If *algorithm* is not one of the supported names.
attributes.signature: def encrypt(self, user_password: str, owner_password: str | None=None, *, permissions: int=-4, algorithm: str='AES-256') -> Document

attributes.docstring: Encrypt for certificate *recipients* with the public-key handler.
attributes.docstring_full: Encrypt for certificate *recipients* with the public-key handler. Where :meth:`encrypt` gates the document behind a shared password, this gates it behind certificates: each recipient opens the file with the private key it already holds, and each one carries its own permissions. There is no user/owner split and no password to distribute. Parameters ---------- recipients: :class:`~aspose_pdf.Recipient` objects, or bare ``cryptography`` certificates, which then all receive *permissions*. At least one is required, and each needs an RSA or EC public key. algorithm: ``"AES-256"`` (the default, ``/V 5 /R 6``, ``/SubFilter adbe.pkcs7.s5``), ``"AES-128"`` or ``"RC4"`` (128-bit), the latter two ``/V 4 /R 4`` with ``adbe.pkcs7.s4``. permissions: Flags for recipients given as bare certificates. Defaults to granting everything; see :class:`~aspose_pdf.Recipient` for the bit layout, which is *not* quite the standard handler's ``/P``. The eight permissions :class:`~aspose_pdf.permissions.Permissions` names sit at the same bit positions in both words, so ``Permissions.denying("copy")`` means the same thing here -- the handler's own fixed bits are normalised on the way out, which is why the default is ``-1`` rather than :meth:`Permissions.all`. ignore_key_usage: Encrypt to a certificate whose ``keyUsage`` extension forbids RSA key transport or EC key agreement. Off by default, because a reader that enforces the extension would reject the result. Raises ------ PdfSecurityException If *recipients* is empty, a certificate cannot transport or agree a key, or *algorithm* is not a supported name.
attributes.signature: def encrypt_for_recipients(self, recipients: Sequence[Recipient | Any], *, algorithm: str='AES-256', permissions: int=ALL_PERMISSIONS, ignore_key_usage: bool=False) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Return a CSV review report with one row per selected annotation.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a CSV review report with one row per selected annotation. Filters and snapshot IDs match :meth:`export_annotations_json`, including popups/widgets by default. Columns are ``page_number`` (one-based), ``annotation_index`` (zero-based), ``id``, ``subtype``, ``author``, ``subject``, ``contents``, ``created``, ``modified``, ``in_reply_to``, ``popup`` and ``parent``. Dates retain their stored PDF spelling; absent text and references become empty cells. Reply and popup references keep source IDs even outside the selected rows. Empty selections produce a header-only report. CSV quoting preserves Unicode, double quotes, delimiters and embedded newlines, with CRLF records. ``encoding="utf-8-sig"`` adds a spreadsheet BOM; semicolon, tab and other valid single-character delimiters are supported. Metadata, cell text and encoded output obey resource limits. Page content, appearance streams, field values and embedded assets are not decoded or exported. All CSV is prepared before writing. Paths are replaced atomically, creating parent folders; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams receive bytes at their current position with short-write handling and remain open. The PDF is unchanged.
attributes.signature: def export_annotations_csv(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, subtypes: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, delimiter: str=',', encoding: str='utf-8', overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return UTF-8 JSON annotation metadata, optionally writing it.
attributes.docstring_full: Return UTF-8 JSON annotation metadata, optionally writing it. ``pages`` selects one-based page indices in the requested order; repeated indices are exported once. ``subtypes`` accepts a subtype string, ``AnnotationType`` or an iterable of either. ``None`` includes every annotation, including popups and form widgets; ``[]`` selects none. All selection arguments are validated before reading metadata. Schema version 2 contains an ``annotations`` array with source page and annotation indices, subtype, rectangle, text, author, selected PDF properties and reference IDs for replies/popups. Coordinates remain in unrotated PDF space and date strings retain their original format. IDs identify objects within this PDF snapshot, not across rewrites; links may name annotations outside the selected output. Supported review annotations can be appended to a PDF using :meth:`import_annotations_json`. This is not a lossless PDF backup. Appearance streams, actions, destinations, field values, embedded assets, custom properties and stream-valued rich text are omitted. Page content and appearance streams are not decoded. Files are written atomically, creating parent folders as needed; ``overwrite=False`` refuses an existing file. Binary streams are written from their current position, retrying short writes, and left open. The complete JSON is prepared before writing any output.
attributes.signature: def export_annotations_json(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, subtypes: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return UTF-8 XFDF review annotations, optionally writing the same bytes.
attributes.docstring_full: Return UTF-8 XFDF review annotations, optionally writing the same bytes. Page/subtype filters match :meth:`export_annotations_json`. Supported review types include notes, free text, line/shape/ink/text markup, stamps, carets and redaction annotations. Other types are skipped. Popups are nested under their selected owners; orphan or filtered-out popups are omitted. Reply links point only to selected annotations. Geometry stays in unrotated PDF coordinates. Common metadata, colors, basic borders and type-specific geometry are mapped to XFDF. Existing names are retained when unique, with deterministic fallback names for missing/duplicate names. Rich text, appearances, actions, field values, embedded assets and unsupported properties are omitted. This export does not apply redactions; supported review data can be restored with :meth:`import_annotations_xfdf`. XML characters and exported geometry are validated under resource limits. No page content, appearance or asset streams are decoded. Output is completed before writing. File replacement is atomic and ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing paths. Binary streams receive data at their current position, retry short writes and remain open; stream failures may leave a partial prefix. The source PDF is not edited.
attributes.signature: def export_annotations_xfdf(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, subtypes: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return annotation metadata as separate CSV files in a ZIP archive.
attributes.docstring_full: Return annotation metadata as separate CSV files in a ZIP archive. Names are ``annotations-page-0001.csv``, ``annotations-page-0002.csv``, etc., following the requested one-based page order (including repeats). ``None`` selects all pages; ``[]`` selects none. Filters and snapshot IDs match :meth:`export_annotations_json`, including popups/widgets by default. Selected pages are read one at a time without decoding page content or appearance streams. CSV follows :meth:`export_annotations_csv`: columns are ``page_number`` (one-based), ``annotation_index`` (zero-based), ``id``, ``subtype``, ``author``, ``subject``, ``contents``, ``created``, ``modified``, ``in_reply_to``, ``popup`` and ``parent``. Quoting preserves Unicode, double quotes, delimiters and embedded newlines with CRLF records. ``encoding="utf-8-sig"`` adds a spreadsheet BOM; semicolon, tab and other single-character delimiters are supported. ZIP uses ``'deflate'`` (level 0..9) or ``'stored'``, fixed timestamps and regular-file permissions. Empty results produce a valid empty ZIP or a manifest with no pages. Selection, entry counts, annotation counts, member bytes and cumulative CSV/manifest bytes obey :class:`PdfLoadLimits`. The archive is completed before output is touched. Paths are written atomically with parent directories created; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams retry short writes at their current position and remain open; write failures can leave partial output. The source PDF is not edited.
attributes.signature: def export_annotations_zip(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, subtypes: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, delimiter: str=',', encoding: str='utf-8', compression: str='deflate', compresslevel: int=6, include_manifest: bool=False, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return embedded-file payloads as ZIP bytes, optionally writing them.
attributes.docstring_full: Return embedded-file payloads as ZIP bytes, optionally writing them. ``names=None`` selects all document-level attachments sorted by their original names. A string selects one exact PDF attachment name; an iterable preserves selection order and includes repeated names once. Unknown names raise ``KeyError``. An empty selection produces a valid empty ZIP. File-attachment annotations are not included. ZIP members use flat basenames, with both slash styles removed. Unsafe characters and controls are replaced, leading/trailing dots and spaces removed, Windows device names prefixed, and UTF-8 names shortened to 240 bytes. Empty names become ``attachment``. Case-insensitive Unicode collisions receive ``_2``, ``_3``, etc. before the extension. Payloads are unchanged; no attachment is extracted to the filesystem. ``compression`` is ``"deflate"`` (default) or ``"stored"``; ``compresslevel`` is an integer from 0 to 9, ignored for stored output. Archive timestamps and permissions are fixed for deterministic output in the same runtime. ``include_manifest=True`` appends ``manifest.json`` with schema version 1 and original/archive names, sizes, MIME types, descriptions, dates as ISO 8601 strings or null, and relationships. The manifest name is reserved, so an attachment of that name is renamed. Selections, entries, text, per-file and cumulative payload sizes obey ``load_limits``. Manifest size is bounded by ``max_object_bytes``; archive growth by ``max_codec_work_bytes``. ZIP bytes are built in memory before any destination is written. Files are replaced atomically with parent directories created; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams are written at their current position, retry short writes and remain open. A stream failure can leave partial bytes. Neither the PDF nor its attachment mapping is changed; page content is not decoded, including on streaming documents. PDF attachment payloads are already loaded by the document's attachment reader.
attributes.signature: def export_attachments_zip(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, names: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, compression: str='deflate', compresslevel: int=6, include_manifest: bool=False, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return versioned UTF-8 block JSON, optionally writing a file or stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Return versioned UTF-8 block JSON, optionally writing a file or stream. Schema version 2 contains ``schema_version`` and a flat ``blocks`` list. Each entry is :meth:`ExtractedBlock.to_dict`: original ``page_index``, ``kind``, ``x``/``y`` anchor, ``text``, ``level``, ``items``, ``rows``, ``column_spans``, ``ordered``, ``alt`` and ``image``. Images are PNG data URIs when requested, otherwise null. Empty pages contribute no entries. Recognition and selection options match :meth:`extract_blocks`. The complete JSON is prepared before writing. Paths are written atomically, creating parent folders; ``overwrite=False`` refuses an existing path. Binary streams are written from their current position, retrying short writes, and left open. The returned bytes equal the written payload. Exporting never changes the source PDF.
attributes.signature: def export_blocks_json(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, include_images: bool=False, paragraph_gap: float | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True, skip_artifacts: bool=False, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Export simple bookmarks as level,title,page CSV for spreadsheet editing.
attributes.docstring_full: Export simple bookmarks as level,title,page CSV for spreadsheet editing. Rows use preorder, with one-based levels and page numbers. An empty page cell is a targetless heading. Only whole-page Fit destinations are supported; local GoTo Fit actions are normalized to direct targets. Names, other actions/views, styling and open state are refused rather than discarded. Use export_bookmarks_json for richer bookmarks. Read unsaved edits and current page identities without decoding page content. CSV uses standard quoting and CRLF records; utf-8-sig adds a BOM. Return bytes and optionally write a path atomically or a binary stream at its current position, retrying short writes and leaving it open. Output is prepared before writing and obeys load limits. overwrite=False refuses existing paths. The PDF remains unchanged.
attributes.signature: def export_bookmarks_csv(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, delimiter: str=',', encoding: str='utf-8', overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return version 1 UTF-8 JSON for the current bookmark tree.
attributes.docstring_full: Return version 1 UTF-8 JSON for the current bookmark tree. Preserve hierarchy/order, titles, bold/italic flags, RGB colour, open state and supported targets: all eight local views, named destinations, GoTo, URI, GoToR and Named actions. Local names resolve to explicit page views by default for transfer between documents. Set ``resolve_named_destinations=False`` to retain names and their PDF name/string representation; destination definitions are not archived. Read unsaved edits and current page identities without decoding page content. Unsupported/malformed targets, missing explicit pages and cycles are refused before output. Scripts, launches, custom action entries and Next chains are outside this exchange format. Return deterministic pretty-printed bytes with Unicode and a final newline. Optionally write a path atomically (creating parent folders), or write a binary stream from its current position and leave it open. ``overwrite=False`` refuses an existing file. Limits follow :attr:`load_limits`. This is not a complete PDF bookmark backup.
attributes.signature: def export_bookmarks_json(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, resolve_named_destinations: bool=True, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return an offline UTF-8 HTML comparison report, optionally writing it.
attributes.docstring_full: Return an offline UTF-8 HTML comparison report, optionally writing it. ``mode`` selects ``"both"``, ``"text"`` or ``"visual"`` comparisons. Page selections and settings follow :meth:`compare_text` and :meth:`compare_visual`. The report includes a page summary, per-pair metrics, text diffs and optional embedded PNG difference images. It needs no scripts, external assets or optional dependencies. Matching pairs are collapsed; differences and tolerated changes are expanded. Source text and labels are escaped. Both selections and all geometry are checked before rendering; one pair is processed at a time. Shared work, cumulative preview pixels and complete HTML bytes obey the stricter source resource limits. Neither document is edited. Output is prepared before writing. Files are replaced atomically; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing paths. Binary streams receive bytes at their current position, retry short writes and remain open. Stream failures may leave a partial prefix.
attributes.signature: def export_comparison_html(self, other: Document, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, other_pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, mode: str='both', dpi: float=72.0, tolerance: int=0, max_diff_ratio: float=0.0, include_annotations: bool=True, include_diff_images: bool=True, ignore_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, ignore_whitespace: bool=False, skip_artifacts: bool=False, title: str='PDF comparison', left_label: str='Original', right_label: str='Revised', overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return selected page image resources as ZIP bytes, optionally saving them.
attributes.docstring_full: Return selected page image resources as ZIP bytes, optionally saving them. ``pages`` uses one-based page numbers; ``None`` selects all pages. Selected order is retained, but repeated pages and shared image objects export once. Distinct image objects with identical pixels remain distinct. Page resources and nested Form resources are scanned without reading page/Form content. Unused, hidden and cropped-out resource images can be included; this is an asset inventory, not a visible-placement list. Inline images, annotation appearances, separate soft-mask streams and unattached legacy image mappings are not separately exported. Members have generated flat names ``image-0001.png``, etc., in selected page/resource-path order. JPEG and JPEG 2000 retain encoded payloads after decoding any outer filters; other supported samples become PNG. Original masks, placement transforms, clipping and PDF Decode effects on encoded JPEG/JPX files are not composited into those files. Rendering/OCR is not performed. Invalid image data or unsupported reconstruction propagates an exception instead of skipping an image. ``include_manifest=True`` appends a versioned ``manifest.json`` mapping files to one-based page indices and resource-name paths, with declared dimensions, sample depth, source filter, soft-mask presence and sizes. ``compression`` is ``"deflate"`` or ``"stored"``; ``compresslevel`` is an integer 0-9. ZIP metadata is fixed for deterministic output in the same runtime. Empty selections produce valid empty archives. Selection, graph traversal, image decoding, encoded files, manifest and archive growth obey resource limits. Images are reconstructed one at a time without populating the source image cache or extraction cursor. Streaming page content remains lazy. The archive is held in memory and fully built before writing a destination. File replacement is atomic; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams receive bytes at their current position, retry short writes and remain open; a stream failure can leave partial output. The source document is not edited.
attributes.signature: def export_images_zip(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, compression: str='deflate', compresslevel: int=6, include_manifest: bool=False, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return CSV with one row per inventoried link target or action.
attributes.docstring_full: Return CSV with one row per inventoried link target or action. Selection, ordering, scope and output handling match :meth:`export_links_json`. Columns include source ``page_number`` (one-based), ``annotation_index`` (zero-based), ``action_type``, ``action_path``, ``uri``, ``resolved_uri``, local ``target_page_number`` and ``remote_page_number`` (both one-based), ``destination_name``, ``destination_view``, ``destination_parameters``, ``file``, ``named_action``, rectangle ``x0,y0,x1,y1`` and ``issues``. Parameters and issues are JSON arrays within CSV cells. Other missing values are empty cells. Empty selections return a header-only report. Standard CSV quoting preserves delimiters, quotes, Unicode and newlines with CRLF records. ``encoding="utf-8-sig"`` adds a spreadsheet BOM. No optional dependencies are needed; the PDF is unchanged.
attributes.signature: def export_links_csv(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, delimiter: str=',', encoding: str='utf-8', overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return a versioned UTF-8 JSON link report, optionally writing it.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a versioned UTF-8 JSON link report, optionally writing it. Selection, ordering, diagnostic codes and scope match :meth:`extract_links`. Schema version 2 contains a ``links`` array with each inventory entry's fields and ``target_page_index``. Page indices are one-based. A destination is ``{page_index, view, parameters}``; its page index is remote for GoToR. Null parameters and invalid targets are retained without executable action payloads. No page content, images or appearances are decoded, and no links or files are opened. Metadata and encoded output obey ``load_limits``. All output is prepared before writing. Paths are replaced atomically, creating parent folders; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams are written at their current position with short-write handling and remain open. The PDF is unchanged.
attributes.signature: def export_links_json(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return individual page PDFs in a ZIP archive, optionally writing them.
attributes.docstring_full: Return individual page PDFs in a ZIP archive, optionally writing them. Each selected page becomes a single-page PDF file in the archive. Pages are named ``page-0001.pdf``, ``page-0002.pdf``, etc. in the order they are selected. An empty selection produces a valid empty ZIP. The ZIP uses flat basenames, with both slash styles removed. Unsafe characters are replaced before writing. Archive timestamps and permissions are fixed for deterministic output. ``compression`` is ``"deflate"`` (default) or ``"stored"``; ``compresslevel`` is an integer from 0 to 9. ``include_manifest=True`` appends ``manifest.json`` with schema version 1, a ``pages`` array, and for each entry: ``archive_name``, one-based ``page_index``, and ``size`` (ZIP entry byte count). Selection follows :meth:`extract_text`: one-based page indices, preserving order and repetitions. ``pages=None`` selects all pages; an empty iterable checks none. Options and page-count limits are checked before any page is read. Streaming inputs read selected pages one at a time without filling full-document caches. File output is staged beside the target and replaced atomically after success; failure leaves existing files intact. Parent folders are created as needed. ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing paths. Binary streams receive bytes at their current position, retry short writes and remain open; write failures can leave partial output. No full-document text string or complete encoded output is accumulated.
attributes.signature: def export_pages_as_zip(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, compression: str='deflate', compresslevel: int=6, include_manifest: bool=False, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return rendered page images in a ZIP, optionally saving the archive.
attributes.docstring_full: Return rendered page images in a ZIP, optionally saving the archive. ``pages`` uses one-based page numbers, retaining order and repeats; ``None`` selects all pages. Members are named ``page-0001.png``, etc., by output position. ``image_format`` is PNG, JPEG (also ``jpg``) or optional WebP. Rendering honors visible CropBox, rotation, layers and normal annotation appearances, unless ``include_annotations=False``. Color modes and encoding options follow :class:`RasterizedPage`; JPEG rejects bilevel. PNG/JPEG need no optional dependency; WebP requires the ``images`` extra. ``include_manifest=True`` appends versioned ``manifest.json`` with the source page index, pixel dimensions and encoded size for every file. ZIP compression is ``deflate`` or ``stored``, with level 0-9 and fixed timestamps/permissions. Empty selections produce valid empty archives. All options, selected geometry and planned raster budgets are checked before rendering. One raster is encoded at a time; the archive is held in memory and completed before writing. File replacement is atomic and ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams receive bytes at their current position, retry short writes and remain open; an I/O failure can leave partial stream output. Source PDF objects are not edited, and unselected streaming page content is not loaded. Rendering and encoding limitations remain those of the existing renderer/codecs.
attributes.signature: def export_pages_zip(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO | None=None, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, image_format: str='png', dpi: float=72.0, background: Sequence[int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, include_annotations: bool=True, mode: str='rgb', threshold: int=128, dither: bool=False, quality: int | float=85, lossless: bool=False, method: int=4, compression: str='deflate', compresslevel: int=6, include_manifest: bool=False, overwrite: bool=True) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Export matches as CSV with context and separate x0,y0,x1,y1 columns.
attributes.docstring_full: Export matches as CSV with context and separate x0,y0,x1,y1 columns. Standard quoting preserves newlines and quotes; records use CRLF. encoding="utf-8-sig" adds a spreadsheet BOM. Selection and output behavior follow export_search_json; the document remains unchanged.

Parts are named ``part-0001.pdf``, ``part-0002.pdf``, etc. in source page order; the last can be shorter. Paths are written atomically with parent directories created; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams retry short writes at their current position and remain open; write failures can leave partial stream output. The source is unchanged.

Paths are written atomically with parent directories created; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams retry short writes at their current position and remain open; write failures can leave partial stream output. The source PDF is not edited.

attributes.docstring: Return immutable layout blocks with original page indices and anchors.
attributes.docstring_full: Return immutable layout blocks with original page indices and anchors. Headings, paragraphs, lists and tables follow the same inferred reading order as HTML/Markdown. Table cells are not truncated. ``include_images`` adds figures with PNG bytes; otherwise figures and image decoding are omitted. No markup conversion, OCR or page rasterization is performed. ``pages`` accepts one-based page numbers, preserving order and repetitions. All options and indices are validated before decoding; streaming inputs read only selected pages and invoked forms. Empty selections return []. ``paragraph_gap`` is a finite positive baseline gap in font sizes, or None for the analyzer's default. ``clip_to_page`` filters anchors outside the effective CropBox. Anchors are in unrotated PDF coordinates, not bounding boxes. Snapshots survive source edits and disposal. ``skip_artifacts=True`` omits text in explicitly marked ``/Artifact`` sequences, including nested blocks and invoked forms. Untagged headers and footers are ordinary text; no positional heuristic is applied.
attributes.signature: def extract_blocks(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, include_images: bool=False, paragraph_gap: float | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True, skip_artifacts: bool=False) -> list[ExtractedBlock]

attributes.docstring: Extract all images from selected pages.
attributes.docstring_full: Extract all images from selected pages. Parameters ---------- pages : Iterable[int] | None One-based page indices to extract images from. ``None`` means all pages. Repeated selections are inspected once in first-selected order. Returns ------- list[Image] A list of :class:`Image` objects from all selected pages. Each object contains the raw image data, resource name, size in bytes, and detected format (e.g., "png", "jpg"). The list preserves page order: all images from page 1, then all from page 2, etc. Notes ----- The image bytes are the *decoded* sample bytes that the stream decoder produces, not the original encoded payload. To obtain the original bytes (e.g., a JPEG payload from a ``DCTDecode`` image), use the engine's :meth:`~aspose_pdf.engine.simple_pdf.SimplePdf.extract_images` directly.
attributes.signature: def extract_images(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None) -> list[Image]

attributes.docstring: Inventory Link annotation targets without executing or fetching them.
attributes.docstring_full: Inventory Link annotation targets without executing or fetching them. ``pages`` selects one-based source pages; None means all pages. Repeated selections are inspected once in first-selected order. Results follow annotation order, direct Dest before A, then action Next preorder. Every target/action has a detached immutable ``ExtractedLink`` with its source page, annotation index, normalized rectangle and action path. Reused targets and shared actions retain each occurrence. URI actions expose raw and base-resolved URLs; GoTo targets resolve named destinations and current local page identities into typed views. GoToR retains remote file/page/name metadata; Launch and SubmitForm expose common file specifications (UF before F), and Named retains its action name. Other action types retain their type without executable payloads. Invalid link geometry/targets/actions appear with issue codes rather than being silently skipped. Malformed annotation containers raise exceptions because their links cannot be inventoried reliably. Only Link annotations and their primary action chains are inspected, including hidden annotations. Bookmarks, AA actions, plain-text URLs, appearance streams, QuadPoints, platform-specific launch dictionaries, embedded-file GoToE targets and network reachability are not inspected. Rectangles use unrotated page user coordinates before cropping, with no UserUnit conversion. No content/image stream decoding, text extraction, filesystem lookup or network access occurs. Reads and result growth obey load_limits; the document remains unchanged.
attributes.signature: def extract_links(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None) -> list[ExtractedLink]

attributes.docstring: Return an independent document containing selected pages in order.
attributes.docstring_full: Return an independent document containing selected pages in order. *selection* is a one-based iterable of page numbers or a one-based range string such as ``"1-3,7,10-"``. String ranges include both endpoints and may descend (``"last-1"`` reverses all pages); an omitted end selects through the last page. ``odd`` and ``even`` select physical odd/even pages; ``last`` names the final page. Order and repeated pages are retained. Page resources, annotations, fields, layers, and bookmarks that belong to those pages travel with them. An empty selection is invalid.
attributes.signature: def extract_pages(self, selection: Iterable[int] | str) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Extract regular text grids as detached ExtractedTable values.
attributes.docstring_full: Extract regular text grids as detached :class:`ExtractedTable` values. ``pages`` contains one-based page numbers, in the requested order; repeats are retained and an empty iterable selects nothing. All indices must be integers within the document. Only selected pages are decoded. Tables follow the layout analyzer's reading order within each page; tables on different pages remain separate, including repeated headers. ``clip_to_page`` leaves out text anchored outside the effective crop box by default. The HTML/Markdown export's geometric heuristics apply: no OCR, border analysis, tag-tree reconstruction or multiline/vertical merge recovery is performed. Whitespace is normalized but cell text is not truncated. Use ``table.to_list()``, ``table.to_csv()`` or ``table.save_csv(path)`` to consume each result. ``skip_artifacts=True`` omits text in explicitly marked ``/Artifact`` sequences, including nested blocks and invoked forms. Untagged headers and footers are ordinary text; no positional heuristic is applied.
attributes.signature: def extract_tables(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True, skip_artifacts: bool=False) -> list[ExtractedTable]

attributes.docstring: The text of all or selected pages, separated by one line break.
attributes.docstring_full: The text of all or selected pages, separated by one line break. ``pages`` is an iterable of one-based integer indices, preserving its order and repetitions. ``None`` selects every page; an empty iterable returns an empty string. Invalid indices are rejected before any page is read. Streaming documents decode only the selected page content. Each page's own line breaks are kept; see :meth:`Page.extract_text`. ``clip=(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` applies the same unrotated PDF-coordinate rectangle to each selected page, selecting overlapping glyph bounds. ``exclude_regions`` omits glyphs overlapping any of its rectangles in the same coordinates, including untagged headers, footers or sidebars. It combines with ``clip``; exclusions take priority. ``None`` or an empty iterable leaves ordinary extraction unchanged. Geometry must be reliable, and complete code units/ligatures are retained or omitted. A logical /ActualText span is omitted whole if any underlying glyph is excluded. See :meth:`Page.extract_text` for limits and gap handling. Empty pages retain their separators, and a subset or region does not replace the cached full-document text. ``skip_artifacts=True`` omits text in explicitly marked ``/Artifact`` sequences, including nested blocks and invoked forms. Untagged headers and footers are ordinary text; no positional heuristic is applied.
attributes.signature: def extract_text(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, skip_artifacts: bool=False, exclude_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None) -> str

attributes.docstring: Return detached positioned words from selected pages in content order.
attributes.docstring_full: Return detached positioned words from selected pages in content order. Results contain ``text``, one-based ``page_index``, ``rect`` (also ``bbox``) and ``quad``. Coordinates are PDF points in unrotated user space, independent of CropBox and page rotation. Bounds use font advances, ascent and descent rather than visible glyph ink. Words are non-whitespace sequences within a measured text run. Adjacent show operands and font changes can form one word; line/run, marked-content and Form XObject boundaries separate words. Punctuation stays attached; no language-specific segmentation or reading-order reconstruction is performed. Hidden layers are omitted. Invisible OCR text counts, and ``skip_artifacts=True`` omits marked artifacts. ``clip`` selects whole words whose axis-aligned rectangles overlap the region, retaining their full text and bounds. It does not crop words or implicitly intersect the page boxes. Unknown/unmeasurable runs and logical /ActualText replacement spans are omitted rather than assigned invented coordinates. Images and widget values are not OCRed. ``pages`` preserves order and repetitions; all indices and options are validated before content is decoded. Streaming inputs read selected page streams and invoked forms, without filling full-document caches or decoding images and unused forms. Resource limits propagate without a partial result. Results survive source edits and disposal.
attributes.signature: def extract_words(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, skip_artifacts: bool=False) -> list[TextWord]

attributes.docstring: Find visually blank pages without changing this document.
attributes.docstring_full: Find visually blank pages without changing this document. Return one-based page numbers in the selected order, ignoring repeats. ``pages=None`` checks all pages; an empty iterable checks none. All indices and options are validated before rendering. Streaming inputs read only selected pages, and each raster is released before the next. Detection uses :meth:`Page.is_blank <aspose_pdf.pages.Page.is_blank>`: at the chosen DPI, a pixel counts as ink if any RGB channel is below ``white_threshold``; an ink fraction at most ``max_ink_ratio`` is blank. Defaults are 72 DPI, threshold 250, zero tolerated ink, with visible annotations included. The renderer's limitations and finite resolution apply; hidden text or data may still exist on a blank-looking page. Rendering errors and resource limits propagate without a partial list.
attributes.signature: def find_blank_pages(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, max_ink_ratio: float=0.0, include_annotations: bool=True) -> list[int]

attributes.docstring: Find groups of pages with identical rendered views without editing them.
attributes.docstring_full: Find groups of pages with identical rendered views without editing them. Each group contains at least two distinct one-based page indices, including the first occurrence. Groups and their members follow first occurrence in the selection. ``pages=None`` selects all pages; explicit indices are validated in full and deduplicated before rendering. Fewer than two distinct pages returns ``[]`` without rendering. Pages match when their raster dimensions and every RGB pixel match at ``dpi`` on white paper, with antialiasing disabled. CropBox, rotation, layer visibility and font substitution follow :meth:`Page.render <aspose_pdf.pages.Page.render>`. Visible annotations and form appearances count unless ``include_annotations=False``. No text extraction or OCR is required. DPI must be finite and positive; flags must be booleans. SHA-256 selects candidates, and a new render of a group's first page confirms pixel equality. At most two completed rasters are held at once, with compact fingerprints for earlier pages. Streaming inputs read only selected pages without filling all-page content caches; candidate verification can read and render reference pages again. Rendering errors and resource limits propagate without a partial list. Equality is specific to this renderer and resolution. Tiny differences may be missed; different physical sizes can round to the same raster dimensions. Scan noise, color changes and other visible pixel changes remain differences. There is no fuzzy matching, rescaling, automatic rotation alignment or margin removal. Hidden text, form values and other stored data may differ even when the visible pages match.
attributes.signature: def find_duplicate_pages(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, include_annotations: bool=True) -> list[list[int]]

attributes.docstring: Find image placements whose effective DPI is below ``min_dpi``.
attributes.docstring_full: Find image placements whose effective DPI is below ``min_dpi``. The finite, positive threshold applies to either image axis; equality passes. ``pages`` contains one-based page numbers, retaining order and repeats; None scans all pages. Each image paint produces its own immutable ``ImageResolutionIssue``, in page/content order, even when the same image or form is reused at different sizes. Image XObjects, inline images and invoked nested forms are inspected. DPI uses declared pixel dimensions, composed transforms and page UserUnit, including rotation, reflection and shear. Singular transforms have no painted area and are skipped. Findings locate full images in unrotated page user coordinates. Clipping, crop boxes, opacity, optional content visibility and overlap are not evaluated; hidden or off-page paints may be reported. Unused resources, annotation appearances, patterns, Type 3 glyph content and separate mask images are not scanned. This is a resolution check, not a sharpness or print certification check: already blurry or upscaled images can have sufficient DPI. No image pixels are decoded and no optional imaging dependency is required. Only selected page content and invoked forms are read, under resource limits, without modifying the source or extraction cursors. Malformed geometry, missing invoked resources and cyclic form calls raise exceptions rather than silently omitting findings.
attributes.signature: def find_low_resolution_images(self, min_dpi: float=150, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None) -> list[ImageResolutionIssue]
