attributes.docstring: Find image placements below multiple DPI thresholds in a single scan.
attributes.docstring_full: Find image placements below multiple DPI thresholds in a single scan. This is a batch version of :meth:`find_low_resolution_images`. It performs the same resolution check for each threshold but returns results grouped by threshold in a dictionary. Use this when you need to know which images are below multiple DPI thresholds without scanning the document multiple times. Parameters ---------- thresholds A mapping of minimum DPI thresholds to names. Each key is a finite, positive DPI threshold; each value is an identifier used in the result dictionary. pages One-based page numbers to inspect, or None for all pages. Repeated selections are inspected once in first-selected order. Returns ------- dict[float, list[ImageResolutionIssue]] A dictionary mapping each threshold to its list of issues, in page order. Empty lists for thresholds with no matches. See Also -------- find_low_resolution_images : Check images against a single threshold. find_texts : Find text for multiple patterns in one pass. Examples -------- Check images against multiple DPI thresholds: >>> results = document.find_low_resolution_images_batch( ... {75: "very_low", 150: "low", 300: "good"} ... ) >>> # results is {75: [...], 150: [...], 300: [...]} >>> # where results[75] includes images below 75 DPI >>> # and results[150] includes images below 150 DPI but >= 75 DPI Limit to specific pages: >>> results = document.find_low_resolution_images_batch( ... {150: "low"}, ... pages=[1, 2, 3] ... )
attributes.signature: def find_low_resolution_images_batch(self, thresholds: Mapping[float, str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None) -> dict[float, list[ImageResolutionIssue]]

attributes.docstring: Return matched text strings without context or geometry.
attributes.docstring_full: Return matched text strings without context or geometry. This is a lightweight companion to :meth:`search_text`. It performs the same pattern matching but returns only the matched substrings, one per hit, in document order. Use this when you only need to know *what* matched and not where or how it appeared. Strings are literal unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds Python's IGNORECASE semantics. Literal occurrences may overlap; regex matches follow ``re.finditer``. Zero-length matches are omitted. Empty patterns are rejected. One-based ``pages`` preserves order and repeats. All options/selections are checked before extraction. Only selected pages are read, without filling document-wide text/content caches. Search follows ordinary text extraction, including hidden-layer filtering and logical replacements; it does not OCR images or search annotation/form values. Results obey load limits and survive source edits/disposal without changing the PDF. Args: pattern: Text or regex pattern to search for. pages: One-based page numbers, or None for all pages. regex: Treat pattern as a regular expression (default: False). case_sensitive: Match case exactly (default: True). Returns: List of matched text strings in page order. Empty list if none. Example: >>> matches = document.find_text("Invoice") # returns ["Invoice", "Invoice", ...] >>> # Same as search_text but without extra metadata >>> exact_matches = [m.text for m in document.search_text("Invoice")]
attributes.signature: def find_text(self, pattern: str | re.Pattern[str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True) -> list[str]

attributes.docstring: Return matched text strings for multiple patterns without context or geometry.
attributes.docstring_full: Return matched text strings for multiple patterns without context or geometry. This is a batch version of :meth:`find_text`. It performs the same pattern matching for each pattern but returns only the matched substrings for each pattern in a dictionary. Use this when you need to know *what* matched for each pattern without the overhead of context or geometry. The search is efficient: the document is scanned only once, and results are collected for all patterns in a single pass. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are ignored and present only to allow clear labeling in the caller's code. The result dictionary preserves the key order from the input mapping. Strings are literal unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds Python's IGNORECASE semantics. Literal occurrences may overlap; regex matches follow ``re.finditer``. Zero-length matches are omitted. Empty patterns are rejected. One-based ``pages`` preserves order and repeats. All options/selections are checked before extraction. Only selected pages are read, without filling document-wide text/content caches. Search follows ordinary text extraction, including hidden-layer filtering and logical replacements; it does not OCR images or search annotation/form values. Results obey load limits and survive source edits/disposal without changing the PDF. Args: patterns: A mapping of search patterns to names. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are labels used in the result. pages: One-based page numbers, or None for all pages. regex: Treat all string patterns as regular expressions (default: False). case_sensitive: Match case exactly (default: True). Returns: A dictionary mapping each pattern key to a list of matched text strings in page order. Empty lists for patterns with no matches. Example: >>> results = document.find_texts({"Old": "old_name", "New": "new_name"}) >>> # results is {"Old": ["Old", "Old"], "New": ["New"]} >>> import re >>> results = document.find_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): "year", re.compile(r"\d{2}"): "number"}, ... regex=True ... )
attributes.signature: def find_texts(self, patterns: Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True) -> dict

attributes.docstring: Bake selected form fields and annotations into static page content.
attributes.docstring_full: Bake selected form fields and annotations into static page content. By default both are flattened. Set ``annotations=False`` for fields only, ``fields=False`` for non-widget annotations only, or pass fully qualified terminal field names in ``fields``. ``pages`` contains one-based page numbers; omitted means all pages. Duplicate selections are ignored. Unknown field names raise ``KeyError`` unless ``strict=False``; invalid selections are rejected before modifying the document. Missing supported appearances are generated only for selected objects. Hidden/NoView objects and objects without a usable normal appearance or rectangle are retained, preserving viewing and printing semantics. A field with widgets on other pages stays editable there. Unselected appearances and the AcroForm's ``NeedAppearances`` flag are preserved. An unsafe page graphics state raises ``PdfValidationException``. If a later page fails, completed pages stay flattened and form collections are refreshed; the failing page's annotations are retained. The whole operation is not transactional. This does not execute JavaScript or flatten XFA forms.
attributes.signature: def flatten(self, *, fields: bool | Iterable[str]=True, annotations: bool=True, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, strict: bool=True) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Resolve optional content once and for all; return pages changed.
attributes.docstring_full: Resolve optional content once and for all; return pages changed. Switching a layer off changes what is *drawn*; the content stays in the file and comes back the moment someone switches it on again. That is right for a viewer and wrong for handing the document to somebody -- a hidden draft watermark or an alternate-language layer is still in there. Flattening deletes what the current configuration hides (marked content, XObject invocations and annotations alike), drops every surviving ``/OC`` reference and removes ``/OCProperties``, leaving an ordinary PDF that shows exactly what was visible. Returns the number of pages whose content changed. A document without optional content is left alone and returns ``0``.

Font sources the renderer may substitute non-embedded fonts from. ``None`` (the default) keeps rendering to the bundled substitute faces, which cover the Standard 14 plus Symbol and ZapfDingbats. Assign a :class:`~aspose_pdf.font_substitution.FontSubstitutionOptions` to let the renderer also draw with fonts from directories you name, programs you supply, or the machine's installed fonts:: document.font_substitution = FontSubstitutionOptions.system() The setting applies to every render path on the document -- including :meth:`save_page_as_image` and :meth:`save_as_tiff` -- and a single options object keeps its font index across pages.

attributes.docstring: Every font this document draws with, one entry each.
attributes.docstring_full: Every font this document draws with, one entry each. The other font APIs answer what is available to *draw* with -- :class:`~aspose_pdf.font_repository.FontRepository` the machine's fonts, :attr:`font_substitution` the ones you have made available. This answers what the document itself uses:: for font in document.fonts: print(font) # Arial (TrueType, embedded TrueType) on pages 1, 2 # Helvetica (Type1, not embedded) on pages 2, 3 missing = [f for f in document.fonts if not f.embedded] weight = sum(f.program_bytes or 0 for f in document.fonts) Each :class:`~aspose_pdf.document_fonts.DocumentFont` says what the font is called, what kind it is, how it is encoded, whether the program is in the file and what it costs, whether the name carries a subset tag, whether the text can be extracted (``has_to_unicode``), and which pages use it. The fonts found are the ones used **for rendering**, by the same walk the PDF/A, PDF/UA and PDF/X checks use -- so a font reached only through a form's default resources or an annotation's appearance is listed too, with no page but a *location* saying where it came from. Fonts that say the same thing are one entry: a document that writes its own ``/Helv`` dictionary on every page uses one font, not twenty. Two *subsets* of one family stay separate, since they carry different glyphs. Reading this does not change the document, and the list is a snapshot -- take it again after embedding fonts or adding pages.

attributes.docstring: Get the interactive form of the document.
Free memory by clearing caches.
Create a document from PDF bytes.
attributes.docstring_full: Create a document from PDF bytes. This is a convenience class method that creates an empty document and loads it from bytes in one step. It is equivalent to:: doc = Document(limits=limits) doc.load_from(data, password=password, ...) but is more concise and follows Python's convention for alternative constructors. Parameters ---------- data : Raw PDF bytes, a bytearray, or any readable binary stream (e.g. ``BytesIO``, an open file handle in ``"rb"`` mode). password : Optional password for standard encrypted PDFs. certificate, private_key : Optional recipient credentials for an ``/Adobe.PubSec`` PDF. key_encryption_key : Optional pre-shared AES key for a CMS KEK recipient. limits : Optional resource policy for untrusted input. Returns ------- Document A document loaded from the provided bytes. Raises ------ ValueError If *data* is not valid PDF data. TypeError If *data* is not bytes, bytearray, or a binary stream. PdfSecurityException If the PDF is encrypted and *password* is missing or incorrect. Examples -------- :: # Load from bytes with open("document.pdf", "rb") as f: doc = Document.from_bytes(f.read()) # Load from BytesIO from io import BytesIO pdf_bytes = download_pdf_from_api() doc = Document.from_bytes(BytesIO(pdf_bytes)) # Load from a file-like object with Document.from_bytes(my_stream) as doc: print(f"Pages: {len(doc)}") Notes ----- The document must be closed with :meth:`dispose` or a context manager when you are finished with it, just like documents loaded from files.
attributes.signature: def from_bytes(cls, data: bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, password: str | None=None, certificate: Any=None, private_key: Any=None, key_encryption_key: bytes | bytearray | None=None, limits: PdfLoadLimits | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Create a document from a PDF file path.
attributes.docstring_full: Create a document from a PDF file path. This is a convenience class method that creates an empty document and loads it from a file in one step. It is equivalent to:: doc = Document(limits=limits) doc.load_from(path, password=password, ...) but is more concise and follows Python's convention for alternative constructors. Parameters ---------- path : File system path to the PDF. password : Optional password for standard encrypted PDFs. certificate, private_key : Optional recipient credentials for an ``/Adobe.PubSec`` PDF. key_encryption_key : Optional pre-shared AES key for a CMS KEK recipient. limits : Optional resource policy for untrusted input. Returns ------- Document A document loaded from the file. Raises ------ FileNotFoundError If *path* does not exist. ValueError If the file is not valid PDF data. PdfSecurityException If the PDF is encrypted and *password* is missing or incorrect. Examples -------- :: # Load from a file doc = Document.from_file("report.pdf") # Load with password doc = Document.from_file("secure.pdf", password="secret") # Use as a context manager with Document.from_file("document.pdf") as doc: print(f"Pages: {len(doc)}")
attributes.signature: def from_file(cls, path: str | Path, *, password: str | None=None, certificate: Any=None, private_key: Any=None, key_encryption_key: bytes | bytearray | None=None, limits: PdfLoadLimits | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Create a document from a binary stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Create a document from a binary stream. This is a convenience class method that creates an empty document and loads it from a stream in one step. It is equivalent to:: doc = Document(limits=limits) doc.load_from(stream, password=password, ...) but is more concise and follows Python's convention for alternative constructors. The stream is read to EOF and is **not** closed afterwards. Parameters ---------- stream : Any readable binary stream (e.g. ``BytesIO``, an open file handle in ``"rb"`` mode). password : Optional password for standard encrypted PDFs. certificate, private_key : Optional recipient credentials for an ``/Adobe.PubSec`` PDF. key_encryption_key : Optional pre-shared AES key for a CMS KEK recipient. limits : Optional resource policy for untrusted input. Returns ------- Document A document loaded from the stream. Raises ------ ValueError If the stream does not contain valid PDF data. TypeError If *stream* is not a binary stream. Examples -------- :: # Load from BytesIO from io import BytesIO pdf_bytes = download_pdf_from_api() doc = Document.from_stream(BytesIO(pdf_bytes)) # Load from an open file with open("document.pdf", "rb") as f: doc = Document.from_stream(f) # Use as a context manager with Document.from_stream(my_stream) as doc: print(f"Pages: {len(doc)}")
attributes.signature: def from_stream(cls, stream: BinaryIO, *, password: str | None=None, certificate: Any=None, private_key: Any=None, key_encryption_key: bytes | bytearray | None=None, limits: PdfLoadLimits | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Synthesise missing annotation appearance streams across all pages.
attributes.docstring_full: Synthesise missing annotation appearance streams across all pages. Builds an ``/AP /N`` appearance from the geometry and colours of every supported shape / text-markup annotation that lacks one (``Square``, ``Circle``, ``Line``, ``Polygon``, ``PolyLine``, ``Ink``, ``Highlight``, ``Underline``, ``StrikeOut``, ``Squiggly``). Returns the number created; existing appearances are preserved unless *force* is given.

attributes.docstring: Regenerate AcroForm field appearance streams from their values.
attributes.docstring_full: Regenerate AcroForm field appearance streams from their values. Builds the variable-text appearance (``/AP /N``) of each text and choice field from its value and default appearance (``/DA``) so the value renders without relying on ``/NeedAppearances``, and points each check box / radio widget's ``/AS`` at the state matching its value. Missing caption-only push-button appearances are also generated. Returns the number of widgets updated. With *keep_existing*, existing normal appearances of text, choice and signature widgets are preserved while missing ones are built. Call after setting field values; :meth:`flatten` does this automatically.

attributes.docstring: Build a bookmark tree from the document's headings.
attributes.docstring_full: Build a bookmark tree from the document's headings. A **tagged** document has already been told what its headings are: the structure tree names them ``/H1``..``/H6``, or ``/H`` with the section nesting giving the level, and that is the author's own answer. An untagged one is read with the same size-tier analysis :meth:`to_markdown` and :meth:`auto_tag` use -- a heuristic, so the headings it finds are the ones those would find, and no better. Each bookmark lands on the heading itself, not on the top of its page: a heading's place comes from the marked-content sequence it owns, or from the block's own anchor, and is written as an ``/XYZ`` destination. A heading whose place cannot be told -- a structure element whose content is not on its own page -- gets the page alone. Levels nest, skips included: an ``H3`` after an ``H1`` with no ``H2`` between them becomes a child of the ``H1`` rather than a sibling. Parameters ---------- max_level : int Ignore headings deeper than this (1 to 6). prefer_structure : bool Read the structure tree when it has headings in it. ``False`` reads the pages whatever the tree says, which is what a document whose tagging is only a shell wants. replace : bool Clear the existing bookmarks first, which is what *generate* means. ``False`` appends to them. open_to_level : int Write bookmarks up to this level **unfolded**, so a reader shows their children. ``0``, the default, leaves every one folded, as a bookmark tree is written unless asked otherwise. zoom : float, optional The magnification each bookmark asks for. ``None`` keeps whatever the reader is already using, which is what a reader expects of a bookmark. Returns ------- int How many bookmarks were created. ``0`` means no headings were found -- a document of body text has none, and one whose only structure is a shell has none to read either.
attributes.signature: def generate_outlines(self, *, max_level: int=6, prefer_structure: bool=True, replace: bool=True, open_to_level: int=0, zoom: float | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Create a flat bookmark list from matches in extracted page text.
attributes.docstring_full: Create a flat bookmark list from matches in extracted page text. A string is literal unless ``regex=True``; a compiled text regex always keeps its flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds case-insensitive matching. Python regex semantics apply, including explicit multiline/DOTALL flags; matches never cross page boundaries. No font-size or heading tags are required. Images and field values are not OCRed or searched. Each match creates one bookmark landing on its page with a fit-to-page destination. ``title_group`` is a capture number/name (default 0, the whole match). Unmatched, empty or whitespace-only groups are skipped; title whitespace is collapsed to single spaces. Repeated matches are retained. There is no inferred hierarchy or exact text-position target. Targets refer to page objects so inserting pages before a matched page does not redirect its bookmark when the document is saved. ``pages`` accepts one-based page numbers, preserving order and repetitions. ``clip``, ``exclude_regions`` and ``skip_artifacts`` follow :meth:`extract_text`. All options/indices are validated before reading selected pages. Streaming inputs read selected page content without filling full-document text/content caches. Page resource decoding follows ordinary extraction and can include unused forms. ``max_count=0`` has no user cap; a positive cap stops after that many created bookmarks. Source resource limits still apply, including matches, titles and the projected outline object count. Python regex matching has no timeout. ``replace=True`` replaces the tree, including clearing it when no titles match. ``False`` appends at the root, preserving existing items/targets. The complete plan is checked before any outline edit; failures preserve live edits and the previous tree. Returns the created bookmark count. Page content is unchanged; save the document to persist the bookmarks.
attributes.signature: def generate_outlines_from_text(self, pattern: str | re.Pattern[str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, title_group: int | str=0, replace: bool=True, max_count: int=0, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, exclude_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None, skip_artifacts: bool=False) -> int

attributes.docstring: Measure visible content on selected pages without modifying the PDF.
attributes.docstring_full: Measure visible content on selected pages without modifying the PDF. Return a dictionary keyed by one-based source page indices, in first-selected order; repeated pages are measured once. None selects all pages, and an empty selection/document returns an empty dictionary. Blank-looking pages retain a None value. Other values are detached ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` tuples in unrotated PDF page user coordinates. Options and the complete selection are validated before any rendering, even for an empty selection. Detection follows Page.get_content_bounds(): white paper, no antialiasing, current CropBox/rotation/layer visibility, and optional visible annotation/widget appearances. At finite DPI it is approximate and may miss faint or tiny marks. Stored hidden content is not inventoried and no OCR is performed. Selected pages render one at a time; streaming inputs do not populate all-page content caches. Render, parser and resource-limit failures propagate without a partial dictionary. Boxes, content, annotations, metadata and extraction cursors remain unchanged. No optional imaging dependency is required.
attributes.signature: def get_content_bounds(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, include_annotations: bool=True) -> dict[int, tuple[float, float, float, float] | None]

attributes.docstring: Return the embedded file named *name* as a FileSpecification,
attributes.docstring_full: Return the embedded file named *name* as a :class:`FileSpecification`, or ``None`` when the document has no attachment with that name.
attributes.signature: def get_embedded_file(self, name: str) -> FileSpecification | None

attributes.docstring: Return one-based page numbers from a page range string.
attributes.docstring_full: Return one-based page numbers from a page range string. *selection* is a page range string such as ``"1-3,7,10-"``. String ranges include both endpoints and may descend (``"last-1"`` reverses all pages); an omitted end selects through the last page. ``odd`` and ``even`` select physical odd/even pages; ``last`` names the final page. Order and repeated pages are retained. This method validates the selection against the document's page count and raises :exc:`PdfValidationException` if any page is out of range. Use :attr:`page_count` to check the document size before resolving a range. Returns ------- tuple of int One-based page numbers in the order specified by the selection.

attributes.docstring: Add one highlight annotation per reliably placed text match.
attributes.docstring_full: Add one highlight annotation per reliably placed text match. Search all pages or one one-based ``page_index``. A string is literal unless ``regex=True``; compiled text patterns retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds case-insensitive matching. Matches are non-overlapping, and zero-width regex matches are ignored. ``max_count=0`` is unlimited; otherwise it caps matches considered across pages, including skipped ones, in extraction order. The result reports live ``annotations`` and ``skipped_fragments`` with page indexes and text offsets. Text without usable font metrics, text assembled across separate runs, and form-XObject text may be skipped. Repeated occurrences are placed only when extraction and geometry agree on their count. Existing page text is preserved. The colour uses the standard grey/RGB/CMYK forms; opacity is between zero and one.
attributes.signature: def highlight_text(self, search: str | re.Pattern[str], *, page_index: int | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, color: ColorValue=(1.0, 1.0, 0.0), opacity: float=0.5, contents: str='', title: str | None=None) -> TextHighlightResult

attributes.docstring: Highlight multiple text patterns in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Highlight multiple text patterns in a single call. This is a convenience method that applies multiple highlight patterns to the document. It is equivalent to calling :meth:`highlight_text` for each pattern, but more efficient as it performs a single scan of the content streams per pattern. Parameters ---------- patterns A dictionary mapping search patterns to options. Each key is a string or compiled regex pattern; each value is a dict of options for that pattern (color, opacity, contents, title, kind). The color defaults to yellow for highlights if not specified. The ``kind`` option is also accepted but only 'highlight' is valid for this method. page_index One-based page number. If omitted and ``pages`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``pages``. pages Iterable of one-based page numbers to process. If omitted and ``page_index`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``page_index``. case_sensitive If True (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns. max_count Maximum highlights to perform across all patterns. ``0`` (default) means unlimited. The count is shared across all patterns. regex If True, all string patterns are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. Returns ------- TextHighlightResult A result object with highlights, skipped_fragments, highlighted_count, skipped_count, and matched_count. See Also -------- highlight_text : Highlight a single text pattern. markup_texts : Mark multiple text patterns with different styles. Examples -------- Highlight multiple patterns: >>> document.highlight_texts({"review": {}, "approved": {}}) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.highlight_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): {"color": (1, 0, 0)}, "Mr.": {}}, ... regex=True ... ) Limit highlights and target specific pages: >>> document.highlight_texts( ... {"important": {}, "critical": {}}, ... pages=[1, 3], ... max_count=5 ... )
attributes.signature: def highlight_texts(self, patterns: dict[str | re.Pattern[str], dict[str, Any] | None], *, page_index: int | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False) -> TextHighlightResult

attributes.docstring: Return the two-element file-identifier array from the PDF trailer.
attributes.docstring_full: Return the two-element file-identifier array from the PDF trailer. The value is ``None`` for freshly created (unsaved) documents; after the first :meth:`save` the array is generated and preserved.

attributes.docstring: Append version 1 or 2 JSON review annotations and return the number added.
attributes.docstring_full: Append version 1 or 2 JSON review annotations and return the number added. Accept UTF-8 bytes, a path or a readable binary stream. Streams are read from their current position and left open. ``page_map`` maps one-based source page indices to existing destination pages; every used source page must be mapped. Without it, page indices are retained. Input order is retained within each page; ``annotation_index`` is informational. Existing annotations are preserved and repeat imports append duplicates. Supported subtypes are Text, FreeText, Line, Square, Circle, Polygon, PolyLine, Highlight, Underline, Squiggly, StrikeOut, Stamp, Caret, Ink, Popup and Redact. Widgets, links, media and unknown subtypes are refused because the export omits data needed to recreate them. Supported review properties recover their PDF name/string types; nonstandard dictionary entries are refused. Appearances are not archived or generated; call ``page.annotations.generate_appearances()`` when needed. Replies and popups are linked to newly imported IDs only. Links to IDs outside the input are omitted; internal popup pairs are completed in both directions. Conflicting popup links, cross-page popups and reply cycles are refused. All JSON, property, page and relationship checks finish before any annotation is added. Malformed/unsupported data and resource-limit failures leave annotations unchanged. Limits follow :attr:`load_limits`. Redact imports markup; it does not redact content.
attributes.signature: def import_annotations_json(self, source: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, page_map: Mapping[int, int] | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Append supported XFDF review annotations and return the number added.
attributes.docstring_full: Append supported XFDF review annotations and return the number added. Accept a path, bytes or a readable binary stream, with the page mapping, append-only behavior and atomic validation of :meth:`import_annotations_json`. The subset matches :meth:`export_annotations_xfdf`, including nested popups, named replies, basic styles and geometry. Missing names are allowed; provided names must be unique. Replies resolve only against names in this input. File/ID metadata never loads external resources. Unsupported annotation types, properties, rich text, form values, DOCTYPE and entity declarations are refused. XML text and geometry are bounded by :attr:`load_limits`. Streams remain open and page content is not decoded. Appearances are not generated automatically. Redact imports review markup and does not remove content.
attributes.signature: def import_annotations_xfdf(self, source: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, page_map: Mapping[int, int] | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Import selected ZIP members as document-level embedded files.
attributes.docstring_full: Import selected ZIP members as document-level embedded files. Accepts a path, ZIP bytes or a binary stream read from its current position and left open. Returns the number of imported members, including replacements. ``names=None`` imports ordinary files in ZIP order; a string selects one exact archive name and an iterable selects names in its order, deduplicating repeats. Unknown names raise ``KeyError``. Directories are ignored; nothing is extracted to disk. By default, a root ``manifest.json`` must use the version-one format produced by :meth:`export_attachments_zip`. It is consumed as metadata, restoring original PDF names, MIME types, descriptions, dates and associated-file relationships. Set ``use_manifest=False`` to import it as an ordinary attachment. Without a manifest, names use the same portable flat-basename rules as ZIP export; ZIP timestamps and file permissions are not imported. ``on_conflict`` handles exact PDF name collisions with existing files or earlier selected members: ``"error"`` (default), ``"skip"``, ``"replace"`` or ``"rename"`` (``_2``, ``_3``, ... before the extension). Replacements replace metadata as well as content. ``compress`` controls PDF embedded-stream compression on save, independently of ZIP storage. Stored and deflated single-disk archives with classic central directories are supported; ZIP64 central directories, encrypted files, symlinks, special files and duplicate archive names are rejected. Structural checks cover the whole archive. CRC and decompression checks cover the manifest and selected, non-skipped files. All checks and staging finish before any attachment changes; page content stays lazy. ``load_limits`` bounds input and working bytes, entry/selection/result counts, metadata text/JSON nesting, per-file and total decoded sizes and compression ratios. The archive and imported bytes are buffered in memory. Invalid archives/options raise ``PdfValidationException``; filesystem and input-stream errors propagate. Changes reach the PDF when it is saved normally.
attributes.signature: def import_attachments_zip(self, source: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, names: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, on_conflict: str='error', use_manifest: bool=True, compress: bool=True) -> int

attributes.docstring: Import a complete level,title,page table and return its node count.
attributes.docstring_full: Import a complete level,title,page table and return its node count. Require that exact header, levels starting at 1 without skipped parents, and one-based positive page numbers or empty cells for headings. Titles retain Unicode, whitespace and duplicates. Import creates whole-page Fit targets without styles. UTF-8 with/without BOM works by default; other encodings and delimiters can be selected explicitly. Append roots by default; replace=True replaces the tree, with a header alone clearing it. A nonempty import requires a document page. page_map maps every used source page to an existing destination page, one-based. Targets bind to page identities and follow subsequent page insertions. No pages are created. All input, mapping, combined-tree and object-limit checks precede live changes; failures preserve existing bookmarks. Read paths, bytes/bytearray or binary streams from their current position, leaving caller streams open. No page content is decoded.
attributes.signature: def import_bookmarks_csv(self, source: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, replace: bool=False, page_map: Mapping[int, int] | None=None, delimiter: str=',', encoding: str='utf-8-sig') -> int

attributes.docstring: Import a complete JSON bookmark tree and return the added node count.
attributes.docstring_full: Import a complete JSON bookmark tree and return the added node count. Accept UTF-8 bytes, a path or a readable binary stream (left open). Append root entries by default; ``replace=True`` replaces the entire tree, including clearing it for an empty bookmarks array. Existing live collection handles remain usable. A nonempty import requires at least one document page. ``page_map`` maps every explicit local source page to an existing destination page; names and remote pages are not remapped. Indices are one-based, coordinates are not transformed. All JSON, target, style, page-map and combined-tree checks finish before the live tree is changed. Duplicate keys, unsupported versions, non-finite numbers and unknown/missing fields are refused. Invalid input and limit failures leave bookmarks unchanged. Retained names resolve against destination definitions, which this import does not create. It neither executes actions nor accesses URLs or remote files.
attributes.signature: def import_bookmarks_json(self, source: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, replace: bool=False, page_map: Mapping[int, int] | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Import links from a CSV report and return the number added.
attributes.docstring_full: Import links from a CSV report and return the number added. Accepts a path, bytes or a readable binary stream, with the page mapping and append-only behavior of :meth:`import_links_json`. The CSV schema matches :meth:`export_links_csv` output with columns: ``page_number``, ``annotation_index``, ``action_type``, ``uri``, ``target_page_number``, ``file``, ``named_action``, ``destination_view``, ``destination_parameters``, ``x0``, ``y0``, ``x1``, ``y1``. ``page_map`` maps one-based source ``page_number`` to existing destination pages. ``delimiter`` and ``encoding`` follow the ``csv`` module. Supported actions are URI, GoTo, GoToR, and Named. Links are inferred from destination fields. Existing annotations are preserved and repeat imports append duplicates. All checks finish before any annotation is added. Resource limits and CSV parsing errors are handled atomically. Limits follow :attr:`load_limits`. Returns the count of successfully imported link annotations.
attributes.signature: def import_links_csv(self, source: str | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, page_map: Mapping[int, int] | None=None, delimiter: str=',', encoding: str='utf-8') -> int

attributes.docstring: Import links from a JSON report and return the number added.
attributes.docstring_full: Import links from a JSON report and return the number added. Accepts UTF-8 bytes, a path or a readable binary stream. Streams are read from their current position and left open. ``page_map`` maps one-based source page indices to existing destination pages; every used source page must be mapped. Without it, page indices are retained and must exist in the destination document. The JSON schema matches :meth:`export_links_json` output: ``{"schema_version": 2, "links": [...]}``. Each link record may contain: - ``page_index`` (1-based): the source page for the link - ``uri``: URL for URI actions - ``destination``: a typed page view ``{page_index, view, parameters}`` - ``file``: remote file path for GoToR actions - ``named_action``: named action like "NextPage" - Other fields from the export are accepted but ignored. Supported actions are URI, GoTo, GoToR, Named, and links inferred from destination fields. JavaScript, Launch and SubmitForm are not created automatically; use the engine API for those. Existing annotations are preserved and repeat imports append duplicates. All JSON, property, page and relationship checks finish before any annotation is added. Malformed/unsupported data and resource-limit failures leave annotations unchanged. Limits follow :attr:`load_limits`. Returns the count of successfully imported link annotations.
attributes.signature: def import_links_json(self, source: str | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, page_map: Mapping[int, int] | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Get or set the document metadata (info dictionary).
attributes.docstring_full: Get or set the document metadata (info dictionary). A ``dict`` of text: ``/Info`` holds text strings (ISO 32000-1 14.3.3), with dates written ``D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm'`` (7.9.4) and ``Trapped`` written as a name — pass ``"True"``, ``"False"`` or ``"Unknown"`` for it and the name is what reaches the file. A value of another type is refused on :meth:`save` with a message naming the entry. A producer's own entries are shown as text where text is faithful (a number, a boolean) and left out where it is not (an array), and every one of them keeps its original type on save unless you change it. An entry you *do* change is written as the text you set, since the type it used to have cannot be read back out of a string. It is a dictionary in both directions: ``del``, ``pop``, ``clear`` and assigning a smaller dictionary all remove those entries from the file on :meth:`save`. An entry with no text form is the exception — you cannot delete what was never shown to you, so it stays, and a warning names it whenever something else was removed.

attributes.docstring: Return a new document alternating this document's pages with *other*.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a new document alternating this document's pages with *other*. Use ``fronts.interleave(backs, reverse_other=True)`` for two scanner passes whose back sides were scanned in reverse order. The first source keeps its order. With ``strict=True`` the page counts must match; ``strict=False`` appends the unmatched tail in its chosen order. No blank pages are inserted, and neither input is edited or disposed. Page resources, annotations, form fields, labels, layers, attachments and bookmarks follow the shared page importer. Local destinations stay attached to their pages. The result keeps this document's Info metadata and resource limits and the higher PDF version. It is independent of both inputs and starts without encryption; existing signatures cannot retain their validity in an assembled document. Dispose it when done.
attributes.signature: def interleave(self, other: Document, *, reverse_other: bool=False, strict: bool=True) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Return True if document is encrypted.
Check if the document complies with the specified PDF/A level.
attributes.docstring_full: Check if the document complies with the specified PDF/A level. Uses the same **heuristic** engine as :meth:`validate_pdfa`; do not use as a certification gate. Parameters ---------- level : str PDF/A level: ``'1a'``/``'1b'``, ``'2a'``/``'2b'``/``'2u'``, ``'3a'``/``'3b'``/``'3u'``, or ``'4'``/``'4e'``/``'4f'``. Returns ------- bool True if compliant, False otherwise.

attributes.docstring: Heuristic PDF/UA-1 catalog structure check (tagged PDF shell).
attributes.docstring_full: Heuristic PDF/UA-1 catalog structure check (tagged PDF shell). Uses the same rules as :meth:`validate_pdfua`. A ``True`` value does **not** mean the document is accessible or PDF/UA certified — only that required catalog entries for tagging passed this library's lightweight inspection. For ISO 14289-2 call ``validate_pdfua(part=2)``.

attributes.docstring: Whether the document conforms to a PDF/X level (heuristic).
attributes.docstring_full: Whether the document conforms to a PDF/X level (heuristic). Uses the same checks as :meth:`validate_pdfx`; do not use as a certification gate -- and note that no free validator covers PDF/X, so unlike the PDF/A checks these are not cross-checked against a reference implementation. Parameters ---------- standard : str ``"PDF/X-1a:2001"``, ``"PDF/X-1a:2003"``, ``"PDF/X-3:2002"``, ``"PDF/X-3:2003"`` or ``"PDF/X-4"``, in any spelling :meth:`aspose_pdf.pdfx.PdfXStandard.by_name` accepts. Returns ------- bool ``True`` when the document raises no PDF/X errors.

attributes.docstring: Yield decoded content stream bytes for each page, one at a time.
attributes.docstring_full: Yield decoded content stream bytes for each page, one at a time. Delegates to :meth:`SimplePdf.iter_page_content_streams`. In lazy mode only one page's content is held in memory at any point. Yields ------ bytes Decoded content bytes for each page in order.

attributes.docstring: Iterate over the pages of the document one at a time.
attributes.docstring_full: Iterate over the pages of the document one at a time. This is a lightweight generator that yields :class:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page` objects without materialising the full list. It works for both normally-loaded documents and documents opened in streaming mode via :meth:`open_streaming`. In streaming mode, each page's content stream is decoded only when :attr:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page.content` is accessed, keeping memory usage proportional to one page rather than the whole document. Yields ------ Page Pages in document order, starting at number 1.

attributes.docstring: Yield independent fixed-size page batches as they are requested.
attributes.docstring_full: Yield independent fixed-size page batches as they are requested. Parts have the same content, metadata and resource policy as :meth:`split_every`, including a shorter final batch. Empty documents yield no parts. The size must be a positive integer; validation and planning occur on the first iteration, before importing any pages. No part is imported until requested, and previous parts are not accumulated. Keep the source open and unmodified until iteration ends. Each yielded document belongs to the caller: close or dispose it when done. Yielded parts remain usable after the iterator or source closes, or if a later import fails. Closing the iterator does not dispose them. The source outline model is restored before every yield, including early termination and failures. Use ``contextlib.closing`` when stopping iteration early to release the iterator's references promptly.
attributes.signature: def iter_split_every(self, pages_per_part: int) -> Generator[Document, None, None]

attributes.docstring: Yield independent documents, one for each page.
attributes.docstring_full: Yield independent documents, one for each page. This is the streaming variant of :meth:`split_pages`. Each yielded document contains exactly one page from the source document. The source document remains unchanged, and the outline model is restored before every yield. Yields ------ Document An independent document containing one page. Each yielded document retains Info metadata, page resources, boxes, labels, annotations, form fields, layers and tags. Examples -------- :: for page_doc in document.iter_split_pages(): with page_doc: # Process each page without loading all into memory page_doc.save(f"page-{page_doc.pages[1].number}.pdf") Notes ----- Use ``contextlib.closing`` when stopping iteration early to release the iterator's references promptly. Each yielded document belongs to the caller: close or dispose it when done. Empty documents yield nothing. The source and its files are unchanged. Each yielded document is independent and does not inherit source encryption or signature validity.

attributes.docstring: Yield independent documents, one for each spread half.
attributes.docstring_full: Yield independent documents, one for each spread half. This is the streaming variant of :meth:`split_spreads`. Each yielded document contains the pages created from splitting one spread into two halves. The source document remains unchanged, and the outline model is restored before every yield. Parameters ---------- pages : iterable of int or None, optional One-based page numbers to split. Other pages stay in source order. Repeats are split once and an empty selection copies the document. Default is all pages. layout : str, optional ``"horizontal"`` (default) reads left then right; ``"vertical"`` reads top then bottom. reverse : bool, optional Reverse the order of halves (default: False). split_ratio : float, optional Position the cut from the left/top, strictly between 0 and 1 (default: 0.5). gutter : float, optional Remove a centered strip in page coordinate units (default: 0.0). flatten_fields : bool, optional Flatten form widgets before splitting (default: True). Yields ------ Document An independent document containing one half of a split spread. Each yielded document retains Info metadata, page resources, boxes, labels, annotations, form fields, layers and tags. Examples -------- :: for half in document.iter_split_spreads(): with half: # Process each half without loading all into memory half.save(f"half-{half.pages[1].number}.pdf") Notes ----- Use ``contextlib.closing`` when stopping iteration early to release the iterator's references promptly. Each yielded document belongs to the caller: close or dispose it when done.
attributes.signature: def iter_split_spreads(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, layout: str='horizontal', reverse: bool=False, split_ratio: float=0.5, gutter: float=0.0, flatten_fields: bool=True) -> Generator[Document, None, None]

attributes.docstring: Yield one detached text string per selected page, without joining them.
attributes.docstring_full: Yield one detached text string per selected page, without joining them. Options and extraction semantics match :meth:`extract_text`. Selection and regions are validated and snapshotted on this call; no page text is read until the iterator advances. Order, repeats and empty strings for blank pages are retained. Keep the source open and its page order unchanged until finished. Closing the iterator stops further reads; strings already yielded remain usable after the source closes. Streaming sources decode only requested pages. Results do not replace the full-document text cache or change the text cursor. Current-page and cumulative UTF-8 text sizes obey the document's decoded-byte limits. A later extraction error propagates after any earlier strings yielded.
attributes.signature: def iter_text_pages(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, skip_artifacts: bool=False, exclude_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None) -> Generator[str, None, None]

attributes.docstring: The document-level scripts, as a mapping of name to source.
attributes.docstring_full: The document-level scripts, as a mapping of name to source. ISO 32000-1 12.6.4.17: the catalog's ``/Names /JavaScript`` name tree holds what a viewer runs when the document opens -- the place to define the functions a field's ``/AA`` scripts call -- and it runs them **in key order**, which is why such names are usually written to sort the way they are meant to run:: document.javascript["00_helpers"] = "function total(a, b) ..." del document.javascript["00_helpers"]

attributes.docstring: The document's search keywords, the ``/Info`` ``/Keywords`` entry.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's search keywords, the ``/Info`` ``/Keywords`` entry. One text entry, comma-separated when a viewer writes several, or ``None`` when absent. Assign text to set it, or ``None`` to remove the entry. The value lives in the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`).

attributes.docstring: The document's default natural language, stored in catalog ``/Lang``.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's default natural language, stored in catalog ``/Lang``. Returns the declared text verbatim, or ``None`` for an absent/null entry. An empty string declares an unknown language. Assign a language identifier such as ``"en-US"`` or ``"zh-Hant-TW"``, or ``None`` to remove the declaration. New nonempty values use 1-8 character ASCII subtags separated by hyphens, with an alphabetic first subtag; registry membership is not checked and spelling is preserved. Reading or writing does not decode page content, change text, or run PDF/UA conversion. Local language overrides remain intact. Malformed metadata types/references raise ``PdfParseException``; metadata sizes and reference traversal obey ``load_limits``.

attributes.docstring: The document's optional content groups (layers).
attributes.docstring_full: The document's optional content groups (layers). Each :class:`~aspose_pdf.layers.Layer` reports its name and whether the default configuration shows it; setting ``visible`` updates the document's ``/OCProperties /D`` configuration, so rendering, graphics absorption and a later :meth:`save` all follow it. A document without optional content returns an empty collection. Example ------- :: for layer in document.layers: if layer.name == "Watermark": layer.visible = False

attributes.docstring: Link a literal phrase to a URI or a destination within this PDF.
attributes.docstring_full: Link a literal phrase to a URI or a destination within this PDF. Match non-overlapping occurrences, respecting case by default. The nonblank ``uri`` is stored verbatim, as with ``URIAction``. Alternatively, omit ``uri`` and supply ``target=FitDestination(3)`` (or another typed Destination), or ``target="chapter-3"`` for an existing named destination. Destination pages are one-based; coordinates must be finite. A named target stays a name, so redefining it redirects the links. Unknown or unresolvable names are rejected. Supply exactly one of ``uri`` and ``target``. Text, fonts and content streams remain unchanged. ``pages`` selects one-based pages in order; ``None`` selects all. ``max_count=0`` is unlimited; a positive cap includes matches skipped for uncertain geometry or overlap with existing links, regardless of their target. Return ``AutoLinkResult`` with live annotations and skipped/existing fragments. Placement and streaming behavior follow :meth:`auto_link`: only reliably located text receives an axis-aligned link rectangle. Forms, unknown fonts, ambiguous repetitions and phrases split across lines or unrelated runs may remain unlinked. No OCR or regular expression matching is performed. Options are validated before edits; an error on a later page can leave earlier pages' links in place.
attributes.signature: def link_text(self, search: str, uri: str | None=None, *, target: Destination | str | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0) -> AutoLinkResult

attributes.docstring: Link multiple text patterns to a URI or destination in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Link multiple text patterns to a URI or destination in a single call. This is a convenience method that links multiple text patterns to the same URI or destination. It is equivalent to calling :meth:`link_text` for each pattern, but more efficient as it performs a single scan of the content streams. Parameters ---------- patterns A dictionary mapping search patterns to options. Each key is a string or compiled regex pattern; each value is a dict of options for that pattern (currently unused, kept for consistency with other batch APIs). uri The URI to link to. Exactly one of ``uri`` and ``target`` must be provided. target A destination to link to. Exactly one of ``uri`` and ``target`` must be provided. pages One-based page numbers or None for all pages. case_sensitive If True (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns. max_count Maximum links to create across all patterns. ``0`` (default) means unlimited. The count is shared across all patterns. regex If True, all string patterns are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. Returns ------- AutoLinkResult A result object with annotations, skipped_fragments, existing_fragments, and counts (linked_count, skipped_count, existing_count, matched_count). See Also -------- link_text : Link a single text pattern. highlight_texts : Highlight multiple text patterns. Examples -------- Link multiple patterns to a URI: >>> document.link_texts( ... {"review": {}, "approved": {}}, ... uri="https://example.com/docs" ... ) Link multiple patterns to a named destination: >>> import re >>> document.link_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): {}, "chapter": {}}, ... target="appendix", ... regex=True ... ) Limit links and target a specific page: >>> document.link_texts( ... {"important": {}, "critical": {}}, ... uri="https://example.com", ... pages=[1], ... max_count=5 ... )
attributes.signature: def link_texts(self, patterns: dict[str | re.Pattern[str], dict[str, Any] | None], uri: str | None=None, *, target: Destination | str | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False) -> AutoLinkResult

attributes.docstring: Load a PDF from a file path, raw bytes, or a binary stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Load a PDF from a file path, raw bytes, or a binary stream. Parameters ---------- source : str, Path, bytes, bytearray, or BinaryIO File path, raw PDF bytes, or any readable binary stream (e.g. ``BytesIO``, an open file handle in ``"rb"`` mode). When a stream is supplied its current position is read to EOF; the stream is **not** closed afterwards. password : str, optional Password for encrypted PDFs. certificate, private_key : optional Certificate recipient credentials for an ``/Adobe.PubSec`` PDF. key_encryption_key : bytes, optional Pre-shared AES key for a CMS KEK recipient. limits : PdfLoadLimits, optional Resource policy for this load. When omitted, the policy configured on the document is reused. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining. Raises ------ FileNotFoundError If source is a path that doesn't exist. ValueError If source is bytes/stream that are not valid PDF data. TypeError If source is none of the accepted types.
attributes.signature: def load_from(self, source: str | bytes | bytearray | Path | BinaryIO, *, password: str | None=None, certificate: Any=None, private_key: Any=None, key_encryption_key: bytes | bytearray | None=None, limits: PdfLoadLimits | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Load a PDF from a binary stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Load a PDF from a binary stream. This is a convenience method equivalent to ``load_from(stream, ...)``, provided for clarity when loading from in-memory streams such as ``io.BytesIO``. Parameters ---------- stream : BinaryIO Any readable binary stream (e.g., ``BytesIO``, an open file handle in ``"rb"`` mode). password : str, optional Password for encrypted PDFs. certificate, private_key : optional Certificate recipient credentials for an ``/Adobe.PubSec`` PDF. key_encryption_key : bytes, optional Pre-shared AES key for a CMS KEK recipient. limits : PdfLoadLimits, optional Resource policy for this load. When omitted, the policy configured on the document is reused. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining. Raises ------ ValueError If stream contains invalid PDF data. TypeError If stream is not a readable binary stream. Notes ----- The stream's current position is read to EOF; the stream is **not** closed afterwards. Examples -------- :: from io import BytesIO # Load from an in-memory buffer buffer = BytesIO(pdf_bytes) document = Document() document.load_from_stream(buffer) # Load from a file-like object with open("document.pdf", "rb") as f: doc = Document() doc.load_from_stream(f) # Load with password buffer = BytesIO(encrypted_bytes) doc = Document() doc.load_from_stream(buffer, password="secret")
attributes.signature: def load_from_stream(self, stream: BinaryIO, *, password: str | None=None, certificate: Any=None, private_key: Any=None, key_encryption_key: bytes | bytearray | None=None, limits: PdfLoadLimits | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Return limits used for loading, lazy processing, and authored assets.
Highlight, underline, strike out or wave-underline matching text.
attributes.docstring_full: Highlight, underline, strike out or wave-underline matching text. ``kind`` is ``"highlight"``, ``"underline"``, ``"strike_out"`` or ``"squiggly"``. ``color=None`` chooses yellow for highlights and black for the other styles. Search options, geometry limits and partial failure behavior match :meth:`highlight_text`; page text is preserved. The result contains live annotation handles, skipped fragments and ``marked_count``, ``skipped_count`` and ``matched_count``.
attributes.signature: def markup_text(self, search: str | re.Pattern[str], *, kind: str='highlight', page_index: int | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, color: ColorValue | None=None, opacity: float=0.5, contents: str='', title: str | None=None) -> TextMarkupResult

attributes.docstring: Mark multiple text patterns in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Mark multiple text patterns in a single call. This is a convenience method that applies multiple text markup patterns to the document. It is equivalent to calling :meth:`markup_text` for each pattern, but more efficient as it performs a single scan of the content streams per pattern. Parameters ---------- patterns A dictionary mapping search patterns to options. Each key is a string or compiled regex pattern; each value is a dict of options for that pattern (color, opacity, contents, title, kind), or None for defaults. The ``kind`` option specifies the markup style for that pattern ('highlight', 'underline', 'strike_out', or 'squiggly'). When omitted, the global ``kind`` parameter is used. kind The default markup kind: 'highlight', 'underline', 'strike_out', or 'squiggly'. Patterns without a ``kind`` option use this value. page_index One-based page number. If omitted and ``pages`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``pages``. pages Iterable of one-based page numbers to process. If omitted and ``page_index`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``page_index``. case_sensitive If True (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns. max_count Maximum marks to perform across all patterns. ``0`` (default) means unlimited. The count is shared across all patterns. regex If True, all string patterns are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. Returns ------- TextMarkupResult A result object with annotations, skipped_fragments, marked_count, skipped_count, and matched_count. See Also -------- markup_text : Mark a single text pattern. highlight_texts : Highlight multiple text patterns. Examples -------- Mark multiple patterns with different colors (same kind): >>> document.markup_texts( ... {"review": {"color": (1, 0, 0)}, "draft": {"color": (0, 1, 0)}}, ... kind="highlight" ... ) Mix different markup kinds: >>> document.markup_texts( ... {"review": {"kind": "highlight", "color": (1, 0, 0)}, ... "draft": {"kind": "underline", "color": (0, 1, 0)}} ... ) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.markup_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): {}, "Mr.": {"title": "Formal Title"}}, ... kind="underline", ... regex=True ... ) Limit marks and target specific pages: >>> document.markup_texts( ... {"important": {}, "critical": {}}, ... pages=[1, 3], ... max_count=5, ... kind="strike_out" ... )
attributes.signature: def markup_texts(self, patterns: dict[str | re.Pattern[str], dict[str, Any] | None], *, kind: str='highlight', page_index: int | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False) -> TextMarkupResult

attributes.docstring: Merge supplied documents, optionally creating a section for each input.
attributes.docstring_full: Merge supplied documents, optionally creating a section for each input. ``create_bookmarks=True`` adds a bookmark to each non-empty input's first imported page and nests its existing bookmarks underneath. ``bookmark_titles`` supplies one non-blank title per input, including empty inputs, and requires ``create_bookmarks=True``. Otherwise titles use the source filename stem, PDF Title, or ``"Document N"`` in input order. Empty inputs receive no new section; existing target bookmarks stay at the root. The target's existing pages receive no new section. Options, titles and resulting bookmark count/depth are checked before importing pages. Later import failures can leave earlier inputs merged. Sources remain independent; merging this document into itself with section bookmarks is refused. The default keeps flat bookmark merging.
attributes.signature: def merge(self, *documents: Document, create_bookmarks: bool=False, bookmark_titles: Iterable[str] | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Move a page to *new_position*, keeping the page itself.
attributes.docstring_full: Move a page to *new_position*, keeping the page itself. The page keeps its object, so the links, bookmarks and named destinations that point at it keep landing on it, and the form fields whose widgets sit on it stay whole -- which a remove-then-reinsert or copy-then-delete reorder cannot promise. Page labels follow their pages. Both numbers are one-based, as everywhere else in the API. Parameters ---------- page_number : int The one-based page number to move. Page numbers start at 1. new_position : int The one-based position to move the page to. The pages between the page's old and new position shift the other way by one. Returns ------- Page The moved page, at its new position. Raises ------ IndexError If *page_number* or *new_position* is not an existing page or position (both must be between 1 and the number of pages in the document), or the document has no pages. Examples -------- :: # Put the last page first doc.move_page(len(doc), 1) # Move page 2 behind page 5 doc.move_page(2, 5)
attributes.signature: def move_page(self, page_number: int, new_position: int) -> Page

attributes.docstring: Return a new document with ``rows * columns`` pages on each sheet.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a new document with ``rows * columns`` pages on each sheet. Each page is brought across as a form XObject with everything it draws with, scaled to fit its cell proportionally and centred in it -- nothing is stretched and nothing is cut off. The sheet is *page_size*, or the first page's own size when none is given, so four pages go onto a sheet the size of one. A landscape sheet for a 2-up of portrait pages is asked for by passing one:: two_up = document.n_up(1, 2, page_size=PageSize.A4.landscape()) *order* is ``"row"`` (left to right, top row first) or ``"column"``. Set ``crop_marks=True`` for eight black trim guides around each placed page's displayed bounds. Length, offset and stroke width are in sheet points; defaults are 9, 3 and 0.5. Marks use available cell whitespace, outer margins and half of each gutter. Insufficient room raises before page content is imported; increase margin/gutter or reduce mark sizes. Empty slots are unmarked. Source page boxes and placement stay the same.
attributes.signature: def n_up(self, rows: int=2, columns: int=2, *, page_size: Any=None, margin: float=0.0, gutter: float=0.0, order: str='row', crop_marks: bool=False, crop_mark_length: float=9.0, crop_mark_offset: float=3.0, crop_mark_width: float=0.5) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Where the document opens, or what it does when opened.
attributes.docstring_full: Where the document opens, or what it does when opened. ``/OpenAction`` (table 28) is either a destination -- a page and how to fit it -- or an action, so this gives back a :class:`Destination` or an :class:`Action`, and takes either. ``None`` removes it, and reading gives ``None`` for a destination whose page the document no longer has: a viewer ignores such an entry rather than opening somewhere else.

attributes.docstring: Open a PDF in streaming/lazy mode for memory-efficient page processing.
attributes.docstring_full: Open a PDF in streaming/lazy mode for memory-efficient page processing. Unlike :meth:`load_from`, page content streams are **not** decoded upfront. Each page's content is decoded on demand when accessed via :attr:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page.content` or :meth:`iter_page_content_streams`. This is ideal for large PDFs where only a subset of pages needs to be processed. Reading text and deleting pages work here as they do anywhere else, and both keep the document lazy: ``extract_text`` decodes one page at a time, and ``pages.delete`` shifts the page's identity without decoding the rest of the file. The returned :class:`Document` is a normal context manager — use it with ``with`` to ensure resources are released:: with Document.open_streaming("large.pdf") as doc: for page in doc.iter_pages(): text = page.content # decoded on demand ... Parameters ---------- path: File system path to the PDF. password: Optional password for encrypted PDFs. limits: Optional resource policy for untrusted input and later lazy work. Returns ------- Document A document with ``_engine_pdf._lazy == True``. Raises ------ FileNotFoundError If *path* does not exist. PdfSecurityException If the PDF is encrypted and *password* is missing, empty, or whitespace-only (after stripping).
attributes.signature: def open_streaming(cls, path: str | Path, *, password: str | None=None, limits: PdfLoadLimits | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Process the document and remove unused resources.
attributes.docstring_full: Process the document and remove unused resources. This includes image/stream deduplication, garbage collection, and stream compression. Parameters ---------- options : OptimizationOptions, optional Controls which techniques run. Defaults to :class:`~aspose_pdf.optimization.OptimizationOptions` with the standard cleanups enabled. compress_streams : bool When ``False``, skip Flate compression of streams (other cleanups still run). Defaults to ``True``. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining.
attributes.signature: def optimize(self, options: OptimizationOptions | None=None, *, compress_streams: bool=True) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Alias for optimize.
attributes.docstring_full: Alias for :meth:`optimize`.
attributes.signature: def optimize_resources(self, options: OptimizationOptions | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Bookmark tree for this document.
attributes.docstring_full: Bookmark tree for this document. Returns a live :class:`~aspose_pdf.outlines.OutlineCollection`. Changes made to the collection are persisted when :meth:`save` is called.

attributes.docstring: Return the current number of pages.
The page label ranges, keyed by the index of the page each starts at.
attributes.docstring_full: The page label ranges, keyed by the index of the page each starts at. See :class:`~aspose_pdf.page_labels.PageLabelCollection`; a page's own label is :attr:`Page.label <aspose_pdf.pages.Page.label>`.

attributes.docstring: How the pages are arranged (``/PageLayout``, table 28).
attributes.docstring_full: How the pages are arranged (``/PageLayout``, table 28). One page at a time, one continuous column, or two of either, with the odd-numbered pages on whichever side. Defaults to :attr:`PageLayout.SINGLE_PAGE`.

attributes.docstring: What a viewer shows beside the page when the document opens.
attributes.docstring_full: What a viewer shows beside the page when the document opens. ``/PageMode`` (ISO 32000-1 table 28): the bookmarks, the thumbnails, the layers or the attachments panel, full screen, or nothing. A document that says nothing, or something the specification does not allow, opens with :attr:`PageMode.USE_NONE`.

attributes.docstring: Get the collection of pages.
What a reader may do with this document: the ``/P`` word, with names.
attributes.docstring_full: What a reader may do with this document: the ``/P`` word, with names. A :class:`~aspose_pdf.permissions.Permissions` -- an ``int`` subclass, so it still compares and masks exactly as the raw signed 32-bit value did, while ``permissions.can_copy`` and ``permissions.allowed`` say what it means (ISO 32000-1 Table 22). An **unencrypted** document has no ``/P`` at all, and nothing is being withheld, so this reports :meth:`Permissions.all` (``-4``) for one.

attributes.docstring: The program that last wrote the file, the ``/Info`` ``/Producer``.
attributes.docstring_full: The program that last wrote the file, the ``/Info`` ``/Producer``. ``None`` when absent. Assign text to set it, or ``None`` to remove the entry. The value lives in the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`).

attributes.docstring: Return an independent image-only PDF of the selected visible pages.
attributes.docstring_full: Return an independent image-only PDF of the selected visible pages. ``pages`` uses one-based page numbers, preserving order and repeats; ``None`` selects all pages. An empty selection returns a new empty document. All options, indices, page geometry and planned output limits are validated before any page renders or an output document is built. Pages render at finite positive ``dpi`` (default 150), on the RGB byte triple ``background``. ``antialias`` is a boolean (True = 3x) or an integer factor 1-8. Visible annotations and form appearances count unless ``include_annotations=False``. The source's font substitution and layer visibility apply, with the renderer's coverage/limitations. ``mode`` is ``"rgb"`` (default, 8-bit DeviceRGB), ``"gray"`` (8-bit DeviceGray) or ``"bilevel"`` (1-bit DeviceGray). Color-mode aliases match raster image exports. Gray uses Rec. 601 luminance. Bilevel uses integer ``threshold`` from 0 to 255 (default 128); values below it are black and values at or above it are white. ``dither=True`` applies Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion for bilevel output. Threshold/dither are validated for every mode but only affect bilevel conversion. Each result page has one opaque image. Converted samples are stored losslessly, using Flate when smaller and allowed by the compression-ratio policy. CropBox and rotation are baked into the image; the displayed physical size is retained, with a new zero-origin MediaBox and zero rotation. Pixel dimensions round up at the selected DPI; image placement uses the original displayed size rather than enlarging it to those pixels. Only rendered appearance is copied. Text/OCR layers, vector paths, annotations, fields, links, outlines, labels, tags, scripts, attachments and original metadata are not transferred as objects. New documents start without encryption or valid source signatures. Text is no longer searchable/selectable; images may be larger and less sharp when zoomed. This is not OCR or a guarantee that unsupported PDF graphics render. Source content/files are unchanged, and streaming sources read only selected pages without filling whole-document text/content caches. One completed source raster is held at a time; the result retains all image samples and compressed streams in memory. It inherits resource limits, including page/object counts, per-image/supersampled pixels, sample/content sizes and cumulative decoded output bytes. Compression buffers are bounded conservatively. Failures dispose partial results. The result survives source disposal; dispose it when done.
attributes.signature: def rasterized_copy(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, dpi: float=150.0, background: Sequence[int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, include_annotations: bool=True, mode: str='rgb', threshold: int=128, dither: bool=False) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Remove existing text from simple page-content text-showing operands.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove existing text from simple page-content text-showing operands. With ``overlay=True`` a filled rectangle (``overlay_color`` -- grey, RGB or CMYK, default black) is drawn over each removed run -- the classic redaction bar. The bar is cosmetic (the text is already removed from the content); a run whose position cannot be tracked is left unmarked. A successful redaction requires a full save: obsolete streams and object storage are discarded, and ``save(incremental=True)`` raises. Existing signatures are invalidated by that rewrite. Seekable output streams are replaced from offset zero and truncated; append-mode and nonseekable streams are refused. Alternate text attached to changed runs and their structure ancestors is removed in full. Tagged Form XObjects and named alternate-text properties inside forms are refused. Unresolved structure mappings, ambiguous property aliases and removal of named properties inherited by forms also raise :exc:`~aspose_pdf.exceptions.PdfValidationException`. If an error occurs after earlier pages were edited, those edits remain in the document. This edits matched page/form text only, not independent copies in metadata, attachments, annotations, images, or unselected occurrences. The original input file is unchanged unless explicitly overwritten. With ``regex=True`` -- or a compiled :class:`re.Pattern` as *search* -- the search is a regular expression, which is what redacting a *shape* rather than a phrase needs: ``\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}`` for a social security number, ``\b\d{4}( \d{4}){3}\b`` for a card. The overlay bars come from the same spans the removal used, so they land on the text that went. See :meth:`replace_text` for how a pattern is matched.
attributes.signature: def redact_text(self, search: str | re.Pattern[str], *, page_index: int | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, overlay: bool=False, overlay_color: ColorValue=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)) -> int

attributes.docstring: Remove multiple text patterns in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove multiple text patterns in a single call. This is a convenience method that redacts multiple text patterns from the document. It is equivalent to calling :meth:`redact_text` for each pattern in *patterns*, but more efficient as it performs a single scan of the content streams. Parameters ---------- patterns A mapping of search patterns to ``None``. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are ignored (redaction removes text rather than replacing it with something). page_index One-based page number. If omitted and ``pages`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``pages``. pages Iterable of one-based page numbers to process. If omitted and ``page_index`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``page_index``. case_sensitive If ``True`` (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns. max_count Maximum redactions to perform across all patterns. ``0`` (default) means unlimited. The count is shared across all patterns. regex If ``True``, all keys are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. overlay If ``True``, draw a filled rectangle over each removed run (the classic redaction bar). The default is ``False``, which removes the text without marking its location. overlay_color The color of the overlay bar when ``overlay=True``. Grey, RGB or CMYK values are accepted. Default is black. Returns ------- int Total number of redactions made across all patterns. See Also -------- redact_text : Remove a single text pattern. replace_texts : Replace multiple text patterns. Examples -------- Redact multiple patterns in one call: >>> document.redact_texts({"password": None, "secret": None}) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.redact_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}"): None}, # SSN pattern ... regex=True, ... overlay=True ... ) Limit redactions and target specific pages: >>> document.redact_texts( ... {"confidential": None}, ... pages=[1, 3], ... max_count=5, ... overlay=True ... )
attributes.signature: def redact_texts(self, patterns: Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], None], *, page_index: int | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, overlay: bool=False, overlay_color: ColorValue=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)) -> int

attributes.docstring: Remove matching review annotations and return removed occurrence count.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove matching review annotations and return removed occurrence count. Combine filters with AND; ``authors`` accepts one exact author or an iterable of alternatives. None disables that filter; an empty author string matches an unset/empty author and an empty iterable matches none. ``case_sensitive=False`` uses Unicode casefolding, without trimming. ``pages`` uses one-based page numbers; repeated pages are inspected once. ``before`` and ``after`` are exclusive date bounds, accepting datetime, date, ISO strings or PDF date strings. Dates mean midnight; naive values and PDF dates without zones use UTC. PDF dates may omit trailing fields, defaulting month/day to 1 and time to zero. ``date_field`` selects ``modified`` (/M) or ``created`` (/CreationDate), without fallback. Missing, invalid or non-string annotation dates do not match date filters. Authors that are not PDF text strings do not match authors. Default subtypes are Text, FreeText, Line, Square, Circle, Polygon, PolyLine, Highlight, Underline, Squiggly, StrikeOut, Stamp, Caret, Ink and Redact. Explicit subtypes can select other kinds, but Widget is refused: use the form API. Links and file attachments are preserved by default. Removing Redact markup does not apply redaction. Owned popups on selected pages are removed with their matched owner, even if the popup itself does not match. Count includes those popups. Surviving replies are preserved, detaching IRT/RT when their parent is no longer attached anywhere; incoming Popup links are repaired too. References to shared targets remain while those targets stay attached. Metadata on other pages is inspected for these repairs.
