A deletion that would orphan a popup outside the selection is refused atomically. ``dry_run=True`` performs the same validation/planning and returns the count without edits. All validation and relationship planning precede mutation, under resource limits. Content, appearances and embedded assets are not decoded; streaming inputs stay lazy. Annotation arrays are replaced rather than editing shared arrays in place. Other PDF data is preserved. Changes remain in memory until saved. This is not physical erasure, tag-tree repair or a secure sanitization operation; detached object bytes or unrelated references can remain in the PDF. Reacquire annotation views after removal because indices may shift.
attributes.signature: def remove_annotations(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, authors: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, before: _datetime.datetime | _datetime.date | str | None=None, after: _datetime.datetime | _datetime.date | str | None=None, date_field: str='modified', subtypes: str | Iterable[str] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> int

attributes.docstring: Remove annotations whose contents match patterns in a single pass.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove annotations whose contents match patterns in a single pass. This is a convenience method that removes multiple annotations based on patterns in their contents. It is more efficient than calling :meth:`remove_annotations` multiple times for each pattern. The method accepts a mapping of search patterns to ``None`` (indicating removal). Patterns may be strings or compiled regex patterns. Parameters ---------- patterns A mapping of search patterns to ``None``. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values must be ``None``. pages One-based page numbers to process. ``None`` (default) processes all pages. Duplicates are processed once. Rejected page numbers raise an error. regex If ``True``, string patterns are treated as regular expressions. Compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys always use regex mode. case_sensitive If ``True`` (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns that already have flags set. dry_run If ``True``, perform all checks and count changes without modifying the document. Return the number of changes that would be made. Returns ------- int Total number of annotations removed across all patterns. Each annotation is counted at most once, even if multiple patterns match its contents. Notes ----- The batch operation scans the document once and applies all patterns to each annotation's contents. If multiple patterns match the same contents, the annotation is removed once. This preserves the same behavior as :meth:`replace_annotation_contents` for annotation sharing and resource limits. Annotations shared with unselected pages are rejected. See Also -------- replace_annotation_contents : Replace annotation contents patterns. remove_annotations : Remove annotations by author, date, subtype. redact_texts : Remove multiple text patterns from page content. Examples -------- Remove annotations with "confidential" in their contents: >>> document.remove_annotations_by_contents({"confidential": None}) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.remove_annotations_by_contents( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{4}"): None} ... ) Limit to specific pages: >>> document.remove_annotations_by_contents( ... {"review": None}, ... pages=[1, 2] ... )
attributes.signature: def remove_annotations_by_contents(self, patterns: Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], None], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> int

attributes.docstring: Remove the embedded file named *name*.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove the embedded file named *name*. Returns ``True`` when an attachment was removed, ``False`` when the document had no attachment with that name. The change is written to the ``/Names /EmbeddedFiles`` name tree on the next save.

attributes.docstring: Remove visually blank pages and return their original one-based page numbers.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove visually blank pages and return their original one-based page numbers. Selection, detection settings and result order follow :meth:`find_blank_pages`. Every selected page is inspected before any deletion. Rendering, option or selection failures leave pages intact. ``dry_run=True`` reports the same candidates without editing anything. An empty document or a selection with no blank pages returns ``[]``. Removing every page raises ``PdfValidationException`` before mutation; a dry run can still report all pages as candidates. Pages are deleted in descending index order, retaining the order of remaining pages. Page label ranges follow normal page deletion. Bookmarks on retained pages keep their destination views; bookmarks on removed pages become targetless headings and retain their children, titles and styles. Detection is the same finite-resolution visual heuristic as :meth:`find_blank_pages`, including annotation visibility. A page that looks blank can still store hidden data. Deletion does not securely erase PDF objects or previous revisions. Source files are changed only on an explicit save. Returned indices always refer to the document before this call, including for unordered or repeated selections.
attributes.signature: def remove_blank_pages(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, max_ink_ratio: float=0.0, include_annotations: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> list[int]

attributes.docstring: Remove visually duplicate pages and return their original indices.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove visually duplicate pages and return their original indices. Detection follows :meth:`find_duplicate_pages`. ``keep="first"`` retains the first member of each group in selection order; ``keep="last"`` retains the last. With ``pages=None``, this is document order. Only selected pages are compared. Repeated indices count once, unselected pages are retained, and surviving pages keep document order. Results are sorted original one-based page numbers, before any deletion. Every comparison finishes before deletion starts. Invalid options, selections, rendering failures and inspection limits leave pages intact. ``dry_run=True`` returns the same candidates without editing pages, navigation or text caches. ``dry_run`` must be a boolean. Empty inputs and selections without duplicates return ``[]``. At least one member of each group is retained, including for entirely blank documents. Page labels follow ordinary deletion. Retained bookmark targets keep their destination views; bookmarks on removed pages become targetless headings with their titles, styles and children intact. Live bookmark objects are updated in place. Local links to removed pages lose their target. Text caches are cleared after removal. Streaming sources read selected page content only, and files change only on explicit save. Equality is specific to the renderer and DPI, and visually identical pages can contain different hidden text, form values or other data. Deletion uses ordinary page editing and does not securely erase stored objects or previous revisions. It is not a transactional rewrite.
attributes.signature: def remove_duplicate_pages(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, keep: str='first', dpi: float=72.0, include_annotations: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> list[int]

attributes.docstring: Remove a page from the document and return it.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove a page from the document and return it. The removed page is returned as a :class:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page` object that can be inserted into another document using :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.PageCollection.insert` or :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.PageCollection.add`. Parameters ---------- page_number : int The one-based page number to remove. Page numbers start at 1. Returns ------- Page The removed page, which can be inserted into another document. Raises ------ IndexError If *page_number* is not a valid page number (must be between 1 and the number of pages in the document). Examples -------- :: # Remove page 3 and insert it at the beginning of another document removed_page = doc.remove_page(3) other_doc.pages.insert(1, removed_page) # Remove the last page last_page = doc.remove_page(len(doc)) Notes ----- After removal, the page count decreases by one, and all page numbers after the removed page are shifted down by one. For example, if you remove page 2 from a 5-page document, the former page 3 becomes page 2, page 4 becomes page 3, and page 5 becomes page 4. The removed page retains all its properties: content, annotations, form fields, layer assignments, page labels, and bookmarks that point to it.

attributes.docstring: Render a page overview as one RGB image without changing the PDF.
attributes.docstring_full: Render a page overview as one RGB image without changing the PDF. ``pages`` selects one-based page numbers; ``None`` selects all pages. Order and repeated indices are preserved. An empty selection raises ``PdfValidationException``. ``columns`` is the maximum number of cells per row; fewer selected pages produce fewer columns. ``thumbnail_size=(width, height)``, ``margin`` and ``spacing`` are integer pixels. Each visible CropBox, with page rotation applied, is fitted and centered inside its thumbnail rectangle without stretching. ``labels=True`` adds 22 pixels below each rectangle for its one-based source page number, drawn with built-in 14-pixel decimal digits. Custom PDF page labels are not used. A rectangle too narrow for its number is rejected; ``labels=False`` removes the label band. ``background``, ``page_background`` and ``label_color`` are RGB byte triples for the sheet, page paper and digits. ``antialias`` follows :meth:`render_page` (boolean or integer 1-8). Visible annotation appearances are included unless ``include_annotations=False``. The document's font substitution setting applies to thumbnails. Final sheet and supersampled thumbnail dimensions are checked against ``load_limits.max_raster_pixels`` before allocating the sheet. Pages are rendered one at a time at their fitted scale; unselected content is not read. Rendering coverage and limitations match ``render_page``. The returned ``RasterizedPage`` uses 72 DPI metadata; layout sizes are pixels and are independent of source page DPI.
attributes.signature: def render_contact_sheet(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, columns: int=4, thumbnail_size: tuple[int, int]=(160, 220), margin: int=12, spacing: int=12, labels: bool=True, background: tuple[int, int, int]=(240, 240, 240), page_background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), label_color: tuple[int, int, int]=(0, 0, 0), antialias: bool | int=True, include_annotations: bool=True) -> RasterizedPage

attributes.docstring: Render a page to an RGB raster image.
attributes.docstring_full: Render a page to an RGB raster image. ``page_index`` is one-based. The result can be encoded with :meth:`RasterizedPage.to_png`, :meth:`RasterizedPage.to_tiff`, :meth:`RasterizedPage.to_jpeg`, :meth:`RasterizedPage.to_webp`, or saved directly with :meth:`RasterizedPage.save`. ``antialias`` smooths edges by supersampling (``True`` = 3x, an integer 1-8 sets the factor, ``False`` disables it). ``shape_substitute_text`` (default on) joins complex-script runs drawn with a bundled substitute face; it needs the optional ``text-layout`` extra and only affects non-embedded fonts. ``draw_annotations`` (default on) composites each visible annotation's normal appearance over the page, the way a viewer shows it. ``font_substitution`` overrides :attr:`font_substitution` for this call. ``clip=(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` selects an area in unrotated PDF coordinates with a lower-left origin. Ordered corners and a positive intersection with the effective CropBox are required. Only that intersection is rasterized, with page rotation applied and page boxes preserved.
attributes.signature: def render_page(self, page_index: int, *, dpi: float=72.0, scale: float=1.0, background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, shape_substitute_text: bool=True, draw_annotations: bool=True, font_substitution: FontSubstitutionOptions | None=None) -> RasterizedPage

attributes.docstring: Render a one-based page inside pixel bounds, preserving its proportions.
attributes.docstring_full: Render a one-based page inside pixel bounds, preserving its proportions. ``size=(width, height)`` must contain positive integers. The effective CropBox, with page rotation applied, is fitted within those bounds. The result has the fitted dimensions, rounded up to whole pixels, without padding or stretching. Small pages may be enlarged. Return an RGB ``RasterizedPage`` with 72 DPI metadata, ready for ``.save()`` or the usual PNG/TIFF/JPEG/WebP encoders. White paper is used by default; ``background`` is an RGB byte triple. ``antialias`` defaults to 3x supersampling; use ``False`` or a factor from 1 to 8. Visible annotation appearances are included unless disabled. Document font substitution and ordinary rendering limitations apply. Rendering uses the fitted scale directly; no full-resolution page image is created first. Supersampled pixels obey ``max_raster_pixels`` before rendering starts, and normal content/image limits still apply. Only the requested page is decoded, including for streaming sources. The PDF's page boxes, content and rotation remain unchanged.
attributes.signature: def render_thumbnail(self, page_index: int, *, size: tuple[int, int]=(160, 220), background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, include_annotations: bool=True) -> RasterizedPage

attributes.docstring: Attempt to repair the PDF document.
Replace annotation contents patterns in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Replace annotation contents patterns in a single call. This method can be called with either a single pattern or multiple patterns. For a single pattern, use positional arguments: ``replace_annotation_contents(search, replacement, ...)`` For multiple patterns, pass a mapping as the first argument: ``replace_annotation_contents({search: replacement, ...}, ...)`` In single-pattern mode, strings match literal substrings unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds IGNORECASE. All occurrences are replaced in each annotation. Regex replacement strings support Python backreferences; literal replacements stay literal. In multiple-pattern mode, a mapping of search patterns to replacement strings is provided. This is more efficient than calling this method multiple times for each pattern. Parameters ---------- search_or_replacements Either a single search pattern (string or compiled regex), or a mapping of search patterns to replacement strings. replacement Replacement text for a single search pattern. Required when ``search_or_replacements`` is a single pattern. page_index One-based page number. If omitted and ``pages`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``pages``. pages Iterable of one-based page numbers to process. If omitted and ``page_index`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``page_index``. case_sensitive If ``True`` (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns that already have flags set. max_count Maximum replacements to perform. ``0`` (default) means unlimited for single-pattern mode, or shared across all patterns in multiple-pattern mode. regex If ``True``, string search patterns are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. dry_run If ``True``, perform all checks and count changes without modifying the document. Return the number of changes that would be made. Returns ------- int Total number of annotation contents modified. See Also -------- replace_text : Replace a single text pattern in page content. replace_texts : Replace multiple text patterns in page content. replace_link_urls : Replace a single link URL pattern. replace_link_urls_batch : Replace multiple link URL patterns. Examples -------- Replace a single annotation content pattern: >>> document.replace_annotation_contents("Old Co", "New Co") Replace multiple annotation contents in one call: >>> document.replace_annotation_contents({"Old Co": "New Co", "2023": "2024"}) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.replace_annotation_contents( ... re.compile(r"\d{4}"), "2024", regex=True ... ) Limit replacements and target specific pages: >>> document.replace_annotation_contents( ... "old", "new", ... pages=[1, 3], ... max_count=5 ... )
attributes.signature: def replace_annotation_contents(self, search_or_replacements: str | re.Pattern[str] | Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], str], replacement: str | None=None, *, page_index: int | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, dry_run: bool=False) -> int

attributes.docstring: Replace stored URLs in primary URI actions of Link annotations.
attributes.docstring_full: Replace stored URLs in primary URI actions of Link annotations. Strings match literal substrings unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds IGNORECASE. All occurrences are replaced in each URL. Regex replacement strings support Python backreferences; literal replacements stay literal. ``pages`` contains one-based page numbers; None selects all and repeats are inspected once. Return the number of distinct changed annotations, excluding no-op replacements. ``dry_run=True`` performs the same plan and checks without edits. Empty resulting URLs are rejected. Options, page indices, metadata and resource limits are checked before mutation; any failure preserves the previous annotations. Matching uses the stored URI spelling, without applying the catalog URI Base, URL normalization or network requests. Relative/custom-scheme and Unicode URIs are supported. Geometry, styling and other action fields are retained; shared actions are copied for each changed annotation. A matching annotation shared with an unselected page is refused to avoid changing it outside the requested selection. This edits primary /A URI actions only. Action Next chains, bookmarks, AA actions, widgets, catalog URI Base and plain page text are untouched. Page content, images, appearances and scripts are never decoded. Save to persist the edits. This is not URI validation or reachability checking; Python's regex engine has no execution timeout.
attributes.signature: def replace_link_urls(self, search: str | re.Pattern[str], replacement: str, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> int

attributes.docstring: Replace multiple URL patterns in Link annotations in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Replace multiple URL patterns in Link annotations in a single call. This is a convenience method that applies multiple URL replacements to the document. It is equivalent to calling :meth:`replace_link_urls` for each key-value pair in *replacements*, but more efficient as it performs a single scan of the annotation metadata. Parameters ---------- replacements A mapping of search patterns to replacement strings. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are the replacement text. pages One-based page numbers to process. ``None`` (default) processes all pages. Duplicates are processed once. Rejected page numbers raise an error. regex If ``True``, all string keys are treated as regular expressions. Compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys always use regex mode, regardless of this flag's value. case_sensitive If ``True`` (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns that already have flags set. dry_run If ``True``, perform all checks and count changes without modifying the document. Return the number of changes that would be made. Returns ------- int Total number of link annotations modified across all patterns. Each annotation is counted at most once, even if multiple patterns match its URL. Notes ----- The batch operation scans the document once and applies all patterns to each annotation's URL. If multiple patterns match the same URL, only the first matching pattern's replacement is applied. This preserves the same behavior as the single-pattern :meth:`replace_link_urls` for annotation sharing, resource limits, and error handling. Annotations shared with unselected pages are rejected. See Also -------- replace_link_urls : Replace a single URL pattern. Examples -------- Replace multiple domain patterns in one call: >>> document.replace_link_urls_batch( ... {"old.example.com": "new.example.com", "old-domain.com": "new-domain.com"} ... ) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.replace_link_urls_batch( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): "2024", "prod": "staging"} ... ) Limit replacements and target specific pages: >>> document.replace_link_urls_batch( ... {"v1": "v2"}, ... pages=[1, 2, 3], ... case_sensitive=False ... )
attributes.signature: def replace_link_urls_batch(self, replacements: Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, dry_run: bool=False) -> int

attributes.docstring: Replace existing text in simple page-content text-showing operands.
attributes.docstring_full: Replace existing text in simple page-content text-showing operands. When *page_index* is omitted, every page is scanned. ``max_count=0`` means unlimited. This is a conservative content-stream edit for simple ``Tj``/``TJ`` operands; it does not perform layout reflow. Returns the number of replacements made. A replacement containing right-to-left or complex-script characters is shaped (HarfBuzz + Unicode bidi): it reuses the run's own embedded font when that font already carries every shaped glyph, otherwise a shaping-capable *font* is embedded and the replacement drawn at the match position, using *layout* (a :class:`~aspose_pdf.text_layout.TextLayoutOptions`) for direction, script, and features. Reshaping needs the optional ``text-layout`` extra; without a usable path the edit raises rather than emit misshaped glyphs. With ``regex=True`` -- or a compiled :class:`re.Pattern` as *search*, which needs no flag -- the search is a regular expression and *replacement* becomes a **template**: ``\1`` and ``\g<name>`` expand to what each match captured, as :func:`re.sub` defines them. ``\d{3}-\d{2}- \d{4}`` finds a shape rather than a phrase, which is what redacting an account number or a date needs. The pattern is matched against one logical text run at a time -- the text the page paints as one -- so ``^`` and ``$`` anchor to the run and not to a line, and a match cannot reach across a break that starts a new run. A pattern that matches the empty string is ignored. An RTL phrase is found in its stored visual order only when searched for as a literal; a regular expression's source is grammar, not text, and is not reordered.
attributes.signature: def replace_text(self, search: str | re.Pattern[str], replacement: str, *, page_index: int | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, font: FontDescriptor | bytes | bytearray | str | Path | None=None, layout: TextLayoutOptions | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Replace multiple text patterns in a single call.
attributes.docstring_full: Replace multiple text patterns in a single call. This is a convenience method that applies multiple text replacements to the document. It is equivalent to calling :meth:`replace_text` for each key-value pair in *replacements*, but more efficient as it performs a single scan of the content streams. Parameters ---------- replacements A mapping of search patterns to replacement strings. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are the replacement text. page_index One-based page number. If omitted and ``pages`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``pages``. pages Iterable of one-based page numbers to process. If omitted and ``page_index`` is also omitted, all pages are processed. Cannot be used together with ``page_index``. case_sensitive If ``True`` (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns. max_count Maximum replacements to perform across all patterns. ``0`` (default) means unlimited. The count is shared across all patterns. regex If ``True``, all keys are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. font Optional font descriptor for shaping complex-script replacements. layout Optional layout options for complex-script replacements. Returns ------- int Total number of replacements made across all patterns. See Also -------- replace_text : Replace a single text pattern. redact_text : Remove matching text with an optional overlay. Examples -------- Replace multiple strings in one call: >>> document.replace_texts({"Old Co": "New Co", "2023": "2024"}) Use with regex patterns: >>> import re >>> document.replace_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): "2024", "Mr.": "Ms."}, ... regex=True ... ) Limit replacements and target specific pages: >>> document.replace_texts( ... {"old": "new"}, ... pages=[1, 3], ... max_count=5 ... )
attributes.signature: def replace_texts(self, replacements: Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], str], *, page_index: int | None=None, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, case_sensitive: bool=True, max_count: int=0, regex: bool=False, font: FontDescriptor | bytes | bytearray | str | Path | None=None, layout: TextLayoutOptions | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Give *pages* a new sheet size and scale their drawing onto it.
attributes.docstring_full: Give *pages* a new sheet size and scale their drawing onto it. The operation :meth:`Page.resize` performs, over a document: every page when none are named. A mixed-size document comes out uniform, each page scaled from whatever it was -- which is what printing a folder of drawings on one paper stock needs. ``mode`` is ``"fit"`` (keep the aspect ratio, even margin on the long side), ``"fill"`` (keep it, let the drawing run past the short side) or ``"stretch"`` (scale the axes apart to fill the sheet exactly). See :meth:`Page.resize`; setting :attr:`Page.size` changes the sheet and leaves the drawing where it was. Returns ------- int How many pages were resized.
attributes.signature: def resize_pages(self, size: Any, *, mode: str='fit', pages: Sequence[int] | None=None) -> int

attributes.docstring: Take out everything the document carries that is not what it shows.
attributes.docstring_full: Take out everything the document carries that is not what it shows. A PDF travels with more than its pages. Who wrote it and when, what tool made it and what that tool kept in its own private store, scripts a viewer runs the moment it opens, whole files embedded inside, layers switched off but still there, comments with a reviewer's name on them. Each of those is removable on its own; this is the one pass that goes through all of them and says what it took:: with Document("contract.pdf") as document: print(document.sanitize()) # removed 7 metadata entries, 1 scripts, 3 actions, 1 attachments document.save("contract-clean.pdf") What is removed, and what is left alone: metadata ``/Info`` (title, author, producer, dates), the XMP packet, and the ``/PieceInfo`` an editor keeps its working data in -- on the catalog and on every page. javascript The ``/Names /JavaScript`` tree, the open action when it *is* an action, the catalog's and every page's additional actions, and any action on an annotation or field that runs script, launches a file or sends data away. A link that opens a URL keeps working: that is what a link is for, and the annotation stays either way. attachments Embedded files, from the name tree and from the ``/AF`` entries that reach them from the catalog and the pages. hidden_layers Optional content is resolved once and for all, as :meth:`flatten_layers` does: content the current configuration hides is **deleted**, not merely switched off. comments Markup annotations -- notes, highlights, stamps, ink -- each of which carries an author and a date (12.5.6.2). links Link annotations. **Off** by default: a link is part of the document's content, and a dangerous action on one is already dealt with by *javascript*. forms The interactive form and its widgets. **Off** by default, since removing it takes the fields' values with it. To keep what the fields show while losing the interactivity, use :meth:`flatten`. What this does **not** touch is the page content: text stays text and images stay images. Text that must not be readable is :meth:`redact_text`'s job, not this one. Returns ------- SanitizationReport The counts of what was removed; ``bool(report)`` is ``False`` when the document carried none of it. Notes ----- The next :meth:`save` is a **full rewrite**, not an incremental one -- an appended revision would keep the unsanitized one in front of it in the same file, so everything removed would still be there to read. For the same reason a save after this breaks any signature the document carries, which is unavoidable: a signature attests to bytes that no longer exist.
attributes.signature: def sanitize(self, *, metadata: bool=True, javascript: bool=True, attachments: bool=True, hidden_layers: bool=True, comments: bool=True, links: bool=False, forms: bool=False) -> SanitizationReport

attributes.docstring: Save the document to a file path or a binary stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Save the document to a file path or a binary stream. Parameters ---------- destination : str, Path, or BinaryIO File system path *or* any writable binary stream (e.g. ``BytesIO``, an open file handle in binary mode, an HTTP response body, …). save_format : SaveFormat, DocFormat, HtmlSaveOptions, MarkdownSaveOptions, or None ``None`` (the default), ``SaveFormat.PDF`` or ``DocFormat.PDF`` write PDF. ``DocFormat.HTML``, ``DocFormat.MARKDOWN`` and ``DocFormat.SVG`` export through :meth:`save_as_html`, :meth:`save_as_markdown` and :meth:`save_as_svg` with their defaults; an ``HtmlSaveOptions`` or ``MarkdownSaveOptions`` passes its settings on, and one it cannot honour raises rather than being ignored. These need a path: an export may be several files. Placeholders such as ``SaveFormat.PPTX`` raise instead of writing a mislabelled PDF. overwrite : bool Only relevant when *destination* is a path. When ``False`` (the default) an existing file raises :exc:`FileExistsError` -- for an export, any of the files it would write, before it writes one. When ``True`` the file is replaced in one step -- the new bytes are staged beside it and renamed over it -- so a save that fails, for want of disk space or anything else, leaves it exactly as it was, including when it is the file this document was loaded from. incremental : bool or None ``None`` (the default) writes an incremental update when the file carries signatures that a rewrite would break -- its ``/SigFlags`` says *AppendOnly* (ISO 32000-1 12.7.2) or a field is signed -- and a full rewrite otherwise, so opening a signed document and saving it keeps its signatures valid. ``False`` asks for a full rewrite regardless, and logs a warning naming what it invalidates. When ``True``, write a byte-preserving incremental update: the original file bytes are emitted verbatim and only the objects added or modified since load are appended as a new revision chained through ``/Prev``. This keeps any existing digital signature valid and is efficient for small edits to large files. Requires a document that was loaded from an existing PDF (a document built from scratch falls back to a full write); encrypted or to-be-signed documents are rejected with :exc:`~aspose_pdf.exceptions.PdfSecurityException`. After text redaction, ``None`` and ``False`` always perform a full rewrite and ``True`` raises the same exception, since preserving any prior revision would also preserve the removed text. A redacted PDF written to a stream replaces its contents from offset zero and truncates the stream; nonseekable and append-mode outputs are refused. What :meth:`sign`, :meth:`add_ltv` and :meth:`add_document_timestamp` asked for is done here, each in a revision appended to the bytes the choice above produces; the document is then reloaded from the file it wrote. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining. Raises ------ UnsupportedFeatureException If *save_format* names an export this package does not implement. Nothing is written to *destination* in that case.
attributes.signature: def save(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO, save_format: Any=None, *, overwrite: bool=False, incremental: bool | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Write the document as HTML and return the HTML files written.
attributes.docstring_full: Write the document as HTML and return the HTML files written. One file by default. ``split_into_pages`` writes ``name-1.html``, ``name-2.html`` … instead, one per page. Figures are embedded as ``data:`` URIs unless *resources_directory* is given: then each distinct image is written there once, as ``name-image-1.png`` and so on, and the HTML links to it by a relative URL. A relative *resources_directory* is taken from the folder the HTML goes to. *embed_images* ``False`` leaves figures out altogether (their alternate text stays). *paragraph_gap* and *clip_to_page* are as for :meth:`to_html`. With *overwrite* ``False`` an export any of whose files exists is refused before anything is written. Each file is written atomically.
attributes.signature: def save_as_html(self, destination: str | Path, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, title: str | None=None, embed_images: bool=True, split_into_pages: bool=False, resources_directory: str | Path | None=None, paragraph_gap: float | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True, overwrite: bool=True) -> list[Path]

attributes.docstring: Write the document as one Markdown file and return its path.
attributes.docstring_full: Write the document as one Markdown file and return its path. Figures are embedded as ``data:`` URIs unless *image_directory* is given: then each distinct image is written there once and linked by a relative URL, as :meth:`save_as_html` does with its *resources_directory*. *markdown_format*, *paragraph_gap* and *clip_to_page* are as for :meth:`to_markdown`; *overwrite* is as for :meth:`save_as_html`.
attributes.signature: def save_as_markdown(self, destination: str | Path, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, title: str | None=None, embed_images: bool=True, image_directory: str | Path | None=None, markdown_format: str='GFM', paragraph_gap: float | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True, overwrite: bool=True) -> Path

attributes.docstring: Write pages as SVG and return the files written.
attributes.docstring_full: Write pages as SVG and return the files written. SVG has no notion of a multi-page document, so each page becomes its own file. One page writes exactly *destination*; several write ``name-1.svg``, ``name-2.svg`` … beside it, numbered by the page's position in the document rather than in *pages*, so the file names still say which page they came from. See :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page.to_svg` for what the conversion does and does not turn into vectors, and for *text*, which chooses between glyph outlines and selectable ``<text>``. *overwrite* is as for :meth:`save_as_html`. Returns ------- list[Path] The files written, in the order the pages were selected.
attributes.signature: def save_as_svg(self, destination: str | Path, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, background: tuple[int, int, int] | None=(255, 255, 255), draw_annotations: bool=True, font_substitution: FontSubstitutionOptions | None=None, precision: int=3, text: str='outlines', overwrite: bool=True) -> list[Path]

attributes.docstring: Stream extracted text to a path or binary stream and return its byte count.
attributes.docstring_full: Stream extracted text to a path or binary stream and return its byte count. Text follows :meth:`iter_text_pages`. The separator is placed only between selected occurrences, including empty pages; ``"\f"`` uses a form feed, and ``""`` joins without a separator. Encoding is incremental, with one BOM where applicable. An empty selection writes the chosen encoding's representation of an empty string. Page text and total output sizes obey the document's resource limits. IDNA, Punycode and binary-to-binary codecs are not supported as TXT encodings. File output is staged beside the target and replaced atomically after success; extraction, encoding or write failures leave existing files intact. Parent folders are created as needed. ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing paths before extraction. Binary streams receive bytes at their current position, retry short writes, remain open, and can retain a prefix if a later page or write fails. Text streams are refused. No full-document text string or complete encoded output is accumulated; use :meth:`open_streaming` to avoid eager input content caches too.
attributes.signature: def save_as_text(self, destination: str | Path | BinaryIO, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, skip_artifacts: bool=False, exclude_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None, page_separator: str='\n', encoding: str='utf-8', overwrite: bool=True) -> int

attributes.docstring: Render pages into a single multi-page TIFF file.
attributes.docstring_full: Render pages into a single multi-page TIFF file. The bytes are :meth:`to_tiff`'s; this writes them to *destination*. Returns ------- Path The path written.
attributes.signature: def save_as_tiff(self, destination: str | Path, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, scale: float=1.0, background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, mode: str='rgb', compression: str='deflate', threshold: int=128, dither: bool=False) -> Path

attributes.docstring: Save a contact sheet as PNG, TIFF, JPEG or optional WebP.
attributes.docstring_full: Save a contact sheet as PNG, TIFF, JPEG or optional WebP. Layout options follow :meth:`render_contact_sheet`. Encoding options follow :meth:`RasterizedPage.save`; the destination suffix chooses the format, with ``.png`` added when absent. PNG, TIFF and JPEG need no optional dependencies; WebP requires the ``images`` extra. The encoded file replaces the destination atomically, after successful rendering and encoding. Return the resulting path.
attributes.signature: def save_contact_sheet(self, destination: str | Path, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, columns: int=4, thumbnail_size: tuple[int, int]=(160, 220), margin: int=12, spacing: int=12, labels: bool=True, background: tuple[int, int, int]=(240, 240, 240), page_background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), label_color: tuple[int, int, int]=(0, 0, 0), antialias: bool | int=True, include_annotations: bool=True, mode: str='rgb', compression: str='deflate', quality: int=85, threshold: int=128, lossless: bool=False, method: int=4, dither: bool=False) -> Path

attributes.docstring: Render one page and save it as PNG, TIFF, JPEG or WebP.
attributes.docstring_full: Render one page and save it as PNG, TIFF, JPEG or WebP. The format follows the suffix of *destination*. ``mode`` selects ``"rgb"``, ``"gray"`` or ``"bilevel"`` output, ``compression`` applies to TIFF and ``quality`` to JPEG/WebP. ``lossless`` and ``method`` apply to WebP, which requires the optional ``images`` extra. ``dither`` applies Floyd-Steinberg dithering when ``mode`` is ``"bilevel"``. ``clip`` selects a region as described in :meth:`render_page`.
attributes.signature: def save_page_as_image(self, page_index: int, destination: str | Path, *, dpi: float=72.0, scale: float=1.0, background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, mode: str='rgb', compression: str='deflate', quality: int=85, threshold: int=128, lossless: bool=False, method: int=4, dither: bool=False) -> Path

attributes.docstring: Save the document to a binary stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Save the document to a binary stream. This is a convenience method equivalent to ``save(stream, ...)``, provided for clarity when saving to in-memory streams such as ``io.BytesIO``. Parameters ---------- stream : BinaryIO Any writable binary stream (e.g., ``BytesIO``, an open file handle in binary mode). save_format : SaveFormat, DocFormat, HtmlSaveOptions, MarkdownSaveOptions, or None ``None`` (the default), ``SaveFormat.PDF`` or ``DocFormat.PDF`` write PDF. Other formats require a file path and raise ``PdfValidationException`` for streams. incremental : bool or None See :meth:`save` for full details. When ``True``, write a byte-preserving incremental update; requires a document loaded from an existing PDF. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If *save_format* specifies HTML, Markdown, or SVG (these exports generate multiple files and need a file path). Notes ----- For redacted documents written to a stream, the entire contents are replaced from offset zero and the stream is truncated. Non-seekable and append-mode outputs are refused. Examples -------- :: from io import BytesIO # Save to an in-memory buffer buffer = BytesIO() document.save_to_stream(buffer) pdf_bytes = buffer.getvalue() # Save with incremental update with open("source.pdf", "rb") as f: doc = Document(f) doc.add_header("Confidential") doc.save_to_stream(buffer, incremental=True)
attributes.signature: def save_to_stream(self, stream: BinaryIO, save_format: Any=None, *, incremental: bool | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Return detached matches with page-local offsets, context and geometry.
attributes.docstring_full: Return detached matches with page-local offsets, context and geometry. Strings are literal unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds Python's IGNORECASE semantics. Literal occurrences may overlap; regex matches follow ``re.finditer``. Zero-length matches are omitted. Empty patterns are rejected. ``context_chars`` is a non-negative character count on each side, cut at the page boundary. Offsets index the page's extracted Unicode text, not PDF bytes. ``rect`` and ``quads`` use unrotated PDF coordinates and are None when placement cannot be established reliably, as with TextFragmentAbsorber. Matches without geometry remain in the report. One-based ``pages`` preserves order and repeats. All options/selections are checked before extraction. Only selected pages are read, without filling document-wide text/content caches. Search follows ordinary text extraction, including hidden-layer filtering and logical replacements; it does not OCR images or search annotation/form values. Results obey load limits and survive source edits/disposal without changing the PDF.
attributes.signature: def search_text(self, pattern: str | re.Pattern[str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, context_chars: int=40) -> list[TextSearchMatch]

attributes.docstring: Return search results for multiple patterns with context and geometry.
attributes.docstring_full: Return search results for multiple patterns with context and geometry. This is a batch version of :meth:`search_text`. It performs the same pattern matching for each pattern, returning matches with page-local character offsets, context, and geometry. Use this when you need to know *what* matched for each pattern along with where and how it appeared. The search is efficient: the document is scanned only once, and results are collected for all patterns in a single pass. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are ignored and present only to allow clear labeling in the caller's code. The result dictionary preserves the key order from the input mapping. Strings are literal unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds Python's IGNORECASE semantics. Literal occurrences may overlap; regex matches follow ``re.finditer``. Zero-length matches are omitted. Empty patterns are rejected. ``context_chars`` is a non-negative character count on each side, cut at the page boundary. Offsets index the page's extracted Unicode text, not PDF bytes. ``rect`` and ``quads`` use unrotated PDF coordinates and are None when placement cannot be established reliably, as with TextFragmentAbsorber. Matches without geometry remain in the report. One-based ``pages`` preserves order and repeats. All options/selections are checked before extraction. Only selected pages are read, without filling document-wide text/content caches. Search follows ordinary text extraction, including hidden-layer filtering and logical replacements; it does not OCR images or search annotation/form values. Results obey load limits and survive source edits/disposal without changing the PDF. Args: patterns: A mapping of search patterns to names. Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are labels used in the result. pages: One-based page numbers, or None for all pages. regex: Treat all string patterns as regular expressions (default: False). case_sensitive: Match case exactly (default: True). context_chars: Number of context characters before and after each match (default: 40). Returns: A dictionary mapping each pattern key to a list of :class:`TextSearchMatch` instances in page order. Empty lists for patterns with no matches. Example: >>> results = document.search_texts( ... {"invoice": "inv", "amount": "amt"}, ... context_chars=20 ... ) >>> # results is {"invoice": [TextSearchMatch(...), ...], "amount": [...]} >>> import re >>> results = document.search_texts( ... {re.compile(r"\d{4}"): "year", re.compile(r"\d{2}"): "number"}, ... regex=True ... )
attributes.signature: def search_texts(self, patterns: Mapping[str | re.Pattern[str], str], *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, context_chars: int=40) -> dict

attributes.docstring: Sign the document when it is next saved.
attributes.docstring_full: Sign the document when it is next saved. A signature covers the bytes of a file, so it is made by :meth:`save`: the document is written as it would be anyway -- as an incremental update when it already carries signatures, which keeps them valid -- and the signature goes into an appended revision of its own. Signing, :meth:`add_ltv` and :meth:`add_document_timestamp` happen in the order they were called. After the save the document is the file it wrote: :attr:`signatures` lists the new signature and a later save appends to it. A :attr:`form` taken before that save lists the fields as they were; take it again. Parameters ---------- field : str, optional Fully qualified name of an unsigned signature field to fill, such as one made by :meth:`Form.add_signature_field`. When omitted, an invisible signature field (``Signature1``, or the next free number) is added to the first page. certificate, private_key : The signer: a ``cryptography`` ``x509.Certificate`` and its RSA, EC or Ed25519 private key; Ed25519 needs ``pades=True`` and digests with SHA-512 (RFC 8419). A PKCS#12 file loads with ``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs12.load_key_and_certificates``. extra_certificates : sequence of x509.Certificate Intermediate certificates to embed, so a validator can build the chain to a trusted root. reason, location, contact, signer_name : str, optional ``/Reason``, ``/Location``, ``/ContactInfo`` and ``/Name`` of the signature dictionary. pades : bool Write a CAdES signature (``ETSI.CAdES.detached``, PAdES baseline B) instead of ``adbe.pkcs7.detached``. A timestamp makes it PAdES-T. timestamp_url : str, optional RFC 3161 timestamp authority to embed a signature timestamp from. timestamp_authority : (x509.Certificate, RSA private key), optional A local timestamp authority, for closed environments and tests. timestamp_timeout : float Seconds to wait for *timestamp_url*. certify : CertificationLevel or int, optional Make this a certifying (DocMDP) signature permitting no changes (1), form filling (2), or form filling and annotations (3). It has to be the document's first signature. appearance : SignatureAppearance, optional Make the signature **visible**: draw who signed, when, why and where -- and an image, if one is given -- into the field's widget. Without it the signature shows whatever the field already showed, which for a field this library authored is an empty box and for a field it added itself is nothing at all. The appearance is drawn into the document *before* it is serialized, so the signature covers it: it cannot be replaced without breaking the signature. Its name line is *signer_name*, or the common name in *certificate* when that is not given, and its date is the moment of the save. Signing a field that exists draws into that field's widget, so the field says where the appearance goes. With no *field*, give the appearance a ``page`` and ``rect`` and the field is added there; an appearance with neither is refused, since the invisible field that would otherwise be added has no area to draw in. Returns ------- Document Self for method chaining. Raises ------ TypeError If the certificate, key or another argument has the wrong type. PdfValidationException If *field* does not name a signature field, the key does not belong to the certificate, or an argument is out of range. PdfSecurityException If *field* is signed already, a certification is asked for on a signed document, or the document is being encrypted for certificate recipients -- it could not be reopened after the save.
attributes.signature: def sign(self, field: str | None=None, *, certificate: Any, private_key: Any, extra_certificates: Sequence[Any]=(), reason: str | None=None, location: str | None=None, contact: str | None=None, signer_name: str | None=None, pades: bool=False, timestamp_url: str | None=None, timestamp_authority: tuple[Any, Any] | None=None, timestamp_timeout: float=10.0, certify: CertificationLevel | int | None=None, appearance: SignatureAppearance | None=None) -> Document

attributes.docstring: The digital signatures in the document, in the order the file holds them.
attributes.docstring_full: The digital signatures in the document, in the order the file holds them. Each is a :class:`~aspose_pdf.signature.PdfSignature` read from its signature field: ``valid`` checks it, ``validate()`` reports trust, certification and PAdES level. A document built here, or one that carries none, has an empty list. What the signatures do not cover is :class:`~aspose_pdf.forms.UnsignedContentAbsorber`'s to report, and whether anything after them looks like tampering is :class:`~aspose_pdf.security.SignaturesCompromiseDetector`'s.

attributes.docstring: Split a scan batch into independent parts using visibly blank pages.
attributes.docstring_full: Split a scan batch into independent parts using visibly blank pages. With ``keep_separators=False`` (default), discard blank pages from the outputs and return each nonblank run as one part. Leading, trailing and consecutive blank pages do not create empty or blank-only parts. With ``keep_separators=True``, attach each separating blank run to the preceding part, keeping leading blanks in the first part. Every source page then appears exactly once. An entirely blank document returns [] by default, or one full copy when keeping separators; an empty document always returns []. A document without blank pages returns one copy. Detection follows :meth:`find_blank_pages`: white paper, antialiasing disabled, finite positive ``dpi``, byte ``white_threshold`` (1-255) and tolerated ink fraction ``max_ink_ratio`` (0-1). Visible annotations and form appearances count unless ``include_annotations=False``. CropBox, rotation, layer visibility and font substitution follow the renderer. Image-only scans work without OCR. Tiny or faint marks, scan borders and unsupported graphics are subject to the renderer's limitations. Blank-looking pages can still contain hidden text or other data. Options and page-count limits are checked first. All pages are scanned one at a time before any part is imported, without filling all-page content/text caches. Results follow :meth:`extract_pages`: retain Info metadata, page resources, boxes, labels, annotations, fields, layers, tags and relevant bookmarks, including live edits and promoted children of excluded parents. Local links are remapped by the page importer; targets outside a part cannot remain valid local page targets. Document-level attachments are not copied. Parts are independent, inherit resource limits, and start without source encryption or valid source signatures. Dispose every returned document when done. Neither the source nor its files are edited. Rendering/import errors propagate, with partial results disposed and the source outline model restored. This operation copies whole pages; it does not erase data from the original PDF or clear hidden data on pages retained in outputs.
attributes.signature: def split_by_blank_pages(self, *, keep_separators: bool=False, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, max_ink_ratio: float=0.0, include_annotations: bool=True) -> list[Document]

attributes.docstring: Return independent chapter documents using bookmarks at ``level``.
attributes.docstring_full: Return independent chapter documents using bookmarks at ``level``. Level 1 selects root bookmarks. Local page destinations, named destinations and GoTo actions are resolved as they stand now; headings, external actions and unresolved targets do not start chapters. Starts are sorted by page, with one output per distinct start page. The first bookmark in outline order supplies the title when several share a page. Each chapter ends before the next start, or at the end of the PDF. Pages before the first start become a ``Preamble`` document unless ``include_preamble=False``. No usable bookmarks at the requested level raises ``PdfValidationException``. The source is unchanged. Results follow :meth:`extract_pages`, with their Info ``Title`` set to the chapter's bookmark title. Relevant nested bookmarks are retained even when an ancestor points outside the chapter. Dispose every result when done. Splitting imports whole pages, not parts between headings on one page; it does not execute bookmark actions. These new documents do not inherit encryption or preserve existing signature validity.
attributes.signature: def split_by_bookmarks(self, level: int=1, *, include_preamble: bool=True) -> list[Document]

attributes.docstring: Return independent parts starting at pages whose form field value matches.
attributes.docstring_full: Return independent parts starting at pages whose form field value matches. Splits the document into multiple parts based on the values of a specified form field. Each unique field value (or matching pattern) creates a boundary between parts. The field's widgets may appear on any subset of pages; the field's value is shared across all widgets of that field. ``field_name`` is the fully qualified field name (e.g., ``"Vendor"`` or ``"Address.Country"`` for nested fields). Use :attr:`Form.keys()` to list available fields. ``pattern`` restricts boundaries to pages where the field value matches. A string is a literal substring unless ``regex=True``. Compiled regular expressions always use regex matching and keep their flags; ``case_sensitive=False`` adds ``re.IGNORECASE``. ``None`` (default) matches any field value and creates a boundary whenever the value changes. Matching is a search anywhere in the field's string representation. Field values are converted to text: checkbox ``True`` becomes ``"True"``, choice field selections are joined with newlines, etc. Zero-width matches count. Patterns cannot be empty. A matching page starts a new part, ending before the next matching page or at the end of the PDF. Multiple matches on one page give one boundary. Leading pages become a separate part unless ``include_preamble=False``. No matches, including an empty document, raises ``PdfValidationException``. Pages are never split internally. Forms are read without decoding page content. The field's value is taken from the field's ``/V`` entry; widget annotations are not rendered. Streaming inputs are scanned one page at a time without filling the full document text or content caches. Python's regex engine has no execution timeout; use patterns appropriate for the input. Results follow :meth:`extract_pages`, retaining source Info metadata and relevant bookmarks, including live edits and children whose parents point outside the part. Neither the source nor its files are changed. Dispose each returned document when done. Partial results are disposed on failure. New parts do not inherit source encryption or retain the validity of existing digital signatures.
attributes.signature: def split_by_field_value(self, field_name: str, *, pattern: str | None=None, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, include_preamble: bool=True) -> list[Document]

attributes.docstring: Return independent parts starting at pages whose extracted text matches.
attributes.docstring_full: Return independent parts starting at pages whose extracted text matches. A string is a literal substring unless ``regex=True``. Compiled text regular expressions always use regex matching and keep their flags; ``case_sensitive=False`` adds ``re.IGNORECASE``. Matching is a search anywhere in each page's extracted text, with Python's regex semantics. Zero-width regex matches count. Patterns cannot be empty. ``clip=(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` restricts boundary detection to glyphs whose font-metric bounds overlap that rectangle, as in :meth:`Page.extract_text`. Coordinates are unrotated PDF points with a lower-left origin, independent of CropBox and page rotation. The same rectangle applies to every page and is validated before scanning. Characters without reliable geometry are omitted in this mode. ``None`` searches full page text. Only boundary detection is filtered. Parts retain whole pages, including text and graphics outside the rectangle. A matching page starts a new part, ending before the next matching page or at the end of the PDF. Multiple matches on one page give one boundary. Leading pages become a separate part unless ``include_preamble=False``. No matches, including an empty document, raises ``PdfValidationException``. Pages are never split internally. Uses ordinary text extraction, including its line breaks, hidden OCR text and limitations; image-only scans need an existing text layer. Matches cannot span pages. Annotations and form values are not searched. Streaming inputs are scanned one page at a time without filling the full-document text or content caches. Python's regex engine has no execution timeout; use patterns appropriate for the input. Results follow :meth:`extract_pages`, retaining source Info metadata and relevant bookmarks, including live edits and children whose parents point outside the part. Neither the source nor its files are changed. Dispose each returned document when done. Partial results are disposed on failure. New parts do not inherit source encryption or retain the validity of existing digital signatures.
attributes.signature: def split_by_text(self, pattern: str | re.Pattern[str], *, regex: bool=False, case_sensitive: bool=True, include_preamble: bool=True, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None) -> list[Document]

attributes.docstring: Return independent documents containing at most ``pages_per_part`` pages.
attributes.docstring_full: Return independent documents containing at most ``pages_per_part`` pages. The size must be a positive integer. Parts retain source page order, with a shorter final part when necessary. Every page appears once; blank pages count normally. Empty documents return an empty list. A size at least as large as the PDF produces one independent copy. Results follow :meth:`extract_pages`: retain Info metadata, resources, page geometry, labels, annotations, form fields, layers and tags. Relevant bookmarks retain live edits and destination views; children of excluded parents are promoted. Document attachments are not copied, and new parts do not inherit source encryption or signature validity. No text extraction or rendering is needed. Streaming sources remain lazy while whole pages are imported one part at a time. Options and result/selection limits are checked before importing; each part inherits the source resource policy. The source and its files are unchanged. Dispose every returned document when done. Partial results are disposed and the source outline model is restored if splitting fails.

attributes.docstring: Return a new PDF with selected pages replaced by a uniform tile grid.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a new PDF with selected pages replaced by a uniform tile grid. Positive integer ``rows`` and ``columns`` divide the displayed CropBox, respecting page rotation. ``order='row'`` reads left to right, top row first; ``'column'`` reads top to bottom, left column first. A nonnegative ``gutter`` leaves equal gaps between cells, in page coordinate units. Unselected pages retain source order; repeats split a page once, ``[]`` copies the PDF and an empty source returns an empty document. Tiles keep source coordinates, rotation and vector/text/image content, with all page boxes set to the cell at PDF writer precision. Cropping hides content rather than erasing it; this does not perform redaction. Non-widget annotations are independently copied with unchanged geometry. Selected widgets are flattened by default; unsupported/hidden widgets, or ``flatten_fields=False`` with widgets, raise before returning output. Metadata, attachments, labels, layers, links and bookmarks follow :meth:`split_spreads`. Each tile keeps its source label. Destinations to a tiled page point to its first tile, with their original views. Tile-specific structure associations are not rebuilt. The result is independent and unencrypted; source signatures cannot remain valid. All options, selections, output counts and cell geometry are checked before import. Source and output resource limits apply, streaming source caches stay lazy, and failures dispose the partial output. Neither the source PDF nor its files or live outline edits are changed.
attributes.signature: def split_grid(self, rows: int=2, columns: int=2, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, order: str='row', gutter: float=0.0, flatten_fields: bool=True) -> Document

attributes.docstring: Return independent documents, one for each page.
attributes.docstring_full: Return independent documents, one for each page. The document is split into single-page parts in source order. Every page appears exactly once. An empty document returns an empty list. Results follow :meth:`extract_pages`: retain Info metadata, page resources, boxes, labels, annotations, form fields, layers and tags. Relevant bookmarks retain live edits and destination views; children of excluded parents are promoted. Document attachments are not copied, and new parts do not inherit source encryption or signature validity. No text extraction or rendering is needed. Streaming sources remain lazy while whole pages are imported one part at a time. Options and result/selection limits are checked before importing; each part inherits the source resource policy. The source and its files are unchanged. Dispose every returned document when done. Partial results are disposed and the source outline model is restored if splitting fails.

attributes.docstring: Return a new PDF with each selected spread replaced by two page views.
attributes.docstring_full: Return a new PDF with each selected spread replaced by two page views. ``pages`` selects one-based source pages to split; other pages stay in source order. Repeats are split once and an empty selection copies the document. ``layout='horizontal'`` reads left then right in the displayed view; ``'vertical'`` reads top then bottom. ``reverse=True`` reverses each pair. CropBox and rotation determine the displayed view. ``split_ratio`` positions the cut from the left/top, strictly between zero and one. ``gutter`` removes a centered strip in page coordinate units; it must leave two positive regions. Both halves retain source coordinates and rotation, with all page boxes set to their regions. Content, fonts and images are copied without rasterization. Cropping does not remove hidden text/drawing or perform redaction. Non-widget annotations are copied to both halves with independent local reply and popup links; their geometry is not moved or trimmed. Selected form widgets are flattened before splitting by default; unsupported/hidden widgets or ``flatten_fields=False`` with widgets raise an exception. Fields on unselected pages remain interactive. Info metadata, attachments, layers, labels and destinations follow the shared page importer. Each half inherits its source label. Destinations to split pages retain the first output half and their existing view coordinates. New half-page structure associations are not rebuilt. Results are independent, unencrypted and cannot retain source signature validity. The source PDF and live outline edits are not changed. Source and output resource limits apply; failures dispose the partial result.
attributes.signature: def split_spreads(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, layout: str='horizontal', reverse: bool=False, split_ratio: float=0.5, gutter: float=0.0, flatten_fields: bool=True) -> Document

attributes.docstring: The document's subject, the ``/Info`` ``/Subject`` entry, or ``None``.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's subject, the ``/Info`` ``/Subject`` entry, or ``None``. Assign text to set it, or ``None`` to remove the entry. The value lives in the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`).

attributes.docstring: Synchronise the ``/Info`` dictionary and the XMP metadata packet.
attributes.docstring_full: Synchronise the ``/Info`` dictionary and the XMP metadata packet. The standard document properties are kept consistent between the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`) and the XMP packet (:attr:`xmp_metadata`) — ``Title``/``Author``/``Subject``/``Keywords``/ ``Creator``/``Producer``/``CreationDate``/``ModDate`` map to ``dc:title``/``dc:creator``/``dc:description``/``pdf:Keywords``/ ``xmp:CreatorTool``/``pdf:Producer``/``xmp:CreateDate``/ ``xmp:ModifyDate`` (PDF dates are converted to/from ISO-8601). Keeping the two in sync is required for PDF/A conformance. *direction* selects which side is authoritative: * ``"info_to_xmp"`` (default) — copy ``/Info`` values into the XMP packet (overwriting the mapped XMP properties). * ``"xmp_to_info"`` — copy the mapped XMP properties into ``/Info``. Both date properties are typed, so a value that is not a date in the source format is **not copied**: it is left where it is and logged, rather than written into the other side as text it cannot hold. Dates that do convert keep their precision — ``D:2026`` becomes ``2026``, not ``2026-01-01``, since both formats truncate from the right. Returns ``self`` for chaining; changes persist on :meth:`save`.

attributes.docstring: Get an editable view of the document's tagged structure tree.
The document's title, the ``/Info`` ``/Title`` entry, or ``None``.
attributes.docstring_full: The document's title, the ``/Info`` ``/Title`` entry, or ``None``. Assign text to set it, or ``None`` to remove the entry:: document.title = "Quarterly report" The value lives in the ``/Info`` dictionary (:attr:`info`). Mirror the standard entries into the XMP packet with :meth:`sync_metadata` when the document carries one.

attributes.docstring: Return the document as PDF bytes.
attributes.docstring_full: Return the document as PDF bytes. This is a convenience method that returns the PDF content as bytes, equivalent to saving to a :class:`BytesIO` stream and calling ``getvalue()``, but more concise and efficient. It is the logical complement to the :meth:`from_bytes` class method, allowing you to round-trip a document through bytes without creating temporary files:: # Load, modify, and get bytes doc = Document.from_bytes(original_bytes) doc.pages.add() modified_bytes = doc.to_bytes() Parameters ---------- incremental : bool or None ``None`` (the default) writes an incremental update when the file carries signatures that a rewrite would break. ``False`` asks for a full rewrite regardless, and ``True`` forces an incremental update. Incremental updates require a document that was loaded from an existing PDF; a document built from scratch falls back to a full write. Encrypted or to-be-signed documents are rejected. Returns ------- bytes The PDF content of the document. Raises ------ PdfSecurityException If *incremental* is ``True`` and the document is encrypted or has pending signatures. Examples -------- :: # Basic usage with Document("input.pdf") as doc: doc.pages.add() pdf_bytes = doc.to_bytes() # Incremental save with Document("source.pdf") as doc: doc.add_header("Confidential") pdf_bytes = doc.to_bytes(incremental=True) Notes ----- The document must be closed with :meth:`dispose` or a context manager when you are finished with it, just like documents loaded from files.
attributes.signature: def to_bytes(self, *, incremental: bool | None=None) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Return the document's inferred structure as one HTML document.
attributes.docstring_full: Return the document's inferred structure as one HTML document. Headings, paragraphs, lists, tables and figures are inferred with the same layout analysis :meth:`auto_tag` uses, and the text is decoded the way :meth:`extract_text` decodes it. HTML has no page model, so pages are separated by a rule and read as one flow. *title* defaults to the document's own ``/Title``. *paragraph_gap* is the largest baseline-to-baseline step, in multiples of the font size, at which a line still continues the paragraph above it (``None``: 1.6, the layout analysis's own). With *clip_to_page* (the default), text and images anchored outside the page's visible area -- its crop box -- are left out, as no viewer shows them. This is a conversion to a *flowing document*, not a facsimile: exact positioning, colour and fonts are dropped. For a facsimile, use :meth:`save_as_svg`.
attributes.signature: def to_html(self, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, title: str | None=None, embed_images: bool=True, paragraph_gap: float | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True) -> str

attributes.docstring: Return the document's inferred structure as Markdown.
attributes.docstring_full: Return the document's inferred structure as Markdown. *markdown_format* is ``"GFM"`` (GitHub Flavored Markdown, the default) or ``"CommonMark"``, which has no tables: a table is written as the HTML block CommonMark passes through. See :meth:`to_html` for what the conversion carries over and for the other arguments.
attributes.signature: def to_markdown(self, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, title: str | None=None, embed_images: bool=True, markdown_format: str='GFM', paragraph_gap: float | None=None, clip_to_page: bool=True) -> str

attributes.docstring: Write the document to a binary stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Write the document to a binary stream. This is a convenience method equivalent to ``save(stream, ...)`` but named for symmetry with :meth:`from_stream`. It writes the PDF content to an in-memory buffer or any writable binary stream without closing it. Parameters ---------- stream : BinaryIO Any writable binary stream (e.g., ``io.BytesIO``, an open file handle in binary mode). incremental : bool or None ``None`` (the default) writes an incremental update when the file carries signatures that a rewrite would break. ``False`` asks for a full rewrite regardless, and ``True`` forces an incremental update. Incremental updates require a document that was loaded from an existing PDF; a document built from scratch falls back to a full write. Encrypted or to-be-signed documents are rejected. Returns ------- None The method writes to the stream directly and returns ``None``. Raises ------ PdfSecurityException If *incremental* is ``True`` and the document is encrypted or has pending signatures. Examples -------- :: from io import BytesIO # Basic usage - round-trip through bytes buffer = BytesIO() with Document("input.pdf") as doc: doc.pages.add() doc.to_stream(buffer) pdf_bytes = buffer.getvalue() # Incremental save to stream with Document("source.pdf") as doc: doc.add_header("Confidential") buffer = BytesIO() doc.to_stream(buffer, incremental=True) Notes ----- The stream is **not** closed after writing. You can continue to use it for additional operations after the method returns.
attributes.signature: def to_stream(self, stream: BinaryIO, *, incremental: bool | None=None) -> None

attributes.docstring: Return pages as SVG documents.
attributes.docstring_full: Return pages as SVG documents. SVG has no notion of a multi-page document, so each page becomes its own SVG document. Every page becomes one SVG document in the returned list, in the order given by *pages* (all pages, in document order, when omitted). See :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page.to_svg` for what the conversion does and does not turn into vectors, and for *text*, which chooses between glyph outlines and selectable ``<text>``. ``background`` paints an opaque page behind the content; pass ``None`` for a transparent SVG. ``precision`` is the number of decimal places coordinates are written with, trading file size against exactness. :meth:`save_as_svg` writes these SVG documents to files.
attributes.signature: def to_svg(self, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, background: tuple[int, int, int] | None=(255, 255, 255), draw_annotations: bool=True, font_substitution: FontSubstitutionOptions | None=None, precision: int=3, text: str='outlines') -> list[bytes]

attributes.docstring: Render pages into the bytes of one multi-page TIFF.
attributes.docstring_full: Render pages into the bytes of one multi-page TIFF. Every page becomes one image in the file, in the order given by *pages* (all pages, in document order, when omitted). Pages are rendered one at a time and encoded as they go, so only the compressed result accumulates rather than every raster at once. ``mode`` selects ``"rgb"``, ``"gray"`` or ``"bilevel"`` output and ``compression`` is ``"deflate"`` (the default) or ``"none"``. ``dither`` applies Floyd-Steinberg dithering when ``mode`` is ``"bilevel"``. :meth:`save_as_tiff` writes these bytes to a file. Every other export has both forms -- :meth:`to_html`, :meth:`to_markdown`, :meth:`to_svg`, :meth:`Page.to_svg`, :meth:`render_page` -- and this is TIFF's.
attributes.signature: def to_tiff(self, *, pages: Sequence[int] | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, scale: float=1.0, background: tuple[int, int, int]=(255, 255, 255), antialias: bool | int=True, mode: str='rgb', compression: str='deflate', threshold: int=128, dither: bool=False) -> bytes

attributes.docstring: Change one embedded file, keeping everything not named here.
attributes.docstring_full: Change one embedded file, keeping everything not named here. :meth:`add_attachment` *replaces* an attachment: re-adding a name to change its description drops the MIME type, the dates and the relationship it already had, because a fresh add supersedes whatever was read from the file. That leaves no way to edit one field, which is what this is for -- an argument left out is left alone:: document.update_attachment("notes.txt", description="Reviewed") *new_name* renames the attachment; it must not collide with another, since a rename that quietly replaced a different file would be worse than an error. Returns the resulting :class:`FileSpecification`, and raises :class:`KeyError` when the document has no such attachment -- a name that does not match is a typo, not a no-op.
attributes.signature: def update_attachment(self, name: str, *, new_name: str | None=None, content: bytes | None=None, mime: str | None=None, description: str | None=None, creation_date=None, mod_date=None, relationship: str | None=None, compress: bool | None=None) -> FileSpecification

attributes.docstring: Validate the PDF document.
Report broken local navigation without changing the document.
attributes.docstring_full: Report broken local navigation without changing the document. Inspect Link annotations on one-based ``pages`` (all by default), then bookmarks in preorder and named destination definitions. Repeated page selections are checked once, retaining their first occurrence. Both flags must be booleans; selection/options are validated before metadata reads. ``pages=[]`` still checks the enabled global sources. Return detached immutable :class:`LinkValidationIssue` values for missing targets, undefined names, missing/stale page references, invalid destinations/actions, conflicting Link Dest/A entries, cycles and malformed navigation containers. Check all eight standard destination views with their exact arities; only XYZ and FitH/V/BH/BV parameters may be null. XYZ zoom must be non-negative and FitR bounds increasing. Name lookup follows each source name/string representation's priority. Read current page identities and unsaved bookmark edits, including action Next chains. URI, remote-file, JavaScript and other non-GoTo actions are not executed or checked for reachability; their Next chains are still inspected. No page content or appearance stream is decoded. Parser/resource failures propagate under :attr:`load_limits`. This checks navigation targets, not full PDF conformance, link geometry, accessibility or exhaustive bookmark/name-tree structural correctness. A targetless bookmark is valid. No repairs are made.
attributes.signature: def validate_links(self, *, pages: Iterable[int] | None=None, include_outlines: bool=True, include_named_destinations: bool=True) -> list[LinkValidationIssue]

attributes.docstring: Validate the document against PDF/A standards (heuristic checks).
attributes.docstring_full: Validate the document against PDF/A standards (heuristic checks). This implementation performs partial, rule-of-thumb checks — not a full PDF/A validator. Use :attr:`PdfAValidationResult.is_heuristic` (always ``True`` here) and :attr:`PdfAValidationResult.HEURISTIC_VALIDATION_NOTICE` when building compliance automation. Parameters ---------- level : str PDF/A conformance level to check (e.g. ``"1b"``, ``"2b"``, ``"4"``). ISO 19005-4 has no accessible/basic/unicode split: its levels are ``"4"``, ``"4e"`` (engineering, which permits 3D and rich media) and ``"4f"`` (embedded files of any type). Returns ------- PdfAValidationResult Detailed result with ``errors``, ``warnings``, ``level``, ``is_heuristic``, and ``is_valid`` fields. ``len(result)`` equals ``len(result.errors)`` for backward-compatible usage.

attributes.docstring: Validate catalog-level PDF/UA prerequisites (heuristic).
attributes.docstring_full: Validate catalog-level PDF/UA prerequisites (heuristic). Checks for ``/StructTreeRoot``, ``/MarkInfo`` with ``/Marked true``, and emits a warning when ``/Lang`` is missing. This is **not** a full PDF/UA validator: use :attr:`PdfUaValidationResult.is_heuristic` and :attr:`PdfUaValidationResult.HEURISTIC_VALIDATION_NOTICE` when building compliance or accessibility automation. Parameters ---------- part : int ``1`` for ISO 14289-1 (the default) or ``2`` for ISO 14289-2, which is defined on PDF 2.0 and additionally requires an XMP ``pdfuaid:rev`` and structure types drawn from the PDF 2.0 standard structure namespace. Returns ------- PdfUaValidationResult ``errors``, ``warnings``, ``is_heuristic`` (default ``True``), and ``is_valid``. ``len(result)`` equals ``len(result.errors)``.
