attributes.docstring: Make PDFs from JPEG/PNG/TIFF/WebP/BMP/GIF images and animation frames.
attributes.docstring_full: Make PDFs from JPEG/PNG/TIFF/WebP/BMP/GIF images and animation frames. Each page is cut to its own picture unless ``page_size`` says otherwise, in which case the image is centred inside that sheet and scaled down to fit within the margin. By default all images and frames become pages of one document; with ``single_document=False`` each image becomes a document of its own. TIFF frames retain their source order, including eight-bit RGBA/LA transparency. GIF/WebP animations produce one page per composited frame, retaining alpha, blend and disposal results; durations and loops are not carried into the PDF. TIFF and WebP/BMP/GIF require the ``images`` extra. Set ``auto_orient=True`` to honor JPEG EXIF rotation and reflection without recompressing the JPEG or requiring Pillow.

attributes.docstring: Options for ImagesToPdf.
attributes.docstring_full: Options for :class:`ImagesToPdf`. ``page_size`` is a :class:`~aspose_pdf.page_size.PageSize`, one of its names, or a ``(width, height)`` pair; without one each page is cut to its own picture, which is what a scan or a photo set wants. ``dpi`` says how many pixels go to the inch when a page is cut to the image (and how large the image is drawn inside a fixed page): 72 is one point per pixel, 300 makes a 300 dpi scan come out at its physical size. ``margin`` is in points and applies to a fixed page size only -- a page cut to its image has no room for one -- and ``single_document`` collects every input into one file instead of one file per image. Each TIFF, GIF or WebP frame counts as one image. TIFF/WebP/BMP/GIF inputs require the optional ``images`` extra; WebP also needs Pillow's WebP codec. Animated GIF/WebP frames become full composited pages in display order, once per stored frame regardless of timing/loops. A numeric ``dpi`` overrides source resolution metadata. ``dpi="auto"`` uses each image/frame's absolute X/Y resolution, falling back to 72 DPI when no usable pair exists. Inch/cm units and PNG/BMP pixels per metre are supported. JPEG EXIF takes priority over JFIF; GIF uses the fallback. ``auto_orient=True`` applies all eight JPEG EXIF orientations, including reflections, when placing the original JPEG bytes without recompression. The default is ``False``. It affects JPEG only; TIFF already applies its own orientation. Missing JPEG orientation means upright; malformed EXIF raises :class:`~aspose_pdf.exceptions.PdfValidationException` when enabled.

attributes.docstring: The page size for output pages, or ``None`` to cut each page to its image.
attributes.docstring_full: The page size for output pages, or ``None`` to cut each page to its image. Reads go straight to the document, so the collection is never a stale copy: both places a PDF keeps these are read -- the ``/Names /Dests`` name tree (PDF 1.2 and later) and the older ``/Dests`` dictionary -- and a name the two disagree about reads as the dictionary's, which is the one a viewer resolves first. Assigning takes a :class:`~aspose_pdf.interactive.Destination`, or a page index as a shorthand for "fit that page":: document.destinations["cover"] = 0 document.destinations["chapter-2"] = XYZDestination(page=7, top=760) del document.destinations["cover"]

attributes.docstring: Place an image on this page and return its resource name.
attributes.docstring_full: Place an image on this page and return its resource name. JPEG, PNG and explicit raw samples work without optional dependencies. Static BMP, GIF and WebP require the ``images`` extra; transparency is preserved, and animated inputs are rejected. Omitted display dimensions default to the corresponding pixel dimensions in PDF points. ``fit="stretch"`` (the default) scales each axis independently. ``fit="contain"`` preserves proportions and fits the entire image within ``(x, y, width, height)``, leaving unused space transparent. ``fit="cover"`` preserves proportions and clips the image to that frame. Both require positive finite width and height. ``anchor`` chooses its position: ``"center"`` (default), ``"top_left"``, ``"top"``, ``"top_right"``, ``"left"``, ``"right"``, ``"bottom_left"``, ``"bottom"`` or ``"bottom_right"``. For cover, it chooses the retained part of the image. Top/bottom follow the frame's current user space, before surrounding transforms or page rotation. Valid anchors have no effect with stretch. Invalid anchors raise ``PdfValidationException`` before reading image files or decoding pixels. Fitting changes placement only: source pixels and page boxes are preserved.
attributes.signature: def add_image(self, image: bytes | bytearray | str | Path, x: float, y: float, width: float | None=None, height: float | None=None, *, fit: str='stretch', anchor: str='center', pixel_width: int | None=None, pixel_height: int | None=None, color_space: str='DeviceRGB', bits_per_component: int=8, name: str | None=None, tag: str | None=None, alt: str | None=None, actual_text: str | None=None, artifact: bool | str | None=None) -> str

attributes.docstring: Draw *text_list* with the top-left of its measure at ``(x, y)``.
attributes.docstring_full: Draw *text_list* with the top-left of its measure at ``(x, y)``. Items are bulleted, or numbered with ``ordered=True``, and the marker sits in a gutter to the left of a body wrapped to the list's ``width`` -- or to the room between *x* and the right edge of the page. Sub-items are set in one step further and get the next depth's marker, with an ordered list's numbering restarting at each sub-list. A list taller than the room left **continues onto the next page**, adding a page like this one when there is none, and an item's marker always goes on the page its first line goes on. The result is tagged as the nested ``/L`` → ``/LI`` → ``/Lbl`` + ``/LBody`` that ISO 32000-1 asks for, with the ``/ListNumbering`` of Table 345 where the markers have a standard name -- so a reader that cannot see the glyphs still knows an ordered list from an unordered one. A list continued onto the next page stays one list. Pass ``tag=False`` to leave it untagged. Returns ``{"pages": [...], "bottom": y, "items": n}``: the pages drawn on, where the list ended, and how many items were placed -- so the next thing on the page knows where to go.
attributes.signature: def add_list(self, text_list: TextList, x: float, y: float, *, bottom_margin: float=36.0, tag: bool=True) -> dict[str, Any]

attributes.docstring: Put *stamp* on this page, over or under what it already draws.
attributes.docstring_full: Put *stamp* on this page, over or under what it already draws. See :mod:`aspose_pdf.stamps`: the stamp is placed inside the part of the page a reader shows, with the page's rotation undone so it stands upright.

attributes.docstring: Draw *table* with its top-left corner at ``(x, y)`` on this page.
attributes.docstring_full: Draw *table* with its top-left corner at ``(x, y)`` on this page. Cell text is wrapped to its column with the font's own advances, rows grow to hold what they are given, and a table taller than the room left **continues onto the next page** -- repeating the rows marked as headers, adding a page like this one when there is none to continue onto. Pass ``bottom_margin`` to say how much to leave at the foot of a page. The structure is tagged as it is drawn -- a ``/Table`` of ``/TR`` of ``/TH`` and ``/TD``, nested as ISO 32000-1 14.8.4.3 asks -- unless ``tag=False``. Returns ``{"pages": [...], "bottom": y, "rows": n}``: the pages drawn on, where the last row ended, and how many rows were placed -- so the next thing on the page knows where to go.
attributes.signature: def add_table(self, table: Table, x: float, y: float, *, bottom_margin: float=36.0, tag: bool=True) -> dict[str, Any]

attributes.docstring: Append positioned text to this page.
attributes.docstring_full: Append positioned text to this page. ``font_name`` selects the Standard-14 path. Pass ``font`` as a :class:`FontDescriptor`, bytes, bytearray, or filesystem path to embed and subset a Unicode Type0/CID font. Pass ``layout`` to enable OpenType shaping, bidirectional text, font fallback, wrapping, and alignment through :class:`~aspose_pdf.text_layout.TextLayoutOptions`. ``color`` is grey, RGB or CMYK: one, three or four components, a single number for grey, a ``"#rrggbb"`` string, or an :class:`~aspose_pdf.color.Color`. Grey and RGB channels may be 0..1 or 0..255; CMYK is 0..1. ``artifact`` marks this as **decoration** rather than content: ``True`` for a bare ``/Artifact``, or one of ``"Pagination"``, ``"Layout"``, ``"Page"`` to say which kind (ISO 32000-1 14.8.2.2). A tagged document needs every mark to be one or the other (ISO 14289-1 7.1), so a rule or a running head drawn by hand says so this way. Asking for an artifact *and* a tag is refused.
attributes.signature: def add_text(self, text: str, x: float, y: float, *, font_size: float=12.0, font_name: str | None=None, font: FontDescriptor | bytes | bytearray | str | Path | None=None, color: ColorValue=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), tag: str | None=None, actual_text: str | None=None, artifact: bool | str | None=None, layout: TextLayoutOptions | None=None) -> Page

attributes.docstring: Draw *block* with the top-left of its measure at ``(x, y)``.
attributes.docstring_full: Draw *block* with the top-left of its measure at ``(x, y)``. Text is wrapped to the block's ``width`` -- or to the room between *x* and the right edge of the page -- with the font's own advances, lines are aligned (``left``, ``center``, ``right`` or ``justify``), and a block taller than the room left **continues onto the next page**, adding a page like this one when there is none to continue onto. Pass ``bottom_margin`` to say how much to leave at the foot of a page. Unlike :meth:`add_text` with ``layout=TextLayoutOptions(...)``, this needs no embedded font and no optional dependency: the standard 14 fonts are measured by their own advances. What it does not do is shape, so right-to-left and complex scripts still want that path. Paragraphs can set ``widow_lines`` and ``orphan_lines`` for minimum fragment lengths before and after page breaks, and ``keep_with_next`` to keep headings with following text. Impossible constraints are relaxed so every line stays within the page bounds. Each paragraph is tagged with its own structure type -- ``/P`` unless it says otherwise -- and a paragraph continued onto the next page stays one element. Pass ``tag=False`` to leave the text untagged. Returns ``{"pages": [...], "bottom": y, "lines": n}``: the pages drawn on, where the text ended, and how many lines were placed -- so the next thing on the page knows where to go.
attributes.signature: def add_text_block(self, block: TextBlock, x: float, y: float, *, bottom_margin: float=36.0, tag: bool=True) -> dict[str, Any]

attributes.docstring: Trim visible white margins by shrinking only this page's CropBox.
attributes.docstring_full: Trim visible white margins by shrinking only this page's CropBox. Render the current visible area on white paper at ``dpi`` without antialiasing. A pixel is ink if any RGB channel is below ``white_threshold`` (1-255). The outer ink pixel edges, mapped back to unrotated PDF coordinates, define the new crop. ``margin`` adds a finite nonnegative number of PDF points on each side, clamped to the current visible area. Visible annotations count unless explicitly excluded. Return this page for chaining. A blank-looking page is left unchanged. MediaBox, rotation, content and object coordinates are preserved; explicit production boxes are not rewritten. This changes visibility, not the stored content: cropped-out data remains in the PDF. Detection is approximate at the chosen DPI and shares the renderer's limitations, like :meth:`is_blank`. Tiny or faint marks may be missed; scan borders and dark speckles count as content. Rendering and resource limit failures propagate before any CropBox is changed.
attributes.signature: def auto_crop(self, margin: float=0.0, *, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, include_annotations: bool=True) -> Page

attributes.docstring_full: The page's ``/BleedBox`` -- what a production run clips the page to. ISO 32000-1 14.11.2. Falls back to the :attr:`crop_box` when the page does not state one, as the entry's default is; a stated box is reported intersected with the media box, since no production box extends beyond the sheet. Assigning ``None`` removes the entry. Unlike the media and crop boxes this one is **not inheritable**, so a value on a page-tree node is not this page's bleed box.

attributes.docstring: Compare this page visually with a page from another document.
attributes.docstring_full: Compare this page visually with a page from another document. Return a comparison result with changed pixel counts, difference ratio, and optional difference images. This is a convenience method that calls :meth:`Document.compare_visual` with this page as the only comparison. Parameters ---------- other The other document to compare against. Must be an open Document. other_page The one-based page index in the other document. ``None`` (default) compares against the first page. dpi Render at finite positive DPI for pixel-level comparison. Higher DPI reveals smaller differences at a higher cost. tolerance Integer 0-255 specifying how much RGB channel difference is allowed. Default 0 requires exact pixel equality. Increase to tolerate minor rendering differences. max_diff_ratio Float 0-1 specifying the maximum allowed difference ratio for a match. Default 0 requires exact equality. Increase to allow some differences. include_annotations Include visible annotations and form appearances in the comparison. Default is ``True``. include_diff_images Include a difference image in the result showing changed pixels in red over pale gray unchanged content. Default is ``False``. ignore_regions An iterable of ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` rectangles in PDF points to exclude from comparison. Pixels inside these regions are ignored. Default is ``None`` (no exclusions). Returns ------- PageVisualComparison A result object with pixel counts, difference ratio, bounding box of changes, match status, and optional difference image. See Also -------- Document.compare_visual : Compare multiple page pairs between documents. Examples -------- Compare this page with the first page of another document: >>> result = page.compare_visual(other_document) Compare with a specific page: >>> result = page.compare_visual(other_document, other_page=3) Allow some tolerance for minor rendering differences: >>> result = page.compare_visual( ... other_document, tolerance=10, max_diff_ratio=0.01 ... )
attributes.signature: def compare_visual(self, other: Document, *, other_page: int | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, tolerance: int=0, max_diff_ratio: float=0.0, include_annotations: bool=True, include_diff_images: bool=False, ignore_regions: Sequence[Sequence[float]] | None=None) -> PageVisualComparison

attributes.docstring: Append a GraphicsPath to this page.
attributes.docstring_full: Append a :class:`~aspose_pdf.paths.GraphicsPath` to this page. Build the path first -- lines, cubic curves, rectangles, ellipses, polygons -- then say how to paint it:: from aspose_pdf import GraphicsPath wedge = GraphicsPath().move_to(300, 400).line_to(400, 460).curve_to( 430, 470, 450, 440, 460, 410 ).close() page.draw_path(wedge, fill_color="#336699", stroke_color=(0, 0, 0)) ``stroke_color`` and ``fill_color`` take grey, RGB or CMYK (see :meth:`add_text`); ``None`` leaves that half of the paint out, and a path with neither is refused rather than written as an invisible operator. ``even_odd`` fills by the even-odd rule instead of the nonzero winding rule (ISO 32000-1 8.5.3.3), which is what decides whether a hole inside a shape is a hole. An :class:`~aspose_pdf.presentation.IPath` is accepted too, and its own ``fill_mode`` and ``transform`` are used for whichever of the two is not given here. The line is drawn with ``line_width``, ``line_cap`` (``"butt"``, ``"round"``, ``"square"``), ``line_join`` (``"miter"``, ``"round"``, ``"bevel"``), ``miter_limit`` and ``dash`` -- a sequence of on/off lengths, or ``(pattern, phase)``. ``opacity`` makes the whole drawing transparent, ``fill_opacity`` and ``stroke_opacity`` each half of it, and ``blend_mode`` is one of the sixteen of 11.3.5; the three are written as an ``/ExtGState``, and a state the page already has is reused rather than added again. ``transform`` is six numbers ``(a, b, c, d, e, f)`` -- or an :class:`~aspose_pdf.presentation.IMatrix` -- applied to this drawing only.

attributes.docstring: Return this page's annotations as CSV in a ZIP archive.
attributes.docstring_full: Return this page's annotations as CSV in a ZIP archive. Names are ``annotations-page-0001.csv``, ``annotations-page-0002.csv``, etc., following the requested one-based page order (including repeats). ``None`` selects all pages; ``[]`` selects none. Filters and snapshot IDs match :meth:`export_annotations_json`, including popups/widgets by default. Selected pages are read one at a time without decoding page content or appearance streams. CSV follows :meth:`export_annotations_csv`: columns are ``page_number`` (one-based), ``annotation_index`` (zero-based), ``id``, ``subtype``, ``author``, ``subject``, ``contents``, ``created``, ``modified``, ``in_reply_to``, ``popup`` and ``parent``. Quoting preserves Unicode, double quotes, delimiters and embedded newlines with CRLF records. ``encoding="utf-8-sig"`` adds a spreadsheet BOM; semicolon, tab and other single-character delimiters are supported. ZIP uses ``'deflate'`` (level 0..9) or ``'stored'``, fixed timestamps and regular-file permissions. Empty results produce a valid empty ZIP or a manifest with no pages. Selection, entry counts, annotation counts, member bytes and cumulative CSV/manifest bytes obey :class:`PdfLoadLimits`. The archive is completed before output is touched. Paths are written atomically with parent directories created; ``overwrite=False`` refuses existing files. Binary streams retry short writes at their current position and remain open; write failures can leave partial stream output. The source PDF is not edited. This is a convenience method that delegates to ``Document.export_annotations_zip`` with ``pages=[self.number]``.

attributes.docstring_full: Extract all images from this page. Returns a list of :class:`Image` objects, each containing the raw image data, resource name, size in bytes, and detected format (e.g., "png", "jpg"). The image bytes are the *decoded* sample bytes that the stream decoder produces, not the original encoded payload. To obtain the original bytes (e.g., a JPEG payload from a ``DCTDecode`` image), use the engine's :meth:`~aspose_pdf.engine.simple_pdf.SimplePdf.extract_images` directly. Returns ------- list[Image] A list of image objects. Empty if the page has no images.

attributes.docstring: The text this page says, with the line breaks it was written in.
attributes.docstring_full: The text this page says, with the line breaks it was written in. Text-positioning operators are what separate one line from the next, so the result keeps them; how those lines are grouped into paragraphs is a judgement :meth:`to_markdown` and :meth:`to_html` make and this does not. ``clip=(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` selects glyphs whose font-metric bounding boxes overlap a rectangle in unrotated PDF coordinates with a lower-left origin. Characters without reliable geometry are omitted in this mode. The rectangle is independent of the page's CropBox and rotation; it does not modify the PDF. ``None`` preserves ordinary full-page extraction. ``skip_artifacts=True`` omits explicitly marked ``/Artifact`` content, such as tagged page numbers and watermarks. It defaults to ``False``. ``exclude_regions`` is an iterable of rectangles in the same coordinate space, removing any overlapping glyphs, including untagged headers and footers. Exclusions take priority over ``clip``. All rectangles are validated before decoding; ``None`` and empty iterables do not filter. Gaps between retained pieces are separated to avoid merging words. Logical /ActualText replacements are omitted whole when any underlying glyph is excluded. Unmeasurable text is omitted conservatively, without raw-string recovery, as with ``clip``. This only filters returned text; it is not PDF redaction and never changes the document.
attributes.signature: def extract_text(self, *, clip: Sequence[float] | None=None, skip_artifacts: bool=False, exclude_regions: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None=None) -> str

Results retain this page's original one-based document number.

Each key is a finite, positive DPI threshold; each value is an identifier used in the result dictionary. See Also -------- find_low_resolution_images : Check images against a single threshold. find_texts : Find text for multiple patterns on this page.

Keys may be strings or compiled regex patterns; values are labels used in the result. regex: Treat all string patterns as regular expressions (default: False). case_sensitive: Match case exactly (default: True). Returns: A dictionary mapping each pattern key to a list of matched text strings in page order. Empty lists for patterns with no matches. Example: >>> results = page.find_texts({"Old": "old_name", "New": "new_name"}) >>> # results is {"Old": ["Old", "Old"], "New": ["New"]}

attributes.docstring: Create a new page from an image file, bytes, or stream.
attributes.docstring_full: Create a new page from an image file, bytes, or stream. The image is embedded as a full-page image at the specified or natural resolution. The page size is derived from the image dimensions unless *size* is given. Parameters ---------- document : Document The document to which the page will be added. image : str, Path, bytes, bytearray, or BinaryIO Image file path, raw bytes, bytearray, or a file-like object with a ``read()`` method (JPEG, PNG, BMP, GIF, WebP). size : PageSize, (width, height), or str, optional Page size to use instead of the image's natural size. A :class:`~aspose_pdf.page_size.PageSize`, its name, or a ``(width, height)`` pair in points. dpi : float, optional Resolution to use when deriving page size from image pixels. Default is 72 DPI (1 point = 1 pixel). fit : str, optional How to fit the image within the page. ``"cover"`` (default) scales the image to cover the entire page, cropping if necessary. ``"contain"`` scales the image to fit entirely within the page, preserving aspect ratio. ``"stretch"`` stretches the image to fill the page, potentially distorting it. Returns ------- Page The newly created page containing the image. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If the image data is invalid or the size is malformed. FileNotFoundError If the image path does not exist. OSError If the image file cannot be read. TypeError If the image is not a supported type or a file-like object's ``read()`` method does not return bytes or bytearray. Notes ----- JPEG and PNG work without optional dependencies. Static BMP, GIF, and WebP require the ``images`` extra. Animated GIFs are not supported. Examples -------- :: # From a file, page matches image size page = Page.from_image(doc, "photo.jpg") # From bytes with explicit A4 size with open("scan.png", "rb") as f: page = Page.from_image(doc, f.read(), size="A4") # From file-like object (e.g., BytesIO) from io import BytesIO page = Page.from_image(doc, BytesIO(image_data)) # From path with custom size in points page = Page.from_image(doc, "chart.jpg", size=(400, 600)) # Use fit mode to control image placement page = Page.from_image(doc, "photo.jpg", fit="contain")
attributes.signature: def from_image(cls, document: Document, image: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, *, size: PageSize | Sequence[float] | str | None=None, dpi: float=72.0, fit: str='cover') -> Page

attributes.docstring: Create a new page from a specific page in a PDF file.
attributes.docstring_full: Create a new page from a specific page in a PDF file. The specified page from the source PDF is imported into the target document. The page's content, resources, annotations, and other properties are preserved during the import. Parameters ---------- document : Document The document to which the page will be added. pdf_source : str, Path, bytes, bytearray, or BinaryIO PDF file path, raw bytes, bytearray, or a file-like object with a ``read()`` method. page_number : int, optional One-based page number to import from the source PDF. Default is 1. Returns ------- Page The newly created page containing the imported PDF content. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If the PDF data is invalid or the page number is out of range. FileNotFoundError If the PDF path does not exist. IndexError If the page_number exceeds the number of pages in the source PDF. TypeError If the pdf_source is not a supported type or a file-like object's ``read()`` method does not return bytes or bytearray. Notes ----- The source PDF is loaded temporarily during the import and closed afterwards. The imported page retains its original properties: content, annotations, form fields, layers, and page boxes. Examples -------- :: # From a file, uses page 1 by default page = Page.from_pdf(doc, "document.pdf") # From a specific page page = Page.from_pdf(doc, "report.pdf", page_number=3) # From bytes with open("source.pdf", "rb") as f: page = Page.from_pdf(doc, f.read(), page_number=2) # From file-like object (e.g., BytesIO) from io import BytesIO page = Page.from_pdf(doc, BytesIO(pdf_bytes), page_number=1)
attributes.signature: def from_pdf(cls, document: Document, pdf_source: str | Path | bytes | bytearray | BinaryIO, page_number: int=1) -> Page

attributes.docstring_full: The page box *boundary* names, with its default applied. Takes a :class:`~aspose_pdf.viewer_preferences.PageBoundary` -- the same enumeration the viewer preferences use to say which box to view or print -- so code holding one of those can ask for the geometry it names:: page.get_box(document.viewer_preferences.view_area)
attributes.signature: def get_box(self, boundary: PageBoundary | str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]

attributes.docstring: Measure visible ink without modifying this page or its boxes.
attributes.docstring_full: Measure visible ink without modifying this page or its boxes. Return ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` in unrotated PDF user coordinates with a lower-left origin, clamped to the effective CropBox. Return None when no ink is found. A full-bleed page returns its visible box. The tuple is detached and remains usable after the document is closed. Render on white paper without antialiasing at finite positive ``dpi``. A pixel is ink if any RGB channel is strictly below the integer ``white_threshold`` (1-255). Visible annotation and widget appearances count unless ``include_annotations=False``. Rotation, clipping, layer visibility and font substitution follow render(). Pixel edges are mapped back using DPI, not rounded raster dimensions. Coordinates are page user units; UserUnit is not applied separately by this helper. This is a visual heuristic, not exact object geometry or OCR. Tiny or faint marks may be missed; dark speckles and scan borders count as ink. Cropped-out or invisible stored data is not measured. Higher DPI costs more time and memory. Only this page is rendered, under resource limits; parser/render failures propagate. No page box, content, annotation or extraction cursor is changed. See auto_crop() to apply a crop later.
attributes.signature: def get_content_bounds(self, *, dpi: float=72.0, white_threshold: int=250, include_annotations: bool=True) -> tuple[float, float, float, float] | None

attributes.docstring: A context manager holding a graphics state over what is drawn inside it.
attributes.docstring_full: A context manager holding a graphics state over what is drawn inside it. Everything appended to the page in the block is drawn under that state -- text and images included, which is how either of those is rotated, scaled or made transparent:: with page.graphics(transform=(0, 1, -1, 0, 500, 100)): page.add_text("sideways", 0, 0, font_size=18) with page.graphics(clip=GraphicsPath().circle(300, 400, 80)): page.add_image("photo.jpg", 220, 320, 160, 160) ``clip`` confines the block to the inside of a path (``W n``, ISO 32000-1 8.5.4), and the state is undone when the block ends, so the rest of the page is unaffected. The other arguments are :meth:`draw_path`'s.
attributes.signature: def graphics(self, *, transform: Any=None, clip: GraphicsPath | None=None, clip_even_odd: bool=False, opacity: float | None=None, fill_opacity: float | None=None, stroke_opacity: float | None=None, blend_mode: str | None=None) -> Any

attributes.docstring_full: Whether this page renders blank on white paper at the chosen DPI. A pixel is ink if any RGB channel is below ``white_threshold`` (1-255). The page is blank if the ink fraction is at most ``max_ink_ratio`` (0-1). Defaults tolerate near-white paper and no darker pixels. Increase the ratio explicitly to tolerate scan noise. Visible annotations count unless ``include_annotations=False``. CropBox, rotation and layer visibility follow :meth:`render`; antialiasing is disabled. This is a visual heuristic at a finite resolution, with the shared renderer's limitations. Hidden data can remain on a blank-looking page. Nothing is removed or modified; render errors and resource limits propagate. Higher DPI can reveal smaller marks at a higher cost.

attributes.docstring: Remove existing text from simple text-showing operands on this page.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove existing text from simple text-showing operands on this page. With ``overlay=True`` a filled rectangle (``overlay_color`` -- grey, RGB or CMYK, default black) is drawn over each removed run -- the classic redaction bar. The bar is cosmetic (the text is already removed); runs whose position cannot be tracked are left unmarked. Saving after a match requires a full rewrite and removes obsolete content storage. Incremental saves are refused and existing signatures are invalidated. Shared content still used by other pages is retained. See :meth:`aspose_pdf.document.Document.redact_text` for alternate-text handling, unsupported cases and output-stream requirements. With ``regex=True``, or a compiled :class:`re.Pattern` as *search*, a *shape* is redacted rather than a phrase -- an account number, a date, a card -- and the overlay bars come from the same spans the removal used.

attributes.docstring: Render this page to an RGB raster image.
attributes.docstring_full: Render this page to an RGB raster image. The renderer is dependency-free and supports common page content: paths, fills/strokes, image XObjects, form XObjects, and embedded-font text. The returned object can be encoded to PNG/TIFF/JPEG, or to WebP with the optional ``images`` extra, and saved directly. ``antialias`` smooths edges by supersampling (``True`` = 3x, an integer 1-8 sets the factor, ``False`` disables it for a hard-edged raster). ``clip=(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` selects an area in unrotated PDF coordinates with a lower-left origin. Ordered corners and a positive intersection with the effective CropBox are required. Only that intersection is rasterized, with page rotation applied and page boxes preserved. ``shape_substitute_text`` (default on) joins complex-script runs drawn with a bundled substitute face; it needs the optional ``text-layout`` extra and only affects non-embedded fonts. ``draw_annotations`` (default on) composites each visible annotation's normal appearance over the page, the way a viewer shows it. ``font_substitution`` overrides the document's :attr:`~aspose_pdf.Document.font_substitution` for this call, naming the font sources non-embedded fonts may be drawn with. ``performance`` is an optional :class:`~aspose_pdf.visualization.PerformanceLogger` the render records its per-phase timings into; without one nothing is measured.

For a single pattern, use positional arguments: ``replace_annotation_contents(search, replacement, ...)`` For multiple patterns, pass a mapping as the first argument: ``replace_annotation_contents({search: replacement, ...}, ...)`` In single-pattern mode, strings match literal substrings unless ``regex=True``; compiled text regexes retain their flags. ``case_sensitive=False`` adds IGNORECASE. All occurrences are replaced in each annotation. Regex replacement strings support Python backreferences; literal replacements stay literal. In multiple-pattern mode, a mapping of search patterns to replacement strings is provided. This is more efficient than calling this method multiple times for each pattern. Parameters ---------- search_or_replacements Either a single search pattern (string or compiled regex), or a mapping of search patterns to replacement strings. replacement Replacement text for a single search pattern. Required when ``search_or_replacements`` is a single pattern. case_sensitive If ``True`` (default), matching is case-sensitive. Ignored for compiled regex patterns that already have flags set. max_count Maximum replacements to perform. ``0`` (default) means unlimited for single-pattern mode, or shared across all patterns in multiple-pattern mode. regex If ``True``, string search patterns are treated as regular expressions. Not required for compiled :class:`re.Pattern` keys. dry_run If ``True``, perform all checks and count changes without modifying the document. Return the number of changes that would be made. Returns ------- int Total number of annotation contents modified. See Also -------- replace_text : Replace a single text pattern in page content. replace_texts : Replace multiple text patterns in page content. replace_link_urls : Replace a single link URL pattern. replace_link_urls_batch : Replace multiple link URL patterns. attributes.docstring: Give this page a new sheet size and scale its drawing onto it.
attributes.docstring_full: Give this page a new sheet size and scale its drawing onto it. Setting :attr:`size` changes the sheet and leaves the drawing where it was, so a smaller sheet crops it and a larger one pads it. This scales the drawing with the sheet, which is what resizing a page usually means: ``page.resize(PageSize.LETTER)`` on an A4 page gives a Letter page showing the same thing. ``mode`` says what to do when the two shapes differ: ``"fit"`` (the default) keeps the aspect ratio and leaves an even margin on the long side, ``"fill"`` keeps it and lets the drawing run past the short side, and ``"stretch"`` scales the axes apart so the drawing fills the sheet exactly. The drawing is **centred** either way, and the sheet keeps its own origin. The crop and production boxes travel with the drawing; the media box becomes the size asked for.

attributes.docstring_full: Scale everything this page draws, leaving the sheet the size it is. One factor scales both axes; two scale them apart. ``about="center"``, the default, keeps the drawing centred on the sheet -- so ``page.scale_content(0.95)`` adds an even margin all round, which is what a printer's non-printable edge wants -- while ``about="origin"`` scales from the sheet's own origin and leaves the drawing's lower-left corner where it was. The page's operators are not rewritten: the content is put inside one ``q`` ... ``Q`` with the matrix at the top. Annotations travel with it, since an appearance stream is fitted to its ``/Rect`` by the reader. To change the sheet *and* the drawing together, use :meth:`resize`; to change the sheet alone, set :attr:`size`. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If a factor is not a positive finite number, *about* is neither name, or the page's content restores a graphics state it never saved -- a page that cannot be wrapped without changing how it draws.

Accepts a :class:`PageSize`, the name of one, or a plain ``(width, height)`` pair in points:: page.size = PageSize.A4 page.size = PageSize.A4.landscape() page.size = "legal" page.size = (300, 400)

attributes.docstring_full: The page's explicit annotation tab order: row, column or structure. ``None`` means no supported setting is present. The PDF ``/Tabs`` entry is local to the page, not inherited. Unknown entries remain untouched. A compatible viewer applies the order to form widgets and annotations; structure order uses the document's existing structure tree.

attributes.docstring: Return this page's inferred structure as an HTML fragment document.
attributes.docstring_full: Return this page's inferred structure as an HTML fragment document. The conversion answers "what does this page *say*", not "what does it look like": the same layout analysis :meth:`Document.auto_tag` uses infers headings, paragraphs, lists, tables and figures, and the text is decoded exactly as :meth:`Document.extract_text` decodes it. Exact positioning, colour and fonts are deliberately dropped -- for a facsimile, use :meth:`to_svg`.

attributes.docstring: Return this page's inferred structure as Markdown (GFM).
attributes.docstring_full: Return this page's inferred structure as Markdown (GFM). See :meth:`to_html` for what the conversion does and does not carry.

attributes.docstring: Return this page as an SVG document.
attributes.docstring_full: Return this page as an SVG document. Paths, clips, text (as glyph outlines), images and axial/radial shadings are exported by the shared rendering interpreter. Blend modes and isolated groups use CSS compositing; soft masks embed alpha maps. Function and mesh shadings are sampled into images. Knockout groups, non-isolated groups with group-level alpha/blend/mask, tiling patterns, patterned strokes/text and overprint preview fall back to a complete embedded RGBA page at 72 dpi, preserving the renderer's limitations. Vector blending requires a viewer supporting CSS Compositing Level 1. ``background`` paints an opaque page behind the content; pass ``None`` for a transparent SVG. ``precision`` is the number of decimal places coordinates are written with, trading file size against exactness. ``text`` decides how the page's words are written out: ``"outlines"`` Each glyph as the curves its font gives it. Exact, and no more selectable than a photograph of the page. The default, and what this has always done. ``"text"`` ``<text>`` elements instead, which a reader can select, search and copy. Every glyph keeps the position the PDF gave it, so the layout does not move; the glyph *shapes* are whatever font the viewer resolves the name to, so they will not match exactly. ``"both"`` The outlines, with the ``<text>`` over them unfilled. The page looks exactly as ``"outlines"`` does and the words are still there to select. The largest of the three. Text a font gives no meaning to -- no ``/ToUnicode``, and an encoding that resolves nothing -- stays outlines whatever this says, because the alternative is putting a guess in someone's copy buffer. Invisible text (rendering mode 3) is collected too: a scanned page's OCR layer is made of nothing else, and this is what makes it searchable.

attributes.docstring: Remove and return a page from the collection.
attributes.docstring_full: Remove and return a page from the collection. This method removes a page from the collection and returns it as a :class:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page` object that can be inserted into another document or used elsewhere. Parameters ---------- index : int, optional The one-based page number to remove. Defaults to ``None``, which removes and returns the last page (following Python's list.pop() convention). Page numbers start at 1. Returns ------- Page The removed page, which can be inserted into another document using :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.PageCollection.insert` or :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.PageCollection.add`. Raises ------ IndexError If the collection is empty or if *index* is not a valid page number. TypeError If *index* is not an integer or ``None``. Examples -------- :: # Remove and get the last page last_page = document.pages.pop() # Remove and get a specific page (e.g., first page) first_page = document.pages.pop(1) # Insert the popped page into another document other_doc.pages.insert(1, popped_page) Notes ----- After removal, the page count decreases by one, and all page numbers after the removed page are shifted down by one. For example, if you pop page 2 from a 5-page document, the former page 3 becomes page 2, page 4 becomes page 3, and page 5 becomes page 4. The removed page retains all its properties: content, annotations, form fields, layer assignments, page labels, and bookmarks that point to it.

A document's label ranges, keyed by the index of the page each starts at.
attributes.docstring_full: A document's label ranges, keyed by the index of the page each starts at. Setting a range where none starts at the first page adds one there, since the tree has to begin at page 0 (ISO 32000-1 table 28): numbered 1, 2, 3, which is what readers show for pages no range covers. Deleting that first range while others remain puts the same one back. Deleting the last range, or :meth:`clear`, removes the labels altogether. Inserting or deleting pages moves the ranges after them, so a page added inside a range is numbered as part of it; pages merged in from another document keep the labels they had there.

attributes.docstring_full: Return all zero-based page indices whose label exactly equals *label*. Results follow page order and include duplicates across restarted or prefix-only ranges. Matching is case-sensitive and keeps whitespace and Unicode unchanged. Empty strings match empty labels. No match, an empty document or absent page labels returns ``[]``; viewer fallback page positions are not labels. An existing empty tree still supplies the default decimal labels, just as :meth:`label` does. Only current label metadata is inspected, including unsaved edits; page content is not decoded or rendered. Results are independent lists. Document page/tree limits, UTF-8 query size, comparison work and result counts obey :class:`~aspose_pdf.PdfLoadLimits`. Invalid Unicode queries and resource-limit failures raise without returning partial results.

A page of a document, drawn onto a page -- a letterhead, a background form.
attributes.docstring_full: A page of a document, drawn onto a page -- a letterhead, a background form. *source* is the page to place: an :class:`aspose_pdf.Page`, or a :class:`aspose_pdf.Document` with *page_index* saying which of its pages. The page is brought across as a form XObject with everything it draws with -- its fonts, its images, the forms nested inside it -- which is the same deep copy a merge makes, so the source document can be closed afterwards. What is placed is the page as a reader *shows* it: its crop box, with its ``/Rotate`` applied. All of :class:`Stamp`'s placement applies on top -- ``zoom`` to scale it, ``rotate`` to turn it, the alignments and indents to put it somewhere, ``opacity`` to see through it, and ``background=True`` to put it *under* the page's own content, which is what a letterhead wants:: letterhead = Document("letterhead.pdf") document.add_stamp(PageStamp(letterhead.pages[1], background=True)) A page of the document being stamped may be placed on another of its pages; placing a page on *itself* is refused, since the content being drawn would be the content being added to.

attributes.docstring: An immutable comparison of two selected pages, using one-based page numbers.
attributes.docstring_full: An immutable comparison of two selected pages, using one-based page numbers. ``text`` and ``other_text`` contain extracted strings after any exclusion filtering and before case or whitespace normalization. A missing page has a ``None`` index and text, distinct from a blank page's empty string. Missing pages never match, even when the other page is blank. ``matches`` compares text after the requested whitespace/case handling. ``unified_diff`` describes those same normalized strings with three lines of context, using one-based page numbers in its headers. It is empty for matches. A missing blank page produces headers alone. LF separates diff lines; missing final LF is marked explicitly. Reports remain usable after either document closes, without retaining document or page objects.
attributes.fields: page_index, other_page_index, text, other_text, matches, unified_diff

attributes.docstring: One pair of rendered pages, using one-based source page indices.
attributes.docstring_full: One pair of rendered pages, using one-based source page indices. A missing page has a ``None`` index and size. Sizes are ``(width, height)`` in pixels. ``changed_pixels`` counts pixels outside the color tolerance, including pixels covered by only one page, except ignored regions. ``total_pixels`` is the union of the two page rectangles, aligned at the top-left without scaling, minus ``ignored_pixels``. Overlapping exclusions count once and pixels outside both pages never count. An entirely ignored pair has zero total pixels and a zero difference ratio. ``bbox`` encloses changed pixels as ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)``, with a top-left origin and exclusive upper bounds; ``None`` means no changed pixels. ``matches`` requires both pages, equal raster sizes, and a difference ratio at most the configured allowance. Missing or differently sized pages never match, even with a ratio allowance of 1. ``diff_image`` is present only when requested. Changed pixels are red, unchanged pixels show a pale grayscale page context, and areas outside both pages are white. Ignored pixels are light blue (RGB 192, 224, 255). Save it with ``RasterizedPage.save()``. The report and image remain usable after either document is closed.
attributes.fields: page_index, other_page_index, size, other_size, changed_pixels, total_pixels, bbox, matches, diff_image, ignored_pixels

attributes.docstring: Return changed pixels divided by nonignored pixels on either page.
One paragraph: what it says, and how it differs from the block.
attributes.docstring_full: One paragraph: what it says, and how it differs from the block. Every style is ``None`` by default, which means *take the block's* -- so a block is styled once and a paragraph only says where it departs from it. ``space_before``/``space_after`` are added to the block's ``paragraph_gap`` rather than replacing it, since the gap is about the space *between* paragraphs and these are about this one. Page-breaking controls: - ``keep_together``: move the whole paragraph rather than split it when it fits. - ``widow_lines``: minimum lines before a page break within this paragraph. - ``orphan_lines``: minimum lines after a page break within this paragraph. - ``keep_with_next``: keep a paragraph with the start of the following one. Line counts default to ``None`` (unrestricted). Linked paragraph chains are kept whole when they fit a fresh page; long paragraphs can still split. Constraints that cannot fit a fresh page are relaxed to keep text within the page bounds. Spacing before a paragraph is not repeated on continuation pages.

attributes.docstring: Return one-based page numbers from page numbers, keywords and ranges.
attributes.docstring_full: Return one-based page numbers from page numbers, keywords and ranges. ``"1-3,7,10-"`` selects pages 1 through 3, page 7, and page 10 through the last page. Numbers in the expression are one-based by default; ``one_based=False`` interprets them as zero-based instead. The returned page numbers are always one-based, ready for ``Document.extract_pages`` and APIs accepting a ``pages`` argument. The same numbers can be passed to facades. Case-insensitive ``odd`` and ``even`` select physical pages 1, 3, 5, ... and 2, 4, 6, ... regardless of ``one_based`` or page labels. ``last`` selects the final page and can be either endpoint: ``"2-last"`` selects from page 2 onward; ``"last-1"`` selects every page in reverse order with the default numbering. Any range may descend, such as ``"4-2"``. Whitespace around items and hyphens is ignored. Input order and repeated pages are preserved, including overlaps between comma-separated items. Empty items, unsupported syntax and pages outside ``page_count`` raise ``PdfValidationException``. Numbers, ``last`` and open-ended ranges require an existing page. ``odd`` and ``even`` return an empty tuple when no pages match; document extraction and splitting still reject empty selections. Expression bytes and the total expanded selection obey ``limits``. Parsing reads no document content.

attributes.docstring: Paths to draw on a page: lines, curves and the shapes built from them.
attributes.docstring_full: Paths to draw on a page: lines, curves and the shapes built from them. A :class:`GraphicsPath` collects the subpaths of ISO 32000-1 8.5.2 -- moves, lines, cubic Bézier curves, rectangles -- and :meth:`aspose_pdf.pages.Page.draw_path` paints it. Building is fluent, so a shape reads as one statement:: from aspose_pdf import GraphicsPath arrow = ( GraphicsPath() .move_to(100, 100) .line_to(200, 160) .curve_to(230, 170, 250, 150, 260, 120) .close() ) page.draw_path(arrow, fill_color="#336699", stroke_color=None) Coordinates are PDF points in the page's own space, y upward from the bottom left -- the same space :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page.add_text` and :meth:`~aspose_pdf.pages.Page.draw_rectangle` place things in.

PDF/X validation options, results, and the standards this library knows.
attributes.docstring_full: PDF/X validation options, results, and the standards this library knows. PDF/X (ISO 15930) is the print-exchange branch of the PDF standards: where PDF/A is about a file still being readable in fifty years and PDF/UA about it being usable by everyone, PDF/X is about a file printing the same way wherever it is sent. A conforming file carries everything the press needs -- every font embedded, one output intent naming the printing condition the colour was prepared for, a stated trim size, a stated trapping status -- and nothing whose result would depend on the reader. Results are **heuristic**, as for PDF/A and PDF/UA, and with one difference worth stating plainly: veraPDF validates PDF/A and PDF/UA but **not** PDF/X, and no other free validator does either, so these checks have not been cross-checked against a reference implementation the way the PDF/A ones have. Treat them as signals, and preflight with a prepress tool before committing a job to print.

Accepts the canonical names (``"PDF/X-4"``), the same without the ``PDF/`` prefix, and spellings without punctuation or case (``"x-1a"``, ``"X1a"``, ``"pdf/x-3:2002"``). A part named without a year resolves to its newest edition. An unknown name raises rather than falling back to a standard the caller did not ask for -- which would write a file claiming conformance to something nobody chose.

attributes.docstring: What a reader may do with an encrypted document: ``/P``, with names.
attributes.docstring_full: What a reader may do with an encrypted document: ``/P``, with names. An ``int`` subclass, so it goes anywhere the raw value went and compares equal to it. Build one with :meth:`all`, :meth:`none`, :meth:`allowing` or :meth:`denying`, adjust it with :meth:`with_` and :meth:`without`, and ask it what it allows with the ``can_*`` properties or :meth:`allows`. The eight class constants are Table 22's bit **values**, so ``Permissions.PRINT == 4``. They are inputs to the constructors above rather than values to OR together by hand -- ORing two of them loses the reserved bits, which is the mistake this class exists to make impossible. Two bits are not independent of each other. ``print_high_resolution`` (bit 12) qualifies ``print`` (bit 3): granted alone it grants no printing, which is how qpdf reads it, so a document meant to be printed properly allows **both**. ``Permissions.denying("print")`` likewise leaves bit 12 set and still forbids printing, which is what the bits mean. Revision matters for what a reader honours: under the old ``/R 2`` only bits 3 to 6 are defined, so denying only ``assemble`` or ``accessibility`` has no effect in a document encrypted that way. This library writes ``/R 4`` or ``/R 6`` unless RC4 is asked for.
attributes.members: PRINT, MODIFY, COPY, ANNOTATE, FILL_FORMS, ACCESSIBILITY, ASSEMBLE, PRINT_HIGH_RESOLUTION, GRANTS

attributes.docstring: Access permissions: the ``/P`` word, as flags with names.
attributes.docstring_full: Access permissions: the ``/P`` word, as flags with names. ``/P`` is a *signed 32-bit integer* whose bits say what a reader may do with an encrypted document, and whose unused bits are all **1** -- so "everything allowed" is ``-4`` and "nothing allowed" is ``-3904``, numbers nobody reads off a page. Worse, combining permissions by hand goes wrong quietly: ``Permissions.PRINT | Permissions.COPY`` as plain integers is ``20``, a ``/P`` with every reserved bit *cleared*, which ISO 32000-1 Table 22 does not allow and some readers take as "nothing is allowed". :class:`Permissions` is that integer with the names attached. It **is** an ``int`` -- ``document.permissions`` still compares, masks and passes anywhere a number did -- and it carries the reserved bits for you:: from aspose_pdf import Document, Permissions with Document("report.pdf") as document: document.encrypt( "", # no password to open "owner-secret", permissions=Permissions.all().without("copy", "modify"), ) document.save("report-protected.pdf") with Document("report-protected.pdf", password="owner-secret") as document: print(document.permissions) # Permissions(print, annotate, ...) print(document.permissions.can_copy) # False print(document.permissions.can_print) # True Granting nothing is not the same as leaving a document unencrypted: an unencrypted document has no ``/P`` at all, and :attr:`Document.permissions` reports :meth:`Permissions.all` for it, because nothing is being withheld.

attributes.docstring_full: One certificate that may open the document, and what it may then do. Parameters ---------- certificate: The recipient's ``cryptography`` :class:`~cryptography.x509.Certificate`. It must carry an RSA or EC public key. When it declares a ``keyUsage`` extension, RSA certificates must permit ``keyEncipherment`` or ``dataEncipherment`` and EC certificates must permit ``keyAgreement``. permissions: This recipient's access flags, defaulting to every permission. A signed 32-bit integer, or a :class:`~aspose_pdf.permissions.Permissions` built by name -- the eight permissions it knows sit at the same bit positions in this word as in the standard handler's ``/P`` (bit 3 print, 4 modify, 5 copy, 6 annotate, 9 fill forms, 10 accessible extraction, 11 assemble, 12 high-quality print). The differences are in the bits noted above, and they are normalised for you, so ``Permissions.denying("copy")`` says here what it says there.

attributes.docstring: Return ``(certificate, permissions)`` for the engine.
Recipients of a public-key (``/Adobe.PubSec``) encrypted document.
attributes.docstring_full: Recipients of a public-key (``/Adobe.PubSec``) encrypted document. The standard security handler gates a document behind a password everyone with access has to know and share. The public-key handler gates it behind *certificates*: the producer names the recipients, and each one opens the file with the private key they already hold. Nothing is shared, nothing is typed, and revoking access to future documents means dropping a certificate from the list. Each recipient also gets its **own** permissions -- one reader may print and another only read the same file -- which no password-based scheme can express:: from cryptography import x509 from aspose_pdf import Document, Permissions, Recipient auditor = x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(Path("auditor.pem").read_bytes()) reviewer = x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(Path("reviewer.pem").read_bytes()) with Document("report.pdf") as document: document.encrypt_for_recipients( [ Recipient(auditor), # everything Recipient( reviewer, permissions=Permissions.allowing("print", "copy"), ), ] ) document.save("report-sealed.pdf") Opening one needs the certificate *and* its private key:: with Document("report-sealed.pdf", certificate=cert, private_key=key) as doc: print(doc.pages[1].content)

attributes.docstring: PdfSignature implementation.
attributes.docstring_full: PdfSignature implementation. This module provides the :class:`PdfSignature` dataclass which represents a PDF digital signature and verifies it against the bytes its ``ByteRange`` covers. The :attr:`PdfSignature.valid` property checks: 1. The ``ByteRange`` array has exactly four integers. 2. The ranges describe two non-overlapping slices that together cover the signed revision (from byte 0 through ``start2 + len2``) except for the signature placeholder. Trailing bytes (e.g. further incremental updates after signing) are ignored for hashing; ``reference_data`` may be longer than that revision. 3. The signer verifies cryptographically over those bytes: the digest algorithm comes from the CMS itself, the ``messageDigest`` signed attribute must match the covered bytes, and the signature value must verify against the signer certificate's public key. If any of these checks fail — or the signature cannot be verified at all — ``valid`` returns ``False``. It answers integrity and signer authenticity only; it does **not** build or check the certificate chain, revocation, or timestamps. For that, and for a structured result, use :meth:`PdfSignature.validate` with a :class:`~aspose_pdf.validation.ValidationOptions` instance.

attributes.docstring: What a visible digital signature looks like on the page.
attributes.docstring_full: What a visible digital signature looks like on the page. A signature field may be *invisible* -- a zero-size widget, covering the whole document and showing nothing -- or **visible**, drawn on a page as a box saying who signed, when, and why. ISO 32000-1 12.7.4.5 puts nothing in the signature dictionary about this: the appearance is an ordinary annotation appearance stream (``/AP /N``), and what goes in it is entirely the producer's business. Which is why it has to be said somewhere, and :class:`SignatureAppearance` is where. It carries no PDF structure of its own. It is a description handed to :meth:`aspose_pdf.Document.sign`, which draws it into the signed revision when the document is saved -- so the appearance is covered by the signature that made it, and cannot be swapped for another without breaking it.

attributes.docstring: How a visible signature is drawn: its text, its image, and its frame.
attributes.docstring_full: How a visible signature is drawn: its text, its image, and its frame. Pass one to :meth:`aspose_pdf.Document.sign`:: document.sign( "Signature1", certificate=cert, private_key=key, reason="I approve this document", location="Prague", appearance=SignatureAppearance(image=logo_png), ) By default it writes four lines -- who signed, when, why, and where -- each labelled, taking the name from ``signer_name`` or, failing that, the common name in the signing certificate. Turn a line off with its ``show_*`` argument, or replace the lot with *text* of your own. Parameters ---------- image : bytes, str or Path, optional A scanned signature, a seal or a logo, as image bytes or a path. PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP and TIFF are read; it is scaled to fit its share of the box, keeping its aspect ratio. image_position : str ``"left"`` (the default), ``"right"``, ``"top"``, ``"background"`` -- the image fills the box with the text over it -- or ``"only"``, which draws no text at all. image_fraction : float How much of the box the image gets when it sits beside or above the text, between 0.1 and 0.9. Default 0.4. text : str, optional The whole text, replacing the composed lines. Newlines break lines; a line too long for the box is wrapped. show_name, show_date, show_reason, show_location, show_contact : bool Which composed lines to include. A line whose value is empty is left out whatever this says -- a signature with no reason given shows no empty ``Reason:``. labels : bool Prefix each composed line with what it is (``Date:``, ``Reason:``). The name line reads ``Digitally signed by ...``. With ``False`` the values are drawn on their own. date_format : str :meth:`~datetime.datetime.strftime` format for the date line. font : bytes, str, Path or FontDescriptor, optional A font program to draw the text with, embedded in the document. Needed for text outside Latin-1 -- a Cyrillic or CJK name has no code in the standard fonts' encodings, and signing refuses rather than drawing the wrong letters. Without one the text is drawn in Helvetica. font_size : float Point size, or ``0`` (the default) to fit the text to the box. text_color : optional Any colour this library accepts; black by default. background : optional Fill colour for the box. ``None`` leaves it unpainted, so whatever the page already draws there shows through. border_color : optional Colour of a frame around the box. ``None`` draws no frame. border_width : float Frame line width in points. Default 1. page : int, optional Zero-based page for the field :meth:`~aspose_pdf.Document.sign` adds when it is given no field name. Ignored when signing a field that exists -- that field's widget says where it is. rect : sequence of four floats, optional ``(llx, lly, urx, ury)`` for that same added field. Signing with an appearance and neither a field nor a rectangle is refused: there would be nowhere to draw it. Raises ------ PdfValidationException If an argument is out of range or the two placement arguments disagree.

attributes.docstring_full: Options for :class:`Splitter`. By default every page of every input becomes a document of its own. *selections* splits into groups instead: each entry is what :meth:`~aspose_pdf.Document.extract_pages` takes -- an iterable of one-based page numbers or a one-based range string such as ``"1-3,7-"`` -- and becomes one output document, in the order given:: SplitOptions(selections=[range(1, 4), [4, 5], "6-"]) A page may appear in more than one selection, or in none. Range strings also accept ``odd``, ``even``, ``last`` and descending ranges such as ``"last-1"``; keywords and open ends resolve separately per input. ``bookmark_level=1`` instead splits at root bookmarks; higher levels select nested headings. It follows :meth:`Document.split_by_bookmarks`, including a leading ``Preamble`` result unless ``include_preamble=False``. This mode cannot be combined with ``selections`` or ``pages_per_part``. ``pages_per_part=N`` instead groups consecutive pages in parts of at most N pages, retaining a shorter last part. It follows :meth:`Document.split_every` for each input independently and cannot be combined with either other mode.

Stamps: a mark put over or under what a page already draws.
attributes.docstring_full: Stamps: a mark put over or under what a page already draws. A stamp is placed, not authored at a coordinate: say which corner it belongs in and how far off it, and it lands there on any page size:: document.pages[1].add_stamp(TextStamp("DRAFT", font_size=64, rotate=45, opacity=0.2, background=True)) document.add_stamp(PageNumberStamp("{page} of {total}", font_size=9, vertical_alignment=VerticalAlignment.BOTTOM, y_indent=24)) document.pages[1].add_stamp(ImageStamp(logo_png, width=80, height=40, horizontal_alignment=HorizontalAlignment.RIGHT, vertical_alignment=VerticalAlignment.TOP, x_indent=-24, y_indent=-24)) A stamp is positioned inside the part of the page a reader shows -- the crop box -- and the page's rotation is undone, so it stands upright on screen whatever ``/Rotate`` says. ``background`` puts it under the page's own content instead of over it. One stamp added to many pages is one object in the file.

attributes.docstring_full: A table of rows, ready to be placed on a page. ``column_widths`` are in points and decide the table's width. Without them, ``columns`` (or the widest row) splits ``width`` -- or the room left on the page -- into equal columns. Set ``auto_column_widths=True`` to distribute that space by measured content instead. Fonts, sizes, padding, headers and column spans are considered. Explicit ``column_widths`` take precedence. The styles here are the defaults every row and cell falls back to: ``font_name`` and ``font_size`` for the text, ``font`` to embed a Unicode font instead, ``padding`` inside each cell, ``border_width`` and ``border_color`` for the lines, ``background_color`` behind the cells, and ``header_background_color``/``header_text_color``/``header_font_size`` for the rows marked as headers. ``repeat_header`` repeats those rows at the top of every page the table continues onto. ``border_widths`` and ``border_colors`` are partial mappings keyed by ``top``, ``right``, ``bottom`` and ``left``. At each level (table, row, cell), uniform border styles override inherited defaults, then per-side entries override the uniform styles. Width zero or a side colour of ``None`` hides that side. Width and colour inherit independently.

Tables: rows, cells, and the measurements that put them on a page.
attributes.docstring_full: Tables: rows, cells, and the measurements that put them on a page. A table is built and then placed, which is what a package with no flow layout can honestly offer:: from aspose_pdf import Document, PageSize, Table table = Table(column_widths=[220, 70, 90], border_width=0.75) table.add_row(["Item", "Qty", "Price"], header=True) table.add_row(["Widget, the larger kind", "2", "9.99"]) table.add_row(["Grommet", "14", "0.40"]) with Document() as document: page = document.pages.add(PageSize.A4) page.add_table(table, 60, 760) document.save("invoice.pdf") Cell text is wrapped to the column's width with the font's own advances, rows grow to hold what they are given, and a table taller than the page continues onto the next one -- repeating the header rows, which is the reason a header is marked as one. Everything is measured in PDF points, with ``y`` counting up from the bottom of the page as it does everywhere else in the package.

attributes.docstring: Text extraction utilities.
attributes.docstring_full: Text extraction utilities. This module provides TextFragmentAbsorber, TextFragmentCollection and related classes for searching and managing text fragments in PDF documents. Font classes for searching and managing text fragments in PDF documents. PictureClausesFormatter for number formatting is also included. Paragraph alignment functionality is also included. Supports three search modes: - No phrase/regex: collect all text fragments line by line. - phrase search: find all occurrences of an exact substring (optionally case-insensitive via TextSearchOptions.case_sensitive=False). - regex search: find all regex matches; results available via both text_fragments and regex_results (set is_regular_expression=True on the TextSearchOptions passed to the constructor or assigned before a visit).

attributes.docstring_full: Absorbs text fragments from a PDF page or document. Usage ----- *Collect all text (no filter):* .. code-block:: python absorber = TextFragmentAbsorber() absorber.visit(page) for frag in absorber.text_fragments: print(frag.text) *Phrase search:* .. code-block:: python absorber = TextFragmentAbsorber("Hello") absorber.visit(page) *Case-insensitive phrase search:* .. code-block:: python opts = TextSearchOptions(case_sensitive=False) absorber = TextFragmentAbsorber("hello", text_search_options=opts) *Regex search:* .. code-block:: python opts = TextSearchOptions(is_regular_expression=True) absorber = TextFragmentAbsorber(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", text_search_options=opts) absorber.visit(page) for result in absorber.regex_results: print(result.text, result.start) Parameters ---------- phrase : str, optional Text phrase to search for. attributes.docstring: Flowing text: paragraphs wrapped to a width, and placed on a page.
attributes.docstring_full: Flowing text: paragraphs wrapped to a width, and placed on a page. Until now authored text was placed one string at a time at one point, and wrapping it meant measuring the font yourself -- or passing ``layout=TextLayoutOptions(...)`` to :meth:`Page.add_text`, which shapes with HarfBuzz and so needs both an embedded font and the optional ``text-layout`` extra. A text block is the plain case: wrap to a measure, align the lines, and carry on to the next page when the room runs out, with nothing to install:: from aspose_pdf import Document, PageSize, TextBlock block = TextBlock(width=440, font_size=11, alignment="justify") block.add_paragraph("Of Man's first disobedience, and the fruit", tag="H1", font_size=18, alignment="center", space_after=12) block.add_paragraph(long_text, first_line_indent=18) with Document() as document: page = document.pages.add(PageSize.A4) end = page.add_text_block(block, 72, 740) document.save("essay.pdf") ``x``/``y`` are the top-left corner of the first line's measure, with ``y`` counting up from the bottom of the page as everywhere else in the package, and everything is in points. The return value says where the text ended, so the next thing on the page knows where to go. A plain string is one paragraph, and a **blank line starts a new one** -- the convention of every plain-text format there is. A single newline stays a hard break inside the paragraph it is in.

attributes.docstring_full: PAdES baseline conformance level reached by a signature. Mirrors the ETSI EN 319 142 baseline levels (named *B-B*, *B-T*, *B-LT*, *B-LTA* in the standard). Each level builds on the previous one: * :attr:`B` - CAdES-BES baseline: the signed attributes carry an ESS ``signing-certificate-v2`` binding and the ``ETSI.CAdES.detached`` ``/SubFilter``. * :attr:`T` - B plus a trusted RFC 3161 signature timestamp or a verified document timestamp covering the signature's complete revision. * :attr:`LT` - T plus embedded material sufficient to validate the signer and TSA paths and their revocation status offline. * :attr:`LTA` - LT plus a trusted document timestamp (``ETSI.RFC3161``) covering that validation material. Mere dictionary presence is not proof. This reports the profile established by the implemented checks, not formal ETSI conformance certification. Always inspect ``ValidationResult.status`` as well: a valid baseline binding can accompany a failed timestamp check.

Configuration for signature validation.
attributes.docstring_full: Configuration for signature validation. Pass an instance of this class to :meth:`~aspose_pdf.signature.PdfSignature.validate` to customise the validation behaviour. Attributes ---------- validation_mode: Determines whether certificate revocation is checked over the network. Defaults to :attr:`ValidationMode.OFFLINE`. validation_method: Selects the signature format to validate. Defaults to :attr:`ValidationMethod.PKCS7`. trusted_certificates: Trust anchors used for chain validation. Each item may be a :class:`cryptography.x509.Certificate` or PEM/DER ``bytes``. When empty, only ``allow_self_signed`` / ``use_system_trust`` apply. allow_self_signed: When ``True`` (default) a cryptographically intact self-signed signature is still reported ``VALID`` (flagged ``SELF_SIGNED``). This does not override explicit/system trust anchors or establish trust in a timestamp authority. check_revocation: When ``True`` perform OCSP/CRL revocation checking. Offline this uses only revocation material embedded in the document; combined with :attr:`ValidationMode.ONLINE`/``AUTO`` it may fetch over the network. Every non-root certificate in the signer and TSA paths is checked; inconclusive evidence yields ``UNKNOWN``, not ``VALID``. check_timestamp: When ``True`` (default) verify an embedded RFC 3161 signature timestamp if present. The TSA must chain to an explicit/system anchor, have a critical timeStamping-only EKU and be valid at the token's time. An untrusted timestamp yields ``INVALID``. Disabling this option never uses a claimed CMS signing time to validate an expired certificate. use_system_trust: When ``True`` also consult the operating-system CA bundle as trust anchors (best effort, via the standard library). network_timeout: Socket timeout (seconds) for any opt-in online OCSP/CRL/TSA request.

attributes.docstring_full: Where a render spent its time. :class:`PerformanceLogger` is caller-owned: hand one to :meth:`aspose_pdf.pages.Page.render` and the rasterizer records how long each phase took into it. Nothing is measured unless a logger is passed, so a render that does not ask for timings pays nothing for them, and two renders in different threads keep their own numbers. :class:`VirtualizationPerformance` is the older, process-global stopwatch of the same API. It works, and callers may use it for their own timings, but the package never writes to it: a library that timed itself into module-level mutable state would interleave two documents rendered at once. It does not virtualise or accelerate anything -- the name is inherited, not a description.

attributes.docstring: Convert an ISO-8601 date/time to a PDF date (``D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSS+HH'mm'``).
attributes.docstring_full: Convert an ISO-8601 date/time to a PDF date (``D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSS+HH'mm'``). Returns ``""`` when *value* is not an ISO-8601 date -- a string that only begins with one included, so ``"2026-09-10 (approx)"`` is refused rather than silently shortened. Precision is preserved in this direction too: ``"2026"`` is ``D:2026``, not ``D:20260101``.

attributes.docstring: Convert a PDF date (``D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSS+HH'mm'``) to an ISO-8601 string.
attributes.docstring_full: Convert a PDF date (``D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSS+HH'mm'``) to an ISO-8601 string. Returns ``""`` when *value* is not a PDF date -- including a string that merely *starts* like one, such as an ISO date that found its way into ``/Info``: ``"2026-09-10"`` is refused rather than read as the year 2026 and rendered ``"2026-01-01"``. Precision is preserved, because both formats truncate from the right and XMP has the shorter forms to say it with: ``D:2026`` is ``"2026"``, not ``"2026-01-01"``. The one component this cannot preserve is a lone hour -- the shortest XMP time is ``hh:mm`` -- so ``D:2026091008`` gains ``:00``.
